description: A running call No. 5 for bilateral cooperation project proposals

beneficiaryAdministration:
The objective of the call is to establish, develop, and/or improve cooperation between Lithuanian NGOs and advocacy-focused civil society organisations in other EU member states, strengthen organisational capacities, and promote collaboration in the field of advocacy, while upholding EU values. Expected impact includes new and strengthened cross-border partnerships, enhanced advocacy skills, increased mutual learning, and improved public understanding of EU values, including equality and the rights of persons belonging to minorities.

Applications can e submitted in a single-stage procedure at any time starting on the date of call publication until January 31, 2027. All proposals first undergo administrative eligibility checks carried out by the Open Lithuania Foundation (OLF). Eligible applications are then assessed by two independent experts according to predefined quality criteria; if their scores differ by more than 30 points, a third expert is appointed. Following expert assessments, the two closest-scoring experts agree on a consolidated evaluation. The Selection Committee reviews the expert conclusions, may propose budgets adjustments, and approves the list of projects recommended for funding. Applications that fail to reach the minimum required scores or are not in compliance with EU values are excluded from further consideration.

A total of 20 projects will be awarded grants of up to EUR 5,000 each within the maximum threshold allowed for financial support to third parties. Projects may last up to 6 months and will receive lump-sum funding paid in two instalments: 80% upon signing the grant agreement and 20% after the approval of final project reports.

Eligibility requirements for applicants:

  1. The applicant is a legal entity registered in the Republic of Lithuania for at least one year prior to the announcement of the rolling call, i.e., no later than 16 December 2024.
  2. The applicant carries out activities in Lithuania.
  3. The applicant is an NGO established and operating in the Republic of Lithuania that meets the following definition “A non-profit voluntary organisation established as a legal entity, having a non-commercial purpose, independent of local, regional, and central government, public entities, political parties, and commercial organisations.” Religious institutions, trade unions, and political parties are not considered NGOs (definition in line with Article 2.3 of the Law on the Development of Non-Governmental Organizations).
  4. The applicant’s activities do not conflict with EU values and actively contribute (or seek to contribute) to the promotion of EU values.
  5. The applicant has submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports to the National Center of Registers for the last two years (2023 and 2024), or financial and annual activity reports from the start of its activities if it has been operating for less than three years. Applicants applying after 1 June 2026 must have submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports for 2024 and 2025.
  6. The Open Lithuania Foundation is not a shareholder of the applicant.
  7. NGOs already participating in the VERTA! Programme (Phase II, 2025–2027) are eligible only if the total cumulative budget of all their applications under the programme, including the amount requested in this call, does not exceed EUR 60,000.
  8. The applicant has not implemented any other bilateral cooperation project under the VERTA! Programme financed from the funds of this call.

Eligibility requirements for partners:

  1. The partner must be a non-governmental organization established and operating as a legal entity in one of the European Union Member States, excluding Lithuania;
  2. The partner conducts advocacy activities in the field of EU values and has at least two years of advocacy experience;
  3. Prior to submitting the application, the applicant and the partner have concluded and signed a letter of intent to cooperate or another type of partnership agreement defining the division of responsibilities.

Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure and the full eligibility criteria can be found here (in Lithuanian): Kvietimas dvišalio bendradarbiavimo projektams finansuoti - ALF

description: About Phortify Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications. About the Phortify Funding Framework Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants

Under this call, Phortify internships refer to short-term, practice-oriented placements, as foreseen in the Phortify Grant Agreement. They are learning-based activities and do not constitute employment.

The Phortify Internship Grants support both students enrolled in Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes and students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s programme, provided that the internship is Phortify-labelled, aligned with the objectives of the Phortify project, and carried out in accordance with the Phortify Grant Agreement.

Participating partners:

Activer Fiber Systems (AFS):

- https://www.afs-jena.de/

ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences:

- https://www.icfo.eu/

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e):

- Master of Science in Applied Physics

- Master of Science in Electrical Engineering: track (1) Semicon Devices and track (2) Connected World Technologies

Warsaw University of Technology (WUT):

- Master of Science in Mechatronics

- Master of Science In Photonics

Friedrich Schiller University (FSU):

- Master of Science in Photonics

- Master of Science in Quantum Science & Technology


How to apply for funding

Funding opportunities will be advertised through (1) the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, (2) the official Phortify website (https://phortify.eu/my-phortify/) and (3) the official Phortify partner websites.

Applications for Phortify funding must be submitted via the Phortify website. Applicants are required to consult the dedicated MyPhortify page, where all funding opportunities available under this pilot call are listed together with detailed application instructions and links to the relevant local application forms.

Nationality eligibility

  1. Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, an associated country, or a country with which the European Union has an ongoing cooperation agreement under the Digital Europe Programme.
  2. Eligible countries include, inter alia, countries participating in Digital Partnerships, Trade and Technology Councils, digital dialogues, or other forms of ongoing international cooperation with the European Commission in the field of digital technologies.

The authoritative list of eligible countries will be published as part of this call and may be updated in accordance with European Commission guidance.

Eligibility

Under this call, Phortify Internship Grants may be awarded to students belonging to one of the following categories:

Category A – Phortify master degree-seeking students

Students who are enrolled in one of the Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes offered by the consortium universities and who undertake a Phortify-related internship during their period of study.

Category B – Phortify non-degree seeking students participating in Phortify student activities

Students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s Degree Programme but who participate in a Phortify-labelled internship, as foreseen under the Phortify Grant Agreement and implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

In all cases, eligible applicants must be students at the time of the internship, and the internship must:

  1. be directly related to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project;
  2. contribute to the academic and professional development of the student;
  3. be carried out during the student’s period of study;
  4. be implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

Applicants must submit the following documentation:

  1. Latest official academic BSc and MSc (if applicable) transcripts
  2. A Phortify-specific motivation letter, describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for Phortify funding and their alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project
  3. A curriculum vitae (CV)

Applications that fail to meet the minimum eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation will be declared ineligible and will not be further evaluated.

Evaluation and selection

The predefined evaluation framework applicable to this call is published on the Phortify website as a dedicated evaluation framework document and applies to all partner institutions.

1. Purpose and Scope

This description defines the evaluation framework applied to applications submitted under the Phortify Internship Grants – Pilot Call.

The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.

2. Evaluation Principles

The evaluation process is based on the following principles:

  1. Transparency and traceability of decisions
  2. Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
  3. Merit-based selection
  4. Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance

3. Evaluation Process Overview

The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:

  1. Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
  2. Comparative assessment and ranking

4.  Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification

Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).

Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.

5.   Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment

Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.

Evaluation Criteria

  1. Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed internship.
  2. Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
  3. Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.

Maximum total score: 15 points.

Ranking and Allocation of Funding

Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months, or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.

Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription, priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.

Selection Committees

Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by the Phortify partner institutions. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.

Documentation and transparency

Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.

Available funding under this call

Type and duration of financial support

Financial support under this call is provided either as a monthly allowance or as a lump sum, depending on the Phortify partner institution.

Monthly allowances are paid for the actual duration of the internship, subject to partner-specific conditions. Lump-sum grants are not linked to a fixed duration and are intended to contribute to the overall costs associated with the internship, such as travel, accommodation, and subsistence.

AFS:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.200/month for master students

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 800/month for bachelor students

ICFO:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 600/month for a maximum duration of 6 months

TU/e:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

WUT:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

FSU:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.500 - lump sum not linked to duration


Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.

description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

description: Under the PowerBoost stream, the only eligible activity is the implementation of an innovation audit, that will be reimbursed with a total of EUR 2000 once the audit is approved, aimed at identifying challenges and opportunities for the Applicant organisation to contribute to grid flexibility, sustainability, and digitalisation in the energy sector. beneficiaryAdministration:
PowerBoost is a targeted support stream designed to help SMEs assess their innovation readiness and strategic potential in the context of the energy transition. Under this stream, beneficiaries receive a lump-sum grant of EUR 2 000 to carry out an innovation audit focused on identifying key challenges and opportunities related to energy use. The audit supports SMEs in gaining a structured understanding of their current processes, technologies, and operational gaps, and in defining priority areas where innovation or the adoption of new technologies could enhance efficiency, flexibility, or integration with renewable energy systems.

Submit the application via the EU Survey Platform, the link to which is available at https://greengridcluster.eu. Applicants are required to upload a template-based Declaration of Honour, duly signed using a qualified electronic signature.

The evaluation and selection process of the PowerBoost open call ensures fairness, transparency, and equal treatment of all applicants. Each submitted application will undergo several verification and evaluation steps before final selection.

Step 1. Administrative and Eligibility Check

After the submission deadline (cut-off date), the GreenGrid Call Manager will verify that:

·       The application was submitted via the official online form within the deadline;

·       All required fields are completed and annexes attached;

·       The applicant meets the SME definition of the European Commission;

·       The applicant’s legal entity is established at least 1 year prior to the submission date.

·       The Declaration of Honour is duly signed with a qualified electronic signature valid as per DSS Demonstration WebApp.

Applications that are incomplete, submitted after PowerBoost Open Call closure, or do not meet eligibility requirements will be considered ineligible and will not proceed to evaluation.

Step 2. Evaluation by Independent Experts

It shall be defined if each eligible application will be assessed by 2 independent evaluators with relevant expertise. Each evaluator signs a declaration on confidentiality and conflict of interest. The evaluation will follow the criteria and scoring system described in Chapter 7 (Evaluation Criteria) of Open Call documentation.

·       Each criterion is scored from 1 to 5 points.

·       The maximum total score is 15 points.

·       The minimum threshold for funding is 12 points.

No additional information submitted after the deadline or provided through external links will be considered.

Step 3. Ranking and Selection

All applications that reach or exceed the threshold of 12 points will be ranked according to:

1.     The final score awarded by the evaluator and confirmed at the Consensus Meeting;

2.     Date and time of submission.

Funding will be allocated sequentially until the available PowerBoost budget is exhausted.

Step 4. Approval and Contracting

Applicants selected for funding will receive a notification email and a Sub-Grant Agreement template for electronic signature. The grant will be paid as a reimbursement after submission and approval of the final Challenge Description Report prepared as a result of the innovation audit. The report submission date will be mutually agreed between the Coordinator and the Beneficiary, but it cannot be later than 31 October 2027.

Step 5. Feedback to Unsuccessful Applicants

All applicants will receive an Evaluation Summary Report with their score and short feedback from the evaluator. Applicants who believe a procedural error has occurred may submit an appeal as described in Chapter 9 (Appealing Procedure) of the Open Call documentation.

Step 6. The Right to Withdraw

At any stage of the process before signing the Sub-Grant Agreement, the Applicant has the right to withdraw its application. The withdrawal may be made either before or after the evaluation has taken place. To do so, the Applicant must send a written notification by email. The titled subject line should clearly state: “Withdrawal – PowerBoost Open Call” to the GreenGrid Call Manager at the address indicated in the Call Guidelines.

Upon receipt of such notification, the application will be considered withdrawn and will not be subject to further evaluation, ranking, or contracting. Any withdrawal submitted after funding approval will automatically terminate the contracting process without further obligations for either party.

description: InnoEnergy Masters+ Scholarship — MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI (AI4GreenDeal)

beneficiaryAdministration:
The AI4GreenDeal project delivers a 120-ECTS Master’s double-degree programme combining energy-domain knowledge with data and AI skills and with innovation and entrepreneurship training, complemented by flexible, stackable self-standing modules. Through this call, the consortium offers to students (Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP)) in the form of full or partial scholarships to attract highly qualified candidates and to widen access to the programme, in line with the project’s target of at least 30% participation from women and/or individuals from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

Two scholarship schemes are offered under this call:

  1. Energy Impact Scholarships — awarded to applicants who demonstrate strong academic preparation and potential to contribute to the energy transition.
  2. Diversity, Entrepreneurship and Digital Champions (DED) Scholarships — awarded across three strands (DEI; Entrepreneurship; Digital Champions) to promote diversity and recognise entrepreneurial or digital-innovation excellence.

Applications are submitted through the InnoEnergy Masters+ online application tool within the published application window: 

https://apply.innoenergy.com/courses/course/55-masters-advanced-energy-systems-and-ai.

The MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI operates a rolling intake with five application rounds between 21 September 2026 and 30 May 2027; scholarship decisions are taken after each round within the overall framework and budget communicated for the intake.

No separate scholarship application is required: every applicant admitted to the programme is automatically considered for an Energy Impact Scholarship and admitted applicants who submit a 1–2 minute motivation video and pay the registration fee may in addition be considered for a DED Scholarship.

Each application is assessed in three stages. The Admissions Office first verifies document validity, general admissibility, recipient eligibility, and exclusion criteria. The Programme Steering Committee — composed of academic representatives of the partner universities acting as independent experts — then confirms programme-specific eligibility, evaluates, and ranks eligible applicants against the published award criteria.( https://ai4greendeal.com/content/uploads/2026/09/AI4GreenDeal_Indicative_Evaluation_Rubrics_070926.pdf ) The programme-independent DED Selection Committee additionally evaluates DED applicants.

Before scoring, every evaluator signs a declaration of confidentiality and absence of conflict of interest. Committee decisions require a quorum, and each round is closed with a signed selection-confirmation report. Scholarship awards are approved by the FSTP Management Office and communicated by official acceptance letter issued by the Admissions Office and signed by the Programme Director. Applicants must confirm participation within five working days of the acceptance letter.

Applicants may appeal decisions on general admissibility or programme-specific eligibility within the period stated in the rejection communication. Scholarship and ranking outcomes are not subject to academic appeal but may be reviewed for procedural compliance.

In case students decline their offer for a scholarship or scholarship funding cannot be allocated because of applicants not fulfilling the minimum thresholds, the remaining budget will move to the next available cut-off moment. If after the fifth cut-off moment, budget is remaining, it may be allocated to students from previous rounds in the order of scoring (highest to lowest).

Eligible countries

Scholarship recipients must be natural persons holding the nationality of one of the DEP eligible countries, which for the intake 2027 is the list of countries below Should the list of DEP eligible countries change, then other nationalities may become eligible.

EU Member States and Associated Digital Europe Programme (DEP) Countries: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland.

Other Eligible Non-EU Countries: Albania, Algeria, Armenia, Argentina, Australia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Canada, Egypt, Georgia, India, Israel, Japan, Jordan, Kosovo, Lebanon, Libya, Mexico, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Palestine, Serbia, Singapore, South Korea, Syria, Taiwan, Tunisia, Ukraine, United States.

Common eligibility and exclusion grounds

The conditions in this section apply to both the Energy Impact Scholarships and the DED Scholarships. Scheme-specific eligibility conditions are set out under each scholarship.

Common eligibility conditions

To be eligible for a scholarship under this call, an applicant must:

  1. hold the nationality of one of the countries listed in eligible countries.
  2. be admitted to the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI; and
  3. accept the InnoEnergy Student Code of Conduct.

Exclusion grounds

An applicant is excluded from consideration for any scholarship under this call, and any scholarship already awarded may be withdrawn, where the applicant:

  1. has previously received an InnoEnergy scholarship.
  2. has submitted false or materially misleading information at any point in the application process.
  3. is receiving other EU funding covering the same participation costs (no double funding); or
  4. is subject to EU restrictive measures.

The Admissions Office verifies these conditions on the basis of documentary evidence and records the outcome in the application tool. Applicants who do not meet the common eligibility conditions or who fall under an exclusion ground are excluded from scholarship support, with the reason recorded.

1. Energy Impact Scholarships

The Energy Impact Scholarships are awarded to applicants who demonstrate strong academic preparation and potential to contribute to the energy transition. Both full and partial scholarships are available. Selection is intrinsically linked to admission: every applicant admitted to the MSc is automatically considered, and no separate scholarship application is required.

Who is considered?

An application is admissible where the applicant has:

  1. submitted the complete online application within the published deadline and in the required certified format.
  2. obtained (or will obtain before enrolment) a Bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS, or an equivalent academic qualification from an internationally recognised university, or qualifies for conditional admission; and
  3. demonstrated English-language proficiency through an accepted test (IELTS Academic overall ≥ 6.5 with no section below 5.5; TOEFL iBT ≥ 92 with writing ≥ 22; or Cambridge CAE/CPE grades A–C), or through a documented exemption. Where the Year-2 host university requires it, a valid test result must be submitted by 15 July (intermediate) and 30 July (final) before the academic year starts.

The Admissions Office verifies admissibility. Late or incomplete applications are not admissible and are not grounds for appeal.

Programme-specific eligibility.

In addition to the common eligibility conditions, applicants for an Energy Impact Scholarship must hold a completed Bachelor’s degree of 180 ECTS or equivalent in engineering (mechanical, electronic, electrical, civil) or a related science, with prior coverage of the fundamentals of electrical and mechanical engineering. The Programme Steering Committee confirms programme-specific eligibility.

2. Diversity, Entrepreneurship and Digital Champions (DED) Scholarships

The DED Scholarships promote diversity and inclusion and recognise entrepreneurial achievement or excellence in digital innovation for energy and sustainability. The scheme comprises three strands — Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI); Entrepreneurship; and Digital Champions — and is evaluated by the programme-independent DED Selection Committee, composed of representatives of InnoEnergy and the partner universities, and not linked to any specific MSc programme. Full and partial scholarships are available.

Who is considered?

An application to the DED scheme is admissible only where the applicant has:

  1. been admitted to the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI following the standard admissions process.
  2. paid the non-refundable registration fee of EUR 295 within the published deadline; and
  3. submitted a motivation video of 1 to 2 minutes indicating one DED strand, uploaded through the InnoEnergy Masters+ online application tool. Videos exceeding the two-minute limit are excluded.

The Admissions Office transmits the list of admissible and eligible applicants to the DED Selection Committee after the registration-fee deadline for each round.

Strand-specific eligibility

In addition to the common eligibility conditions, applicants for a DED Scholarship must meet the strand-specific profile requirements: relevant D&I engagement, gender-balance contribution, entrepreneurial experience, or digital-innovation project experience, as applicable to the selected strand.

Scholarship values

Scholarship coverage and associated rights

What follows in this section — on scholarship coverage, associated rights, and the items covered and not covered — applies equally to the Energy Impact Scholarships and the DED Scholarships. The scholarship — whether full or partial — is expressed as a waiver of the participation fee for the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI. The sections below set out what the scholarship covers, what remains for the recipient’s own account, and how the scholarship value relates to the amount declared as Financial Support to Third Parties.

Items covered by the scholarship

The full and partial scholarships are intended to cover, in whole or in part, the costs associated with the following items:

  1. Institutional enrolment at the host universities, including access to courses, exercises, and laboratory sessions (where applicable).
  2. ESADE Innovation & Entrepreneurship Track, including accommodation and travel.
  3. Masters+ events: Masters+ Connect — including travel and accommodation & Enlit Europe — accommodation only.
  4. The right to attend extra-curricular activities organised within the AESAI Programme.
  5. Examination fees.
  6. Travel costs (such as long-distance train or flight) to and from extra-curricular activities organised by the participating schools. Minor travel costs, such as bus tickets to and from the airport, are not included.
  7. Accommodation costs during extra-curricular activities.
  8. Administrative services.

Items not covered by the scholarship

The costs for the items listed below are not covered by the scholarship (non-exhaustive list). These costs are for the recipient’s own account, where applicable at the hosting university:

  1. Travel to and from the host universities.
  2. Travel to and from, and accommodation during, the internship (where applicable).
  3. Accommodation (other than accommodation during extra-curricular activities).
  4. Local transportation and parking.
  5. Visa and residence permits.
  6. Books.
  7. Transcripts and degree certificates.
  8. Recreation.
  9. Insurance.
  10. Re-examination fees and/or library late fees.
  11. Costs for introduction programmes at the hosting universities.

description: This support scheme is launched to support and facilitate Master students to take part in educational activities external to their own organization. call_title: AI4Gov-X Cascade Funding Call - first edition [AI4Gov-X-FSTP-CALL-01-2026]
description: The procedure follows the principles of: transparency, equal treatment, confidentiality, absence of conflict of interest. Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored. Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget. The final award decision is endorsed by POLI.design. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal. Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations. Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of POLI.design. Payments will be made by POLI.design, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications (for the two objectives/priorities) by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI4Gov-X consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, until twice the initially allocated amount.

Applications will be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrantsTM platform (https://polidesign.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation. Beneficiaries must be natural persons and as a precondition, be enrolled students in the MagiX master's course (for objectives/priorities 1 and 2) and/or (for objective/priority 1) in one or more of the AI4Gov-X extracurricular activities, strictly identified from the list published on the project's website, at this link: https://ai4gov-x.eu/extracurricular-activities/. Please note that the list will be updated on a monthly basis while the Call is open. Additionally for objective/priority 2 only, beneficiaries must be unemployed people, able to document the existence of an internship contract with a host organisation from the public or private sector, residing in an eligible country for the Call (for a full list see Further information below).

A same natural person holding the necessary requisites may apply to both objectives within the same cut-off date or within two distinct cut-off dates. However, he or she can receive the financial benefits of either objective/priority only once.

Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, POLI.design. Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.

For both priorities/objectives, admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrantsTM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.

To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:

- A signed application form,

- Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv),

- A motivation letter, specifically mentioning their employment status,

- Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable),

- Signed declarations (on conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrantsTM platform.

Applicants to priority/objective 1 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course and/or in an extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, and

- An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, fees, etc.).

Applicants to priority/objective 2 must additionally submit:

- A proof of enrollment or acceptance in the MagiX master's course,

- Copy of an internship contract, or equivalent legally binding agreement, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date, showing the amount paid by the host organisation.

All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.

For both priorities/objectives, eligibility conditions will be that

- The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below).

- They must be enrolled in, or formally accepted into, the MagiX master's course and/or any of the extracurricular activities of AI4Gov-X (depending on the priority/objective) at the time of application.

- They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country.

- They cannot receive double funding for the same operation.

- They cannot be awarded twice under the same priority/objective.

- They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with POLI.design or any other AI4Gov-X partner.

For priority/objective 2 only, a supplementary eligibility condition will be that

- The applicants must be unemployed people documenting their enrollment in an internship programme at a host organisation residing in an eligible country (see Further information below).

Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points):

Criterion

Description

Score

Excellence and relevance

Academic/professional background and relevance to AI4Gov-X topics

0–30

Motivation and expected impact

Motivation, expected learning and career impact

0–25

Financial need

Economic situation and justification of need

0–25

European added value

Cross-border dimension, diversity contribution, EU public sector fit

0–20

No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order:

- Applicants documenting their enrollment in (or acceptance into) both the MagiX master's course and at least one extracurricular activity of the AI4Gov-X programme (only for objective/priority 1);

- Applicants coming from countries that are not full members of the AI4Gov-X consortium.

- Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average.

- Female applicants.

The maximum financial support per beneficiary is:

EUR 5 000 (for both priorities/objectives 1 and 2)

The awarded amount for priority/objective 1 is calculated on the basis of:

- Actual and justified travel costs,

- Actual and justified accommodation costs,

- Actual and documented registration/participation fees.

as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.

The awarded amount for priority/objective 2 is calculated on the basis of the stipend/salary received by the beneficiary, as documented in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement (see above). For the avoidance of any doubt, the reimbursement of travel and accommodation costs, or other types of cost, is also eligible provided it is explicitly mentioned in the internship contract, or equivalent agreement.

For both priorities/objectives, eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application.

The priority/objective 1 scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 156.

The priority/objective 2 scheme reimburses an equivalent amount to the one perceived by the intern, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 234.

call_title: Open Call for innovative projects enhancing the valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams
description: This call targets innovative SMEs developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams, contributing to more sustainable and resilient agri-food ecosystems through the development of new processes, services and products. This Innovation Call includes financial support for projects especially focusing on the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients for food and non-food applications, products, business processes, and technologies (including digital) that maximise the valorisation of agri-food biomass and side-streams. These projects should have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6. 1.The Innovation Open Call targets: SMEs in the agri-food production and/or processing sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise their own biomass/by-products/side-streams for the agri-food sector; SMEs offering solutions and/or technology for the valorisation of biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector (development and application of new technologies or processes). 2.The applicant’s project must lead to the implementation of either a new process, a new product, or a new service or a combination of them. 3.Proposals can be submitted either by a single SME or by an SMEs consortium with up to three (3) SMEs. 4.Applicants can be SMEs registered at EU Member States and countries associated to the Single Market Programme. 5.Projects must have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of at least 6. 6.For Single SME projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (1 SME) is €60.000. 7.For collaborative projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (2-3 SMEs) is €90.000. 8.Innovation grants must be matched by at least 15% private financial contribution (debt or own financial resources), with proof required. AMENDMENT 16 JULY 2026 Following aspects of the call text have been updated and clarified: Thematic priorities - scope of the call and valorisation pathways Call definitions: biosolutions added, TRL requirements clarified Documents required: no stamp needed, only signature Eligibility criteria Evaluation procedure, criteria and scoring: 2 stage evaluation process in Cut-off 2, pre-selection (knock-out stage) added. Timing of the evaluation procedure cut-off 2 prolonged Re-submission of proposals: to be done in new application form Period to file complaints SPOC contact details Pay attention that there is an adapted application form for cut-off 2!

This evaluation period shall take place within two months after the closure of each cut-off date.

Top-ranked proposals that meet the threshold scores will be awarded and contacted immediately after the final ranking and enter the Sub-Grant Agreement phase which shall last approximately one month.

call_title: WoodStock Grants to support climate-smart wood construction solutions
description: The construction sector is central to Europe's climate transition. At the same time, significant volumes of hardwood, residual wood, low-quality wood, and damaged wood remain until today underutilised. Unlocking this potential can reduce waste, strengthen local value chains, and create sustainable economic opportunities. The WoodStock grants support this transition by supporting one-year projects that combine innovation, circularity, and community engagement — embedding the New European Bauhaus (NEB) values of together, sustainable, and beautiful into practical construction solutions. Funding may be used for one or more of the following activities: Demonstration: Prototyping, experimental set-up of innovations related to WoodStock. Testing: Physical and mechanical validation, certification preparation. Co-creation: Activities with local actors and users to improve the solution and embed them in the local value chain and community. Training: Workshops to develop new skills and knowledge. Dissemination: Communication about the solutions to a wide audience (including video production) (max. 20% of total budget)., Eligible expenses may include equipment, laboratory testing, materials, logistics, multimedia production, and staff costs related to the above-mentioned activities. Selected projects are expected to: Develop climate-smart wood construction solutions beyond TRL5. Jointly organise one co-creation session with a WoodStock Living Lab in the Netherlands, France, Slovenia, Poland, Ireland or Norway. Document successful and unsuccessful innovation steps they have made, and lessons learned throughout the process. Share experiences and lessons learned with the WoodStock consortium. Contribute to the WoodBook and the European Wood Construction Observatory. Align dissemination with the WoodStock communication partner and contribute to WoodStock communication materials by providing input. For questions about the call, please contact grants@woodstockproject.eu.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Funding body: Ghent University

Who can apply?

Eligible applicants must be:

  1. An SME, start-up, or non-profit organisation
  2. Or a consortium led by an SME, start-up or non-profit organisation

Applicants must be based in an EU Member State or a country associated with Horizon Europe (Pillar 2).

Professionals from architecture, design, forestry, wood industries, construction, and green building sectors, as well as members of the European Bauhaus community are encouraged to apply. Interdisciplinary collaboration across the wood construction value chain is strongly encouraged.

Two-step selection process

Step 1 - eligibility criteria

Proposals must:

  1. Be submitted through the Evalato submission form on the WoodStock website before the call deadline
  2. Be in line with the description and involve participant(s) from EU Member State(s) or countries associated with Horizon Europe
  3. Demonstrate how they will achieve at least ambition level I for each of the NEB values (together, sustainable, beautiful), using the NEB Compass
  4. Demonstrate how they will facilitate the use of at least one type of currently underutilised wood source types: hardwood, damaged wood, low-quality wood, and post-consumer and residual wood as defined by the WoodStock project

Only proposals meeting these criteria will be further evaluated.

Please note that there is a strict prohibition of double funding from the EU budget. Applicants will be required to confirm that the project, in whole or in part, has not received funding from any other EU grant and has not been or will not be submitted for funding under any other EU grant.

Step 2 - evaluation criteria

Eligible proposals will be scored (0-5 points per criterion). Each proposal must score at least 3 points for each evaluation criterion. Based on the overall scores, all proposals that meet the threshold will be ranked.

The six evaluation criteria are:

  1. New European Bauhaus: Embedding the NEB values (together, sustainable, beautiful). Applicants should specify their ambition levels and demonstrate how they make usre of the NEB working principles: participatory processes, multi-level engagement, and transdisciplinary approach. Applicants can consult the WoodStock zero-waste design guidelines for inspiration on how to apply the NEB values to concepts using underutilised wood.
  2. Circularity: Demonstrating in qualitative and quantitative ways the benefits in local wood use, resource efficiency, zero-waste design, longevity, and environmental gains. This criterion will be evaluated based on the WoodStock design guidelines.
  3. Community-based: Integrating clearly into the local community through co-creation activities, local employment, or a positive social impact.
  4. Scalability: Providing a realistic and concise plan for scaling and replicating the innovation to increase the potential for positive impact.
  5. Systemic: Contributing to systemic change across the wood construction value chain. Consortia that create meaningful collaborations between otherwise disconnected actors will be preferred.
  6. Capacity of the applicant: Proving demonstrated expertise, experience, equipment, and networks to achieve the project objectives.

The following criteria provide added value for the selection but are not required for eligibility:

  1. Innovative business model: Proposals with a clear plan for a circular and (environmentally and socially) sustainable business model will be preferred, supported by the sustainable business model canvas (NEB Toolbox).
  2. Existing building stock: Solutions applicable to upgrading the existing building stock (including renovation, building extensions, or valorisation of underused urban spaces) will be preferred.

furtherInformation:
The WoodStock Grants offer a unique opportunity for SMEs, start-ups, non-profit organisations, or consortia led by one of these to make better use of underutilised wood in construction and develop climate-smart wood construction solutions beyond Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 5.

Through this call, four selected projects will receive up to € 50,000 each to test, validate and scale up innovative zero-waste solutions in real-world contexts. The committee will award a maximum of one grant per EU Member State (or Horizon Europe associated country), based on the country of the lead applicant only. One project will be granted per underutilised wood source type (hardwood, low-quality wood, damaged wood, post-consumer wood and residual wood). If a wood source type has no application that reaches 3 points on every evaluation criterion, the overall second-best proposal from among the other underutilised wood source types will be granted instead. By joining the WoodStock project, grant recipients will contribute to activating the European wood construction market and to demonstrating the feasibility and scalability of circular approaches across the value chain.

€ 30,000 will be paid upon signing the agreement. A progress report is required after six months, and a final report after one year. The final payment will be made following positive evaluation.

The selection committee may adjust proposed budgets if necessary (without exceeding € 50,000).

Funding restrictions defined by the European Commission or the Research Executive Agency for Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) may also apply.

In case an SME is involved in multiple project applications, please be aware that the total amount of funding received within the WoodStock grants cannot exceed € 60,000, in accordance with Financial Support to Third Parties regulations.

Estimated timeline:

  1. 15 December 2026, 17:00 CET: deadline for submitting
  2. January 2027: evaluation period
  3. February 2027: information to applicants
  4. February - March 2027: signature of the grant agreements
  5. March - April 2027 (at the latest): starting date of the actions
  6. After half a year: progress report
  7. After 1 year: final reporting, including a financial report
  8. September 2028: reports of the actions evaluated
  9. October 2028: final payments

beneficiaryAdministration:
TU Wien DigHum Summer School


Applications are open from April 28, 2026. The deadline to submit the applications is June 28, 2026, at 4.00 p.m. (Eastern European Time, EET).

Applicants are required to complete the Application Form and upload the following documents, clearly labelled with the applicant's name:

1) Signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

2)  Curriculum Vitae;

3)  Short Motivation Letter;

4)  Supporting Documents for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.

Applications must be submitted in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English. If the provided documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.


Evaluation Committee

A Joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by TU Wien, will review all applications. The Committee will include:

●   Representatives of TU Wien (4 persons) 

●   At least one student representative of TU Wien ;

●   At least one representative from the EURIDICE consortium partners.

The Committee will finalize the evaluation by June 30.



The Joint Evaluation Committee will assess each application and assign points according to the following criteria:

1.  Academic and Social Achievements

-   Academic performance, scientific, volunteering, and social activities: 5- 20 points.

2.  Certified Disabilities

-   Based on verified disability documentation: 5 points.

3.  Low Socio-Economic Background

-   Applicants whose family income falls between the first quartile (Q1) and the median income (Q2) in their country of origin will receive will receive 5 points. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the application.




All applications will be ranked based on the total number of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application may receive a maximum of 30 points in total. A total of 5 scholarships will be awarded. 

The decision of the Evaluation Committee is final.

The list of selected scholarship recipients will be published on the EURIDICE website at TU Wien.



Purpose, Amount, and Duration of the Scholarship

TU Wien hereby announces a Call for Applications for the Digital Humanism Summer School 2026, this call is issued within the framework of the activities planned under the Project European Inclusive Education for Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (EURIDICE), and is intended for masters students and young researchers across different fields of study of specialized modules as produced under the EURIDICE project in the 2025/2026 academic year. The total budget allocated for this Call amounts to EUR 13.140,00.

The Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the Digital Humanism Summer School. Its objectives are to:

●  support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds by providing them with equal access to international learning opportunities;

●  promote inclusiveness, diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education;

●  cover participation fee, accommodation and travel costs.

The scholarship also serves as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic barriers that hinder participation in international education.

The scholarship is awarded as a lump sum for a one-week period. There is no automatic entitlement or renewal.

The amount of the scholarship is EUR 1100.00 per external student (this lump sum covers participation fee, accommodation for six nights, and travel expenses to and from Vienna), or EUR 480 for students residing in Vienna. 

Expected duration ofthe Scholarship Programme: 1 week.

Scholarships will be awarded based on the evaluation scores (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded per application.



Eligibility Criteria

1.  Eligible applicants include all students from European countries and countries associated to DIGITAL EUROPE PROGRAMME who face financial challenges during their studies.

2.  Students are also encouraged to apply if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

1. Students with Certified Disabilities

Students with certified disabilities may apply for a Summer School scholarship. According to Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, persons with disabilities are defined as those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of national disability status.

2. Students with Low Socio-Economic Backgrounds

Students from families with low socio-economic conditions are eligible to apply. Low socio- economic status is defined according to students' family income. Required proofs include a tax statement, income certificate, or official social benefit statement.


This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by the TU Wien.

The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by TU Wien in its own name and under its own responsibility. TU Wien’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of TU Wien.

The Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the Digital Humanism Summer School. Its objectives are to:

●  support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds by providing them with equal access to international learning opportunities;

●  promote inclusiveness, diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education;

●  cover participation fee, accommodation and travel costs.

The scholarship also serves as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic barriers that hinder participation in international education.

The scholarship is awarded as a lump sum for a one-week period. There is no automatic entitlement or renewal.

The amount of the scholarship is EUR 1100.00 per external student (this lump sum covers participation fee, accommodation for six nights, and travel expenses to and from Vienna), or EUR 480 for students residing in Vienna. 

Expected duration ofthe Scholarship Programme: 1 week.

Scholarships will be awarded based on the evaluation scores (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded per application.



Eligibility Criteria

1.  Eligible applicants include all students from European countries and countries associated to DIGITAL EUROPE PROGRAMME who face financial challenges during their studies.

2.  Students are also encouraged to apply if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

1. Students with Certified Disabilities

Students with certified disabilities may apply for a Summer School scholarship. According to Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, persons with disabilities are defined as those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of national disability status.

2. Students with Low Socio-Economic Backgrounds

Students from families with low socio-economic conditions are eligible to apply. Low socio- economic status is defined according to students' family income. Required proofs include a tax statement, income certificate, or official social benefit statement.


This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by the TU Wien.

The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by TU Wien in its own name and under its own responsibility. TU Wien’s own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of TU Wien.
