description: The procedure follows the principles of: transparency, equal treatment, confidentiality, absence of conflict of interest. Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored. Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget. The final award decision is endorsed by UVEG. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal. Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement (see text here: https://aisecrett.eu/bid-to-our-call/FSA) specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations. Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of UVEG. Payments will be made by UVEG, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI-SECRETT consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, up to twice the initially allocated amount. A same natural person can apply multiple times at different cut-off dates but can receive the financial benefits of this Call only once.

Applications will only be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrantsTM platform (https://aisecrett.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation.

Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, Universidad de Valencia (UVEG). Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.

Admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrantsTM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.

To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:

-      A signed application form;

-      Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv);

-      A motivation letter (explicitly stating employment status and financial need);

-      Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable);

-      Signed declarations (no conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrantsTM platform;

-      A proof of enrolment or acceptance in the AI-SECRETT master’s programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date;

-      A proof of enrolment or acceptance in at least one extracurricular activity of the AI-SECRETT project, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date; and

-      An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, registration/participation fees, other costs).

All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.

Eligibility conditions will be that

-      The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below);

-      They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country;

-      They cannot receive double funding for the same operation;

-      They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with UVEG or any other AI-SECRETT partner.

Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points):

Criterion

Description

Max score

Excellence and relevance

Academic/professional background and fit with AI‑SECRETT vertical industries (*)

30

Motivation and expected impact

Learning objectives, career impact, clarity of plan

25

Financial need

Economic situation and justification of requested support

25

European added value

Cross‑border dimension, diversity contribution

20

(*) Agri-Food, Cultural and Creative Industries, Energy and Environment, Housing, Manufacturing, Mobility and Transport, and Non-Touristic Services.

No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order:

  1. Applicants enrolled in more than one extracurricular activity.
  2. Applicants from countries not full members of the AI‑SECRETT consortium.
  3. Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average.
  4. Female applicants (if merit equivalent).

The maximum financial support per beneficiary is:

EUR 5 000 (five thousand Euros / 00)

The awarded amount is calculated on the basis of:

-      Actual and justified travel costs,

-      Actual and justified accommodation costs,

-      Actual and documented registration/participation fees,

-      Actual, justified and documented other costs.

as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.

The awarded amount will be adjusted to the recipient’s country of origin following the latest adjustment coefficients of the Marie Skłodowska Curie actions available (see e.g. https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/wp-call/2023-2024/wp-2-msca-actions_horizon-2023-2024_en.pdf).

Eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application.

The scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 240.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Biodiversa+ is pleased to announce that its 6th annual EC co-funded research call - BiodivFuture - will be open on the 9 of September.

A two-step application procedure will apply, with a mandatory submission of pre-proposals at the first step and submission of full proposals at the second step, via the Electronic Proposal Submission System (EPSS).


TRANSNATIONAL RESEARCH CONSORTIA AND ELIGIBILIT

To be eligible, transnational research consortia must be composed of eligible research partners from minimum 3 different countries financially participating in the call and requesting support from minimum 3 different Funding Organisations; including at least two different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries.

Proposals must be exclusively written in English.

Each research partner involved in a proposal must comply with the eligibility criteria and rules of its national / regional funding organisations.

ASSESSMENT CRITERIA

Research proposals will be evaluated by independent experts against the following criteria:

1.   At step 1 (pre-proposal stage): (1) Fit to the scope of the call, (2) novelty of the research and (3) impact;

2.   At step 2 (full proposal stage): (1) [Scientific] excellence, (2) quality and efficiency of the implementation [of the project plan], and (3) impact (including expected policy and societal impact, and approach to stakeholder engagement).

Research proposals shall demonstrate significant transnational added value of the project. In addition, they are expected to be interdisciplinary, involving as needed multiple academic disciplines (natural sciences, technical sciences, social sciences, humanities and art). Proposals are also strongly encouraged to be transdisciplinary to include non-academic stakeholders working together with researchers to co-produce knowledge of high relevance for society and end-user oriented. 

Applicants must carefully read the detailed assessment criteria (Call Document 6).

All detailed information are available from www.biodiversa.eu/biodivfuture

furtherInformation:
SCOPE OF THE CALL

BiodivFuture focuses on supporting future-looking research and innovation that will address biodiversity and novel ecosystems, as well as their socio-ecological dynamics and consequences relating to the sustainability goals of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and associated future pathways and trajectories of change. The call covers investigating the causes (drivers), effects (biological responses), and outcomes (including opportunities, risks and trade-offs) of current and future trajectories of change in all relevant realms (terrestrial, freshwater, marine and coastal areas), in all regions of the world. It aims at funding novel, high-quality transnational research with potential for societal and political impact that will significantly improve our understanding of novel ecosystems with holistic, systemic, and integrated approaches.

In the face of inevitable and potentially irreversible change, knowledge generated under this call should ultimately lead to actions to achieve impacts that sustain resilient, interconnected, diverse and ecologically functioning ecosystems. This could include critical reflection on what constitutes ecosystem states that best preserve or restore natural resources by taking multiple costs and benefits (trade-offs) into account and the diversity of contexts, scales, perspectives and world views. Well-functioning ecosystems should benefit people and protect nature at scales from local to global and emphasise biodiversity, trophic complexity, economic vitality, and societal well-being.

THEMES

Research priorities covered by BiodivFuture are structured into three non-mutually exclusive themes. Projects are welcome to address one or several of these themes.

  1. THEME A – NOVEL ECOSYSTEM FUNCTIONING: Understanding the functioning of novel ecosystems and their links to socio-cultural and socio-economic dynamics, identifying mechanisms and developing approaches that can facilitate biodiversity gains.
  2. THEME B – PATHWAYS TO NOVEL ECOSYSTEMS: Studying robust, plausible, and concrete pathways to novel ecosystems and associated socio-ecological dynamics to prosper under temporal asynchronies and uncertainties.
  3. THEME C – BIODIVERSITY BENEFITS AND EQUITY IN THE CONTEXT OF NOVEL ECOSYSTEM: Studying fair and equitable sharing of biodiversity benefits in the context of novel ecosystems, supported by inclusive, collaborative, and investment-oriented pathways for nature-positive socio-ecological transformation.


NOVEL ECOSYSTEMS - A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK TO SET THE SCEN

Novel ecosystems have been defined by Hobbs et al. in 2013 as “a system of abiotic, biotic and social components (and their interactions) that, by virtue of human influence, differ from those that prevailed historically, having a tendency to self-organise, and manifest novel qualities without intensive human management”. Since the publication of this paper, the limits of this definition have been challenged by different disciplines and other definitions have emerged. Overall, the conceptual framework of novel ecosystems usually comprises of (1) new ecological communities (including species living outside their historical native ranges), (2) which present a suite of interactions and processes consistent with a self-organised, functioning ecosystem, and (3) are unlikely to revert to conditions preceding their emergence, with or without human intervention, due to significant biotic and abiotic changes. Building on this framework and acknowledging the plurality of views and definitions, proposals submitted to this call must demonstrate how they are addressing novel ecosystems.


Applicants must carefully read the announcement of opportunity (Call Document 1) that further details the scope of the call.


PARTICIPATING COUNTRIES

The full up-to-date list of funding organisations participating in this call, their reserved budget and their national / regional eligibility rules are available on the Biodiversa+ website: https://www.biodiversa.eu/biodivfuture-funding-organisations/

description: The scope of the I3FLOAT 1st Open Call is to fund SMEs with proposed innovations in the field of Floating Offshore Wind and proposing a technological solution to one of the challenges posed by the I3FLOAT project. The support scheme aims to fund projects that are relatively close to commercialisation. The expected current TRLs for projects funded under the support scheme are TRL 6-8. Applicants to the 1st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges, which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges, more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner. Open Challenges refers to innovations that are aligned with the 44 prioritised innovation lines identified in the Floating Wind Strategic Innovation Agenda in areas such as Floating substructures, mooring systems and dynamic cables; Electrical infrastructure and grid connection; Wind turbine, tower or alternative supporting structures and FOW-specific control; Industrialisation; Logistics and offshore installation; Operation, Maintenance and Decommissioning. Further detail is available in the Annex 1 of the Submission Toolkit. Specific Challenges are related to specific sectoral needs proposed by so-called Challenge Owners. Examples would be the challenge "Single-pass welding outside for local FOWT serial assembly" proposed by I3FLOAT partner Eolink or "Logistic optimization on the transport of offshore wind structures" proposed by I3 Board member Navantia Seanergies. The list of the 11 Specific Challenges is available in Annex 2 of the Submission Toolkit.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The I3FLOAT Open Call will open on September 7th, 2026, 10:00 CEST (Brussels Time). To apply, please complete the submission form on the Goodgrants platform at the following link, no later than November 10, 2026, at 17:00 CET (Brussels Time).

Each applicant can request a maximum of € 60,000. As an application can bring up to two applicants from two different regions in collaboration, the maximum budget for each project application can be € 120,000.

Applicants to the 1st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges, which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges, more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner. The Open Call will fund up to 10 innovations proposed for Open Challenges and up to 11 innovations corresponding respectively to each of the 11 Specific Challenges.

SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application. Only one application per SME will be accepted. if an SME is present alone or in a consortium in more than one proposal, only the last submitted proposal will be admissible.

Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met:

  1. Applicants must be SMEs according to the European definition of SMEs. The formal definition and the SME self-assessment questionnaire are available here;
  2. Applicants must have their headquarters or an affiliated entity in one of the regions represented in the I3FLOAT consortium, and/or be a member of one cluster partner in the I3FLOAT project by June 2026, and/or be established in a Less Developed Region - LDR or outermost or overseas region following the European Commission definitions;
  3. Applicants should be able to prove their financial stability and capacity and pass any financial check. This includes completing a financial capacity self-assessment available here and align with the obligations listed in section 7.3.1 of the Submission Toolkit;
  4. Applications should address either one of the 11 Specific or one of the 44 Open I3FLOAT Challenges. If an application addresses more than one challenges, it will be declared not eligible
  5. Applicants cannot submit several proposals. If several applications from the same applicants are submitted, only the latest one will be admissible;
  6. Applicants should not have any ownership connection with one partner in the I3FLOAT consortium;
  7. Applications must be written in English (applications partially or completely written in another language are not eligible);

The evaluation and selection process is overseen by two partners of the I3FLOAT project, BASQUENERGY Cluster and Pôle Mer Méditerranée, constituting the Evaluation Committee. All other partners and members of the I3FLOAT Advisory Board are taking part in the evaluation and selection process as evaluators.

Following the submission of applications, a three-steps assessment process will be followed, safeguarding the principles of transparency and equal treatment, as described below:

1) Eligibility check of the application form;

2) Qualitative evaluation of each application by 3 partners of the I3FLOAT project or members of the I3 Advisory Board.

3) Ranking list of all scores. A ranking list per Specific Challenge will be done. The highest score will be selected for funding. For Open Challenges, only one ranking list will be done, and applications will be selected following the ranking until the available budget has been spent.

description:
The scope of the I3FLOAT 1st Open Call is to fund SMEs with proposed innovations in the field of Floating Offshore Wind and proposing a technological solution to one of the challenges posed by the I3FLOAT project. The support scheme aims to fund projects that are relatively close to commercialisation. The expected current TRLs for projects funded under the support scheme are TRL 6-8.

Applicants to the 1st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges, which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges, more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner.

Open Challenges refers to innovations that are aligned with the 44 prioritised innovation lines identified in the Floating Wind Strategic Innovation Agenda in areas such as Floating substructures, mooring systems and dynamic cables; Electrical infrastructure and grid connection; Wind turbine, tower or alternative supporting structures and FOW-specific control; Industrialisation; Logistics and offshore installation; Operation, Maintenance and Decommissioning. Further detail is available in the Annex 1 of the Submission Toolkit.

Specific Challenges are related to specific sectoral needs proposed by so-called Challenge Owners. Examples would be the challenge "Single-pass welding outside for local FOWT serial assembly" proposed by I3FLOAT partner Eolink or "Logistic optimization on the transport of offshore wind structures" proposed by I3 Board member Navantia Seanergies. The list of the 11 Specific Challenges is available in Annex 2 of the Submission Toolkit.
destinationDetails:
The I3FLOAT Open Call will open on September 7th, 2026, 10:00 CEST (Brussels Time). To apply, please complete the submission form on the Goodgrants platform at the following link, no later than November 10, 2026, at 17:00 CET (Brussels Time).

Each applicant can request a maximum of € 60,000. As an application can bring up to two applicants from two different regions in collaboration, the maximum budget for each project application can be € 120,000.

Applicants to the 1st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges, which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges, more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner. The Open Call will fund up to 10 innovations proposed for Open Challenges and up to 11 innovations corresponding respectively to each of the 11 Specific Challenges.

SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application. Only one application per SME will be accepted. if an SME is present alone or in a consortium in more than one proposal, only the last submitted proposal will be admissible.

Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met:

  1. Applicants must be SMEs according to the European definition of SMEs. The formal definition and the SME self-assessment questionnaire are available here;
  2. Applicants must have their headquarters or an affiliated entity in one of the regions represented in the I3FLOAT consortium, and/or be a member of one cluster partner in the I3FLOAT project by June 2026, and/or be established in a Less Developed Region - LDR or outermost or overseas region following the European Commission definitions;
  3. Applicants should be able to prove their financial stability and capacity and pass any financial check. This includes completing a financial capacity self-assessment available here and align with the obligations listed in section 7.3.1 of the Submission Toolkit;
  4. Applications should address either one of the 11 Specific or one of the 44 Open I3FLOAT Challenges. If an application addresses more than one challenges, it will be declared not eligible
  5. Applicants cannot submit several proposals. If several applications from the same applicants are submitted, only the latest one will be admissible;
  6. Applicants should not have any ownership connection with one partner in the I3FLOAT consortium;
  7. Applications must be written in English (applications partially or completely written in another language are not eligible);

The evaluation and selection process is overseen by two partners of the I3FLOAT project, BASQUENERGY Cluster and Pôle Mer Méditerranée, constituting the Evaluation Committee. All other partners and members of the I3FLOAT Advisory Board are taking part in the evaluation and selection process as evaluators.

Following the submission of applications, a three-steps assessment process will be followed, safeguarding the principles of transparency and equal treatment, as described below:

1) Eligibility check of the application form;

2) Qualitative evaluation of each application by 3 partners of the I3FLOAT project or members of the I3 Advisory Board.

3) Ranking list of all scores. A ranking list per Specific Challenge will be done. The highest score will be selected for funding. For Open Challenges, only one ranking list will be done, and applications will be selected following the ranking until the available budget has been spent.
duration: 12 months (projects must be implemented between 1 January 2027 and 31 December 2027)

description: ECT2 will expand the existing portfolio of whole-city transformation activities and interventions by focusing on implementation barriers shared by cities across the Mission. The core shift introduced in this call is a move away from broad, domain-based support towards a more focused model that organises action around clearly defined systemic barriers and bottlenecks. To this end, ECT2 is organised around six challenge areas which represent critical city-wide implementation barriers that currently prevent cities from translating Climate City Contract ambitions into replicable and scalable outcomes. The challenge areas are: Place-based heating and cooling Nature Based Solutions at city scale Urban energy systems City finance innovation for climate neutrality Large-scale building retrofits and renovations Decarbonising urban mobility and logistics All applicants must: Choose the challenge area that resonates most and anchor the rationale for intervention within this area. Within their chosen challenge area, formulate an adequate context-specific impact pathway following the impact framework. While the impact pathway describes how the proposed intervention is expected to create change, the Impact Framework provides the progression from problem to impact and the structure for how that change will be monitored, evidenced and reported. Across all challenge areas, ECT2 aims to enable cities to move from constrained implementation to durable, city-wide transformation by combining activities which remove diagnosed systemic blockers and accelerate progress to climate neutrality. To this end, the programme aims to ensure that Mission Cities can: Deploy and scale climate‑neutral solutions by addressing institutional, policy, financial, governance, market or social bottlenecks that limit uptake or speed. Translate research, innovation and evidence into operational policy and delivery systems, ensuring that scientific and technical knowledge is effectively embedded into city decision‑making. Strengthen city capacities and capabilities so that climate‑neutral delivery becomes business‑as‑usual, independent of individual champions or one‑off projects. Cover a broad range of levers for change (policy, green technology, finance, governance, behavioural change, social innovation, multi-actor collaboration, procurement, new business models as circular economy, etc.) Enable collaborative governance and citizen engagement models that support systemic, cross‑sectoral climate action and deliver just transition outcomes. The selection of proposals will result in multiple implementation-enabling innovations focussing on resolving key implementation challenges. Interventions will work individually and in combinations/clusters to generate resolutions for shared barriers. Activities eligible for funding are: Interventions should consist of the following activities to be eligible for funding: Pioneering Activities: Activities that adapt, test or deploy innovative or enabling solutions at city level. Systemic, Science‑based Innovative Initiatives: Activities that strengthen the connection between research, evidence and city delivery. Capacity and capability‑building activities: Activities that establish new knowledge, skills and institutional competence within city administrations and key local actors. Collaborative governance and community‑building activities: Activities that build more collaborative, inclusive and systemic governance arrangements. Please note: proposed interventions may cover several or all of these descriptions of eligible activities – this list is intended to allow for flexibility in proposing interventions, rather than limiting proposed interventions to any one eligible activity alone. Applicants will be requested at the point of submitting a proposal to describe and declare the links between their proposed interventions and the eligible activities as listed above. For more information please refer to the Call Guidelines, which provide information on the aim, scope, and approach of the call and clarify how to submit a proposal, budget requirements, and the review mechanism and decision-making process.

beneficiaryAdministration:
This Call for proposals, to support the drastic cut down of greenhouse gas emissions and the achievement of ‘climate neutrality’, invites Mission Cities from the “100 Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities by 2030” to undertake a 22‑month grant-supported programme centred around innovations that aim to overcome systemic implementation challenges in order to shift the dial from testing and experimentation to enable whole-city transformation and generate evidence fit for multi-city pan-European replication and adoption.

Reflecting the experiences and learnings from previous calls, the ECT2 call particularly seeks solutions that can translate enabling innovations into durable and policy-anchored delivery structures which will more likely generate sustained emissions reductions and EU-wide transformation.

For any information please contact ect@netzerocities.eu.


How to submit a proposal?

The applications are submitted online via the grant management platform:

If not already registered with the system, use this link to register.

If you have previously registered with the system (i.e. for applying to one of the Pilot Cities Programme calls): please use this link (and bookmark it!) to log-in.

If you do not remember your password, please use these password reset instructions

Guidance on how to submit your application can be found through the following links:

  1. How to register in the System?
  2. FAQ & Instructions

Please note that any proposals submitted outside of the proposal submission system will not be accepted; and that the system will be locked after the deadline. If you experience technical difficulties, please consult the system guidance. If you are still unable to resolve your system issue, follow the guidance on how to raise a support request via appropriate channels.


Who can apply?

Only local authorities or city administrations selected to be part of EU Mission for climate-neutral and smart cities by 2030 (Mission Cities) are eligible to apply to and receive funding under this Call. For the avoidance of doubt, this call is addressed to designated Mission cities only and therefore these consortia may not include other city, district, or municipal authorities (i.e., ‘non-Mission’).

Please note: Administrations of a higher level of governance (i.e., a metropolis, region, or national/governmental departments) are eligible to participate as consortium partners where there is a formal governance link with the Mission City/cities leading or involved with the proposal. However, they do not count towards the eligible Mission City count (i.e., as related to the prescribed budget envelopes and the number present in the proposal) unless the metropolis or region is itself the Mission City, formally.


A group of Mission Cities (national or trans-national) may apply together in a consortium. However, in that case, one of the Mission Cities will have to be designated as the consortium leader for all administrative and process-related purposes. In the case of a group of cities applying together in one proposal, the size of the requested subgrant must follow the award amounts as stated at section 7.3 of the Call Guidelines.

Other organisations could also participate as members of a consortium led by a Mission City. These organisations could be, for example: research institutions, universities, SMEs, NGOs, associations, citizen groups or other relevant stakeholders involved in the implementation of the climate ambitions of a Mission City participating in the consortium.


For comprehensive information, including eligibility criteria, please consult the Call Guidelines.


Evaluation process

This Call will follow a three-stage evaluation and selection process, as described in chapter 9 of the call guidelines:

Stage 1: Eligibility check

The eligibility check stage entails the assessment of pass/fail requirements . Proposals must comply to the full set of eligibility criteria to proceed to Stage 2.

Proposals that fail the eligibility criteria will not be considered further in the process and applicants will be informed of the outcome.


Stage 2: Evaluation and scoring of eligible proposals

Scores will be made against the individual assessment criteria by at least two independent external experts, based on the submitted proposals. These experts are appointed from the pool of experts identified through an open call and contracted by the coordinator as part of the NetZeroCities project. The experts from this pool are deployed against all Calls for NetZeroCities sub-granting programmes. This evaluation is made using criteria grouped into the three main categories of: Mandate to Act, Capacity to Act, and Impact.

The detailed criteria for assessment of proposals for the SGA3-NZC ECT2 programme’s financial support to third parties scheme is defined in section 9.3 of the Call Guidelines.


Stage 3: Portfolio selection & Funding decision

The selection committee will select a portfolio of interventions through a dedicated selection process. The portfolio will be selected with the intention to support Mission Cities to overcome challenges to, experimenting with, and learning about, the implementation phase of the Cities Mission: i.e. enabling (Cities) Mission innovation implementation. It will also aim at complementing the existing cohorts of Enabling and Pilot Cities (i.e. inter-cohort portfolio) selected through previous calls, creating opportunities to exploit learning and outcomes of these diverse interventions over the course of the programme.

All submissions will be assessed fairly and transparently in the scope of the eligibility criteria, assessment of quality criteria, and strategic programme considerations as outlined in section 9.4 of the Call Guidelines. Decisions as to whether a proposal is accepted or rejected will be communicated as detailed in this document.

The core shift introduced in this call is a move away from broad, domain-based support towards a more focused model that organises action around clearly defined systemic barriers and bottlenecks.

To this end, ECT2 is organised around six challenge areas which represent critical city-wide implementation barriers that currently prevent cities from translating Climate City Contract ambitions into replicable and scalable outcomes.

The challenge areas are:

  1. Place-based heating and cooling
  2. Nature Based Solutions at city scale
  3. Urban energy systems
  4. City finance innovation for climate neutrality
  5. Large-scale building retrofits and renovations
  6. Decarbonising urban mobility and logistics

All applicants must:

  1. Choose the challenge area that resonates most and anchor the rationale for intervention within this area.
  2. Within their chosen challenge area, formulate an adequate context-specific impact pathway following the impact framework. While the impact pathway describes how the proposed intervention is expected to create change, the Impact Framework provides the progression from problem to impact and the structure for how that change will be monitored, evidenced and reported.


Across all challenge areas, ECT2 aims to enable cities to move from constrained implementation to durable, city-wide transformation by combining activities which remove diagnosed systemic blockers and accelerate progress to climate neutrality. To this end, the programme aims to ensure that Mission Cities can:

  1. Deploy and scale climate‑neutral solutions by addressing institutional, policy, financial, governance, market or social bottlenecks that limit uptake or speed.
  2. Translate research, innovation and evidence into operational policy and delivery systems, ensuring that scientific and technical knowledge is effectively embedded into city decision‑making.
  3. Strengthen city capacities and capabilities so that climate‑neutral delivery becomes business‑as‑usual, independent of individual champions or one‑off projects.
  4. Cover a broad range of levers for change (policy, green technology, finance, governance, behavioural change, social innovation, multi-actor collaboration, procurement, new business models as circular economy, etc.)
  5. Enable collaborative governance and citizen engagement models that support systemic, cross‑sectoral climate action and deliver just transition outcomes.


The selection of proposals will result in multiple implementation-enabling innovations focussing on resolving key implementation challenges. Interventions will work individually and in combinations/clusters to generate resolutions for shared barriers.


Activities eligible for funding are:

Interventions should consist of the following activities to be eligible for funding:

  1. Pioneering Activities: Activities that adapt, test or deploy innovative or enabling solutions at city level.
  2. Systemic, Science‑based Innovative Initiatives: Activities that strengthen the connection between research, evidence and city delivery.
  3. Capacity and capability‑building activities: Activities that establish new knowledge, skills and institutional competence within city administrations and key local actors.
  4. Collaborative governance and community‑building activities: Activities that build more collaborative, inclusive and systemic governance arrangements.


Please note: proposed interventions may cover several or all of these descriptions of eligible activities – this list is intended to allow for flexibility in proposing interventions, rather than limiting proposed interventions to any one eligible activity alone.

Applicants will be requested at the point of submitting a proposal to describe and declare the links between their proposed interventions and the eligible activities as listed above.


For more information please refer to the Call Guidelines, which provide information on the aim, scope, and approach of the call and clarify how to submit a proposal, budget requirements, and the review mechanism and decision-making process.

duration: Twenty-two (22) months from 1st of April 2027 to 31st of January 2029
furtherInformation:
Funding

The funding will be allocated across three subgrant envelopes as follows:

  1. 500.000 EUR: proposals with a minimum of one Mission City plus at least one additional consortium partner.
  2. 1.000.000 EUR: proposals with a minimum of two distinct Mission Cities (i.e. formally selected as such), plus any additional consortium partners.
  3. 1.500.000 EUR: proposals with a minimum of three distinct Mission Cities (i.e. formally selected as such), plus any additional consortium partners.


Form of grant:

Financial support is provided in the form of a cascading grant based on, and reimbursed against, actual costs incurred and submitted in interim and final reporting.


Timeline:

  1. 31 August 2026, 12:00 CET – call launch
  2. 03 December 2026, 12:00 CET – call deadline
  3. 05 February 2027 – decision communication
  4. 19 February 2027 – publication of call outcomes and cities selected
  5. 01 April 2027 – programme starting date
  6. 31 January 2029 – programme ending date


Info Sessions:

  1. 15 September 2026 – Ambition and Approach for ECT2 (90’) REGISTER
  2. 29 September 2026 – Eligibility, Assessment Criteria and how to submit (90’) REGISTER
  3. 09 October 2026 – Impact Framework and Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) (90’) REGISTER


Relevant documentation:

  1. Call guidelines: Provide information on the aim, scope, and approach of the call and clarify how to submit a proposal, budget requirements, and the review mechanism and decision-making process.
  2. Call Financial Guidelines: Explain the application budget cost eligibility rules and contain the main legal and financial rules.
  3. ECT2 Challenge area briefs (including proposed impact pathways): contain a description of the 6 challenge areas available for selection in this call
  4. Budget Template: An Excel-based budget template to support cities and their consortium partners to draft budgets, prior to putting them in the submission system.
  5. Call Application Template: A Word template containing the application narrative questions and check-boxes for a correct submission. This is to support offline/collaborative drafting, before copying into the submission system ahead of the deadline.
  6. Work Plan Template: An Excel-based template for capturing the key work plan components, and that reflects the submission system’s work plan architecture (Work Packages, Deliverables, Activities). This is to support offline/collaborative drafting, before copying into the submission system ahead of the deadline
  7. Risk register template: An Excel-based template for capturing risks, and that reflects the submission system’s Risk table architecture. This is to support offline/collaborative drafting, before copying into the submission system ahead of the deadline
  8. Impact Framework template and Indicators Template: A template that summarizes the 'impact' section of your application and will be attached to your application in the system. Can be filled through with the indicators listed in the indicators set.
  9. Indicators set: List of indicators available for the Impact Framework.
  10. Letter of Support: Mandatory. Letter of support from the city mayor (or equivalent) and/or any city official mandated to sign on the city/mayor/city council’s behalf, for the NZC Enabling City Transformation Programme. In the case of a multi-city proposal, one letter must be provided for each city.

call_title: FORTIS Open Call #2: Pushing towards the deployment of FORTIS and Exploiting the FORTIS solution in other key sectors
description: The FORTIS Open Call #2 aims to attract system actors and innovators - universities, research organizations, mid-caps, SMEs, startups, and domain end-users - capable of incorporating their technologies into the FORTIS framework or demonstrating cross-sector adoption. Proposals must enter at TRL 4–5 and aim to achieve TRL 7 by project completion. Applicants must submit their proposal under one of the following main topics/subtopics: ● Topic OC#2.1: Pushing towards the deployment of FORTIS (Integration and pilot deployment) ○ Subtopic 1: Optimisation of HRC / Task Allocation ○ Subtopic 2: Flexible Interface Digital Twin ○ Subtopic 3: HRI Watchdog ○ Subtopic 4: HRI Activities Digital Twin ○ Subtopic 5: Omnideployment of the FORTIS Solution ○ Subtopic 6: Ergonomics-Aware Human State and Interaction Context for Adaptive HRC ○ Subtopic 7: Interfaces with XR ○ Subtopic 8: Trust-Aware Multi-Sensor Localisation and Mapping for FORTIS Robotic Platforms ● Topic OC#2.2: Exploiting the FORTIS solution in other key sectors (Open Topic for technology transfer & cross-sector validation in non-core civilian HRI domains such as agriculture, healthcare, events, retail, etc.)

beneficiaryAdministration:
The FORTIS project invites multidisciplinary consortia of eligible entities - universities/RTOs, mid-caps, SMEs, startups, and end-users - to submit proposals that demonstrate integrating, deploying, or scaling up technologies within the FORTIS ecosystem or transferring solutions to new sectors. An indicative total of 14 proposals will be supported across two main call topics:

● Topic OC#2.1 (Pushing towards the deployment of FORTIS): Total budget of € 2,065,373.46. Supports at least 8 projects with an indicative contribution of up to € 250,000 per project. Consortia must consist of 3 eligible entities (including at least 1 SME) from at least 2 different eligible countries.

● Topic OC#2.2 (Exploiting the FORTIS solution in other key sectors): Total budget of € 1,077,373.46. Supports at least 6 projects with an indicative contribution of up to € 170,000 per project. Consortia must consist of 2 eligible entities (including at least 1 SME); single-country consortia are allowed.

Funding Limits & Conditions:

● A strict lifetime cumulative ceiling of € 200,000.00 per individual legal entity applies across all FORTIS Open Calls (OC#1 and OC#2 combined).

● Funding rates follow standard Horizon Europe rules: 100% for non-profit entities (universities/RTOs) and 70% for SMEs/for-profit entities.

● Budget for non-industry partners cannot exceed 30% of the total project budget. All call information and documentation are available at: https://fortis-project.eu/open-call-2/

Applicants must apply online and complete all mandatory sections at: https://www.f6s.com/fortis-open-call-2/apply

beneficiaryAdministration:
NTNU Open Call 2 Offer  

The DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 presents a valuable opportunity for students aspiring to advance their digital skills through international placement in fields related to the digitalisation of wind and energy systems. 

Through this call, up to fifteen (15) selected candidates will receive a scholarship to support their exchange stay in Norway during either Spring or Autumn Semester of 2027. 

  1. Award type: Scholarships are provided as stipend to cover living and subsistence costs during the 6-months-exchange period. 
  2. Financial value: Each selected beneficiary will receive a stipend of EUR 6,940. 
  3. Tuition fees: Exchange students from NTNU’s partner universities are exempt from tuition fees in accordance with NTNU Regulations.  
  4. Welfare fee: All students are required to pay a mandatory welfare fee of approximately 70 EUR per semester, which must be covered personally by the applicant. This one-time payment is due by February 1st for Spring semester and September 1st for Autumn semester, and detailed instructions regarding the payment process will be provided by the NTNU International Office as part of the formal admission and enrolment procedure. 
  5. Payment mechanism: Stipends may be distributed via cash cards provided by NTNU’s Unit for International Relations for use within Norway. Disbursement is subject to signing the mobility agreement, confirmation of enrolment, and compliance with all eligibility and reporting requirements outlined in the Open Call. 
  6. Call interdependency: Autumn 2027 scholarships will be funded from the remaining funds after Spring 2027 cut-off, which makes it dependant on the number of candidates successful for the Spring 2027 call.  

Applicants profile 

DigiWind scholarships are available for students undertaking a 6-month study period at NTNU and enrolling in courses within the following eligible M.Sc. programmes: M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering and M.Sc. Marine Technology. 

Applicants must be final year students or hold one of the following degrees obtained at an internationally recognised university or higher education institution: 

  1. Bachelor of Science in Engineering (B.Sc. Eng.). 
  2. Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.). 
  3. Bachelor of Natural Science (B.Sc.). 

Applicants must have a background within a relevant field of engineering to meet the prerequisites of the M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering or M.Sc. Marine Technology courses. 

Eligible candidates must be passport holders from EU/EEA countries, or Digital Europe Programme (DEP) associated countries and demonstrate their active student status through an official Certificate of Enrolment for the current academic year in a NTNU partner university.  

Proficiency in English is a fundamental requirement, as it is the official language of both the Open Call and the master's programme. Unless the applicant is a native speaker, they must provide a certified score report meeting minimum thresholds: an IELTS Academic score of 6.5, a TOEFL iBT score of 88, or a Cambridge English (C1/C2) score of 180.  

Candidates are expected to be organized and detail-oriented, ensuring that all necessary documentation is submitted via the F6S platform for the Spring semester by the November 2nd, 2026, or for the Autumn semester by the 1 March 2027 deadline. 

Beyond technical qualifications, successful applicants will reflect DigiWind and NTNU’s core commitment to diversity, social equality, and gender balance. We particularly encourage applications from women and individuals from economically disadvantaged or diverse demographic backgrounds who seek to contribute to the wind energy field.  

Evaluation process  

Submission will be done EXCLUSIVELY via F6S platform Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027. Students are allowed to apply to only one of the semesters (either Spring 2027 or Autumn 2027).  

A complete list of applicants will be compiled, including basic information for statistical and transparency purposes (which will be also shared with the European Commission). 

Applications that pass the eligibility check will undergo an internal evaluation, conducted by a panel of experts from NTNU. For more information on the selection and evaluation process please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants.  

Results notification 

Following the expert’s evaluation, all eligible applicants will be ranked according to their final assessment scores. Scholarships will be awarded based on this order of merit, beginning with the highest-ranked candidates. 

Evaluation results will be compiled into an Evaluation Summary Report. Applicants will be notified of the results via email, as follows: 

  1. For Accepted Applicants: 
  2. An Evaluation Summary Report. 
  3. An invitation to proceed to the enrolment phase and following steps. 
  4. For Rejected Applicants: 
  5. An Evaluation Summary Report for those who passed the eligibility check and underwent internal evaluation phase. 
  6. A rejection letter to ineligible applications. 

Successful applicants must confirm their acceptance of the formal scholarship offer within five (5) business days by replying to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org.  

For more details, please refer to the Guidelines for Applicants. 

Redress process 

Applicants who are not satisfied with the evaluation of their application, may submit a written appeal within three (3) business days of receiving their result. Appeals will be reviewed by a panel, chaired by the NTNU DigiWind representative, the Project Officer and one external member.  

Appeals are typically not allowed for disagreements with the academic judgment (score) or if the decision was based on the applicants misunderstanding of the application instructions. Valid grounds for appealing scholarships offer decision generally focus on errors in the assessment process or claims of discrimination. 

All requests for appeal must be sent to the DigiWind NTNU Open Call team at ntnu-opencall@digiwind.org

description: Culture Helps Solidarity - Second call for proposals for collaboration grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
Culture Helps Solodarity - Open Call for Collaboration grants

Second Round, September - November 2026

Culture Helps Solidarity supports arts and culture professionals from Ukraine to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connection during and after the war. Running until 2028, the project combines three grant schemes - individual grants, thematic project grants, and collaboration grants - with a rich programme of mentoring, learning, and peer exchange. The project is co-funded through the Creative Europe programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (Amsterdam), an independent foundation fostering European belonging through culture; together with Insha Osvita (Kyiv), a Ukrainian NGO and professional learning community developing educational and cultural programmes; zusa (Berlin), an international NGO fostering collaboration and collective learning for social and cultural change; and the VETERANKA Movement (Kyiv), Ukraine's leading community of women veterans advocating for women's rights, leadership, and reintegration.

This open call is the second and final call for proposals for collaboration grants. At least 15 international projects will be awarded. Culture Helps Solidarity will continue to open Calls for thematic project grants and individual care grants also in 2027.

What are we looking for?

This call for proposals seeks to support collaborative projects between at least two organisations based, respectively, in Ukraine and Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU member states and more countries participating in Creative Europe) that work with culture to improve access to cultural participation and support the integration of displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries, or refugees into their host communities - with particular attention to vulnerable groups, veterans, and their mental well-being. The call prioritises partnerships between Ukrainian-led organisations, whether based in Ukraine or operating in exile, and non-Ukrainian organisations, especially from neighboring Creative Europe countries.

Through these collaborations, the call aims to foster:

  1. cross-border networking, the exchange of professional experience and good practices,
  2. stronger capacities for intercultural dialogue and mental health support, and
  3. the professional development of cultural managers,

while highlighting a culture of solidarity in shaping a European future for Ukraine.

What do we offer?

The Fund makes grants available in two amounts:

• up to €20.000 for partnerships of two organisations;

• up to €30.000 for partnerships of three or more organisations.

Grants will be awarded across these two available funding categories. Applicants must clearly indicate in their applications the grant amount for which they are applying.

Grants can cover a large variety of costs including production costs, marketing and advertising costs, rental and running costs for studios and cultural venues, IT, communication and production tools and materials, and - upon special request and where appropriate (e.g. when lost/destroyed) - purchase of other goods, means, or services necessary for the implementation and execution of the project.

Grants can also be used to cover travel costs, expert fees, artists' honoraria, legal services, staff- and operational costs. However, these amounts must all be proportionate and justifiable.

Although co-financing is not mandatory, it is recommended that the grant is used to cover a maximum of 80% of the total project budget.

The project timeline may be up to 12 months. Activities related to the project may not take place before the start date (1 February 2027).

Important notice: Applicants should take into consideration some procedural and administrative time required for contracting procedures when planning the starting date for their project. Although our grantmaking team will do their best to respect the published schedule, delays may occur due to handling unforeseeable contracting requirements. Applicants are therefore encouraged to plan their intended project start dates with sufficient flexibility in mind.

The submission deadline for proposals is Tuesday, 10th November 2026, 13:00 Amsterdam time/ 14:00 Kyiv time.

Eligibility criteria:

  1. Applications must be submitted in English and must include a complete application form and budget;
  2. Applicants must be above 18 years old and must demonstrate a sufficient level of English to work and communicate effectively in English;
  3. The call is open to collaborations of at least two organisations, with the lead applicant submitting the proposal, and entering into a grant agreement in case the proposal is selected;
  4. At least one partner must be a civic, public or private1 organisation with a legal status in Ukraine, active in Ukraine or in exile and operating in the cultural, creative or civil sector;
  5. In addition, at least one partner must be a civic, public or private organisation with a legal status and active in one of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU member states and more countries participating in Creative Europe), and operating in the cultural, creative or civil sector;
  6. At least one partner must be a cultural organisation and/or actively working on the integration of displaced Ukrainians both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries, or refugees from Ukraine into their new living environments and professional realities and communities - veterans in particular;
  7. The proposed project must not receive funding from any other Creative Europe scheme;
  8. Proposals submitted by political parties will not be considered;
  9. Strictly humanitarian initiatives or individual requests for cost-of living support will not be considered.

Selection criteria and process:

  1. Relevance to the overall theme and objectives of the call - Does the project work with arts and culture to improve access to cultural participation and support the integration of displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and/or Creative Europe countries, or refugees into host communities? Does it have a particular focus on vulnerable groups, veterans and their mental well-being through culture?
  2. Quality of partnership - Does the proposal convincingly demonstrate the partners’ capacities, complementarities between organisations and motivation to collaborate?
  3. Authenticity and experimentation - Does the proposal and the partnership constellation demonstrate a genuine and innovative approach to the call’s objectives? This includes exploring new forms of cultural collaboration, audience engagement, intercultural dialogue, or activities that contribute to mental well-being, while bringing together partners whose complementary skills, experience, and networks create meaningful cross-border learning and exchange.
  4. Feasibility and implementation potential - Does the proposal demonstrate a convincing feasibility and implementation potential, including a balanced and realistic budget?
  5. Impact - Does the proposal demonstrate how it will have a positive impact on the communities addressed? Does it demonstrate a vision for the partnership beyond the project period, and how it will contribute to building long-term cultural relations between the Ukraine and Creative Europe countries and to the broader issues of the European integration of Ukraine?
  6. Sustainability - Does the proposal embody a convincing understanding of environmental sustainability, fair and green transition and the ecological impact of war in particular?

Following an eligibility check, applications will be assessed by a team of internal and external experts from a wide range of geographic, cultural and professional areas. At least 15 international projects will be awarded.

As part of the grant, awarded partnerships will receive one-on-one mentoring support, participate in community calls as well as an in-person networking meeting. These in-kind support activities are an integral part of the grant, participation in them is therefore compulsory.

Timeline 

1 September 2026                   call for proposals open

15 September 2026                 info session & matchmaking event

10 November 2026                call closed

End of January 2027                proposals assessed and selected

1 February 2027                       earliest starting date for selected projects 2

Summer 2027                           in-person networking event (date TBC)

31 January 2028                      end date of selected projects

29 February 2028                   submission deadline for final reports


How to apply?

More information, useful tips, and the application form (which includes the budget section and budget form) are available at: https://culture-of-solidarity-fund.grantplatform.com/

Applicants are strongly encouraged to develop their proposals through human expertise, critical thinking, and artistic or professional judgment. Proposals that rely primarily on AI-generated content or concepts are discouraged and may be given lower priority in the assessment process.

Should you have further questions, please contact us at chs@culturalfoundation.eu.

﻿

2 Important notice: Applicants should take into consideration some procedural and administrative time required for contracting procedures when planning the starting date for their project. Although our grantmaking team will do their best to respect the published schedule, delays may occur due to handling unforeseeable contracting requirements. Applicants are therefore encouraged to plan their intended project start dates with sufficient flexibility in mind.

description: EFFEA Call #5

beneficiaryAdministration:
The European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists – EFFEA, an initiative of the European Festivals Association, is a fund that supports collaborations between festivals from different countries. Together, these festivals provide emerging artists with a platform to develop their work and gain visibility on the international stage. EFFEA extends an open invitation for festivals to collaborate across borders and establish a network of colleagues centred around the concept of a residency. Through EFFEA, festivals join hands to foster the success of emerging artists.

EFFEA's fifth call for festivals to support emerging artists is open from 1 September to 3 November 2026. 50 residencies will be selected involving 50 emerging artists (individuals, groups or collectives) in the seat of around 150 festivals, a leading festival in collaboration with a minimum of two partner festivals each.

There are two categories of residencies:

1. EFFEA Discovery: Festivals support artists at the early stages of their careers but with a strong potential to break through internationally. 40 grants of 8.000€ will be attributed to this category.

2. EFFEA Springboard: Festivals support artists already established in their own country and ready to develop their careers internationally. 10 grants of 15.000€ will be attributed to this category.

Eligibility criteria

  1. The partnership must represent at least 3 festivals from 3 eligible countries (1 leading festival and 2 partner festivals).
  2. Both leading and partner festivals must exist for at least one edition.
  3. Both leading and partner festivals must be registered on www.FestivalFinder.eu before submitting their application.
  4. A festival may apply for one grant as a leading festival and is eligible to apply for multiple grants as a partner festival.
  5. Proposed artists may be individual artists, collectives, companies, ensembles, or groups of any age and nationality.
  6. Artists must have either nationality or legal residence in one of the eligible countries.

Eligible Countries   

Leading festivals and artists should have their official address in one of the following eligible countries: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Montenegro, Moldova, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Tunisia, Ukraine.

Festivals with their official address from the following countries are allowed to participate as partner festivals only: Israel, Palestine, Switzerland, Turkey, and the UK. Artists from these countries can also be proposed.

Eligible disciplines

description: Social Power - Convocatoria 2

beneficiaryAdministration:
Civil society organisations based in Spain are invited to submit proposals under the Social Power project. This call supports initiatives that address three thematic rights agendas: decent employment in a fair productive system, gender justice and diversity and social protection and housing, particularly in contexts of inequality or discrimination. The three thematic rights provide a concrete operational framework to advance fundamental rights and EU values in practice.

-Call publication date: 1 September 2026

-Deadline to submit proposals: 2 November 2026 before 17:00h (CET)

-Full guidelines and application form available at: https://socialpower.es/

Evaluation criteria (maximum score 100 points):

Relevance (maximum 40 points, minimum 25): assessment of the social need, alignment with the call’s priorities, understanding of the rights situation and experience with target groups. An additional 3 bonus points will be awarded to organisations based outside Madrid and Barcelona (municipalities under 1 million inhabitants).

Quality and Coherence (maximum 40 points, minimum 3 points required for the Budget sub-criterion): sound project design, feasibility, gender mainstreaming, clarity of indicators and a realistic budget.

Impact (maximum 20 points): focus on social innovation, empowerment, alliances, participation and influence on public policy.

Only proposals scoring 70 points or more will be considered for funding. Final selection will consider thematic distribution, risk assessment and budget review.

The evaluation process will include automated tools and human oversight. A generative AI tool will support consistency by providing a preliminary analysis based on predefined criteria.

call_title: Levelling Course on Entrepreneurship in Healthcare 2027
description: Levelling Course on Entrepreneurship in Healthcare 2027

beneficiaryAdministration:
How to apply:

Step 1: register your organisation in the EU Funding & tender opportunities portal to obtain a Participant Identification Code (PIC number).

Step 2: apply to the call via EIT Health’s application platform .


The selection process is a single-stage submission followed by an admissibility and eligibility check, online pitches, and an ethical, legal, and social issues review. The below sections provide further details about each stage.

5.1.1 Admissibility and eligibility, exclusion and selection stages

1. Admissibility and Eligibility Check: Formal verification of application admissibility and eligibility status is done by EIT Health staff members according to the requirements of the Call. See chapters 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4 on application conditions.

5.1.2 Evaluation of proposals

2. Online Pitching:

Pitching sessions will consist of a pitch and a question and answers session. Each evaluation panel member will evaluate proposals based on a review of the submitted application, the pitch, and the answers to the question and answers session. The evaluation panel will consist of three external independent experts and up to two EIT Health subject matter experts.

Following the evaluation criteria (see paragraph 5.2), each panel member will score proposals based on the submitted application, the pitch, and the answers provided during the question and answers section of the pitch session.

Each application will receive a single score and feedback on the application from each panel member. Final scores for each application will be out of 100 and are calculated by taking the mean of the reviewers’ scores.

Applicants are expected to ensure their availability for the pitching sessions and to accept the pitching date and time assigned if invited to a pitching session. EIT Health will not be able to rearrange pitching slots according to the availability of applicants.

3. Ethical Legal Social Issues Review:

Independent experts will evaluate each project suggested for funding on the Ethical, Legal, and Social Issues (ELSI) to ensure that all elements in the proposal linked to critical ethical, legal and social considerations are well defined and addressed, thereby helping to de-risk the EIT Health portfolio.

4. Final Selection notification:

Following the online pitching sessions and ELSI review, applications will be ranked from highest scoring to lowest scoring based on the scores given by the external evaluators.

EIT Health management makes the final funding decision based on expert recommendations, evaluation scores, and available funding. Only applicants with an evaluation score of at least 70/100 will be considered for funding. All applicants will be notified of the final outcome and receive feedback from each expert in accordance with the timetable in paragraph 4.1 above.

The top-ranked applications will be selected for funding and invited to the contracting stage (paragraph 3.6). If an applicant does not pass through contracting, the next applicant in the ranking list might be contacted, as long as they have scored at least 70 / 100 in the final score.

call_title: EFCSN Permanent Call for Protection Grants
description: EFCSN Permanent Call for Protection Grants

beneficiaryAdministration:
Fact-checkers are frequently the targets of attacks and harassment as they speak truth to power. The fact-checking community has been repeatedly harassed: individual fact-checkers and organisations have faced threats, vandalised offices, SLAPPs, and coordinated online hate campaigns designed to censor or cancel their work.

In response, the consortium comprised of the European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN), together with its members Faktograf, Pagella Politica, Fact Review, FactCheck Cyprus, and Greece Fact Check, has initiated a protection scheme with the support of the European Union.

The primary aim of this scheme is to provide direct, rapid support to fact-checkers in need (e.g. due to online harassment campaigns, hacking attempts, vandalisation of office spaces, threats of physical violence, physical attacks, threats of imprisonment or lawsuits, SLAPPs). Those facing harassment or requiring assistance for their psychological, physical, online or legal safety may submit requests for support under this call. All submissions will be handled with the utmost security and processed as quickly as possible to provide aid to those affected.

Support and Eligible Activities

Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following:

  1. Psychological Support: counselling, burnout prevention, and specialised training. Please note that costs for general staff wellbeing not linked to a specific incident or harassment situation are not eligible.
  2. Legal Aid: defence against defamation, harassment, cyber and physical violence, SLAPP suits, copyright disputes, etc. Please note that legal costs related to commercial disputes, employment matters, or issues unrelated to fact-checking activities are not eligible.
  3. Safe Workspace: this may include installation of security systems, purchase or rental of security equipment, rental of a secure workspace, or costs to enable staff to work remotely during a period of risk. For fact-checkers, the workspace is understood as the reporting assignment itself and the physical space immediately surrounding it.
  4. Emergency Relocation: transport, temporary housing, crisis coordination for teams in danger, etc.
  5. Cybersecurity: upgrades for encryption, security tools, and risk assessments, etc. Please note that general IT infrastructure upgrades not linked to a specific security threat or incident are not eligible.

Eligibility Criteria

To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements:

  1. Legal entity: applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit.
  2. Certification: applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations or fact-checking organisations that can demonstrate they respect in practice the European Code of Standards for Independent Fact-Checking Organisations.
  3. Location: organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (see this document for the most up-to-date list).
  4. Single applicants: this call is intended for single applicants, i.e. consortia of organisations cannot apply for this call.

Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration

  1. Total Call Budget: €340,169
  2. Maximum Grant Amount: €20,000 per support request; in exceptional cases (e.g. relocation of a large team), grants can be up to €40,000. Such requests must be reasoned in detail and must be approved by the EFCSN Governance Body in addition to the standard selection procedure outlined below.
  3. Funding Rate: 50%
  4. Form of Grant: lump sums
  5. Number of Grants: ~17
  6. Payment Structure: 75% upon approval of request, 25% following the approval of the final report.
  7. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table.
  8. List of eligible costs:
  9. Direct costs must be directly related to the implementation of the requested support and fall under one of the following categories (although the examples below are not exhaustive):
  10. A. Psychological Support: costs related to mental health, wellbeing support, physical checkups related to long-lasting stress, including counselling sessions, burnout prevention activities, and specialised trauma training provided by qualified professionals.
  11. B. Legal Aid: costs related to legal support services, including legal counsel or lawyer fees, court or filing fees, legal document translation, notary services, and other directly related legal expenses.
  12. C. Physical Safety: costs related to ensuring the physical safety of staff or premises, including security system installation, security equipment purchase or rental, secure workspace rental, remote work setup costs, and related services.
  13. D. Emergency Relocation: costs related to urgent relocation and crisis response, including transport, temporary accommodation, crisis coordination services, subsistence costs during relocation, and related support.
  14. E. Cybersecurity: costs related to digital security and protection, including security software or tool licences, cybersecurity audits or risk assessments, secure hardware (e.g. encrypted devices), implementation and setup costs, and related services.
  15. Retroactive costs: if a grant is approved, costs are eligible from the time of application submission.
  16. Indirect / Administrative costs: these are capped at 10% of total direct costs.
  17. Max. Grant Duration: 12 months
  18. Rolling basis: this call is open on a rolling basis from 2 September 2026 until 31 May 2028 (or until funds are depleted).

Selection Procedure

The evaluation will be conducted in two steps:

Phase 1: AI Processing. The application platform will automatically review submitted applications to ensure that all required information has been provided and that applicants meet the basic eligibility criteria.

Phase 2: Expert Evaluation. Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, urgency, regional vulnerability, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. Consortium experts may request additional advice from a multidisciplinary group of experts, comprising the Protection Scheme Advisory Board, and escalate particularly delicate decisions to the EFCSN Governance Body. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below.

The evaluation is conducted in several steps, depending on the amount and urgency of the request, as shown in the image linked here.

The main criteria for evaluating the requests are:

Category

Description

Max. points

Need

Clear evidence of an acute operational or financial gap directly tied to the emergency situation. Financial statements and other documents may be requested as evidence.

10

Urgency

Time-sensitive circumstances where delayed support would meaningfully worsen the outcome.

10

Regional Vulnerability

Context of operating environment: political, economic, or press freedom constraints that amplify risk.

10

Absorptive Capacity

Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner.

10

How to Apply and Timeline

To apply, please submit your request through the application platform. Requests for urgent support will be processed within 48 hours; other requests will be processed within 5 working days.

Reporting

An outcome report (financial and narrative) is expected from all grant recipients.

Transparency Notice

This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on efcsn.com/funding-opportunities. Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration.

NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle.

Questions?

Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com.
