beneficiaryAdministration:
Submission and evaluation procedures are detailed in the Call Announcement available on the Water4All Partnership website.

Submission Procedures

A two-step application procedure will apply equally for the Joint Transnational Call (JTC) and its modalities (the Regular and the Early Career Researcher (ECR)). Pre-proposals and full proposals must be submitted electronically via a specifically designed web platform, the Electronic Proposal Submission System, using the templates provided and in line with the Guidelines for Proposal Submission.

Applicants should note that the online system may experience high traffic volumes in the last hours before the submission deadline and it is therefore highly recommended to submit the final version of the pre / full-proposal well in advance of the deadline to avoid any last-minute technical problems. Requests for extensions of the deadline due to last minute technical problems will not be considered.

Evaluation Procedures

A two-step evaluation procedure will apply, for the pre-proposals (step 1) and the full proposals (step 2) respectively. The evaluation procedure will be common for all proposals submitted under the JTC and Early Career Researcher (ECR) modality. The Call Secretariat (CS) will check that no Conflict of Interest exists concerning the proposals evaluated.

All proposals, either submitted under the Regular or the ECR modality, will be evaluated by the same Evaluation Panel (EP) and in accordance with the same evaluation criteria defined in chapter 5 of the Call Announcement, and ranked in the same ranking list.

An independent observer will be invited as external observer to the EP meetings to assess the conformity of the general procedure with the EU regulation.


Step 1 (Pre-proposal stage)

Pre-proposals submitted correctly and within the deadline will be checked for eligibility by the Call Secretariat against criteria defined in chapter 4 of the Call Announcement and by the Funding Partner Organisations (FPOs) according to their national/regional criteria.

All eligible pre-proposals should be subject to a scientific evaluation by three EP members, as far as possible, based on two criteria - ‘Excellence’ and ‘Impact’. One of the evaluators will act as the rapporteur during the EP meeting.

During the EP meeting, the evaluation results of each pre-proposal will be presented by the rapporteur. The EP will discuss the pre-proposals and agree on the final scores for each criterion. All applicants will receive a consensus report from the EP.

A ranking list of pre-proposals will be produced, including only those pre-proposals that meet the minimum threshold, i.e., 3 out of 5 in each criterion. The final score will be agreed by the EP for each criterion, and afterwards, the two criteria will be summed up to produce the final score.

The objective of this first step is to identify the best proposals to proceed to Step 2 and to ensure balance between requested and available funds at the national/regional level. The ranked eligible pre-proposals will be sent to the Call Steering Committee (CSC) and divided in 3 groups, according to their scores: Group A (highest evaluation scores), Group B (medium evaluation scores) and Group C (low evaluation scores). All pre-proposals in Group A, will be invited to Step 2. Among the pre-proposals in Group B, proposals will be selected to Step 2, taking into account the ranking list, the representativeness of all FPOs, the participation in the ECR modality and the funding ratio limits. Pre-proposals in Group C will be dismissed for their low classification.

Consortium Coordinators will be informed of the outcomes by the CS and, if appropriate, invited to submit a full proposal.


Step 2 (Full proposal stage)

After the submission deadline for full proposals, the submitted full proposals will be checked to ensure that they meet the formal call criteria and have not changed substantially from the respective pre-proposals. Full proposals not meeting the formal conditions will be rejected without further review.

As in Step 1, each full proposal will be reviewed by three members of the EP based on three criteria - ‘Excellence’, ‘Impact’ and ‘Quality and Efficiency of Implementation’. The EP members will assess the full proposals in advance of the EP meeting and prepare individual evaluation reports. In case of a missing expertise in the EP for some full proposals, the CS will identify and mobilize external experts to obtain three individual evaluation reports.

The evaluation results for each full proposal will then be presented by the rapporteur during an EP meeting and discussed by the EP members. The EP meeting will complete the evaluation procedure by agreeing on the final individual score for each criterion, and the overall score for each proposal. Due to the large number of proposals evaluated, the EP could decide to focus on those proposals that report divergent scores from the evaluators. Any proposal where there is a consensus between the evaluators on any of the three criteria being below the threshold (i.e., 3 out of 5 in each criterion) may not be discussed and ranked by the EP (regardless if there is divergence or not in other scores). The overall threshold on the final score is 10/15: no project with a lower score will be funded.

The decisions of the EP should be taken collectively, preferably by consensus or by simple majority of the panel members, in case consensus cannot be reached. The rapporteur will produce a common consensus report on behalf of the EP for each full proposal, which will be transmitted to the applicants.

Final ranking list(s) of proposals (either per modality (JTC or ECR) and/or per topics) will be produced based on the final scores, following the same methodology as in Step 1. The final ranking list(s) will be forwarded to the CSC, which will meet to decide on the projects to be recommended for funding by FPOs. For this decision, the CSC will strictly follow the order of the ranking list(s) from the EP until the available funding is exhausted.

The applicants will be informed about the final outcome of the call.

call_title: ForestPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures
description: The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector. Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic. TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change” This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts. Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration. TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions” This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands. Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services. TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products” This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing. Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake. TOPIC 4 – Forest Value Chains, Markets and Governance: “How forest-based sectors, markets and governance are organised” This topic supports research and innovation strengthening the resilience, sustainability, and functioning of forest-based value chains, markets, and governance systems, supporting the transition towards a sustainable and circular forest-based bioeconomy. It aims to support resilient, sustainable, competitive, and innovative forest-based value chains and governance systems capable of responding to environmental, economic, and societal transitions. Proposals should address, where relevant, forest-based value chains and market organisation; innovative business models, economic viability and investment readiness; policy, regulatory and governance instruments; barriers to market uptake and innovation deployment; cascading use, circularity and efficient resource use; skills, labour, education and workforce development; and European resilience in sustainable raw material supply, value chains, local processing capacities and forest-based economies. The topics provide strategic direction and facilitate evaluation. They are not exhaustive and do not restrict the submission of innovative or cross-cutting proposals aligned with the overall objectives of the call.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The Joint Call follows a two-stage application and evaluation procedure.


Pre-proposals must be submitted electronically through the FOREST Electronic Submission and Evaluation System (ESES). They will undergo a formal eligibility check by the Call Office, national/regional eligibility checks by the relevant Research Funding Organisations, and scientific evaluation by an independent International Expert Panel.


Following the first-stage evaluation, selected consortia will be invited to submit full proposals. Full proposals will undergo a further formal and national/regional eligibility check and independent scientific evaluation by the International Expert Panel.


Final recommendations for funding will be made by the Call Steering Committee on the basis of the scientific evaluation, ranking lists and available national/regional and EU funding.


Applicants must also comply with the applicable national/regional requirements set out in the Funder Regulations.

description: Expected Innovation Experiments Applicants will propose an innovation experiment that improves an existing product, service or application using Space-IoT Box resources. The proposed experiment must: Address a relevant climate-smart agriculture challenge. Use Copernicus, Earth Observation, IoT or other Space-IoT Box-supported resources. Demonstrate how the existing product, service or application will be improved. Present a clear implementation plan, expected outputs and budget. Show potential value for users, customers or stakeholders in the Lake Victoria Basin region or the wider target countries. Example Application Areas Applicants may propose innovation experiments linked to areas such as: Weather and climate monitoring using IoT sensors and remote sensing data. Water quality monitoring for fish farming. Fish farming decision-support services. Crop monitoring and crop phenology. Farm input planning, irrigation support and farm management. Crop disease risk monitoring and alerts. Seasonal planning and agroclimatic zoning. Precision agriculture using satellite imagery and IoT data. Hydrological flow assessment using IoT observations and satellite image analysis. These are example areas. Applicants may propose other relevant climate-smart agriculture solutions that can benefit from Space-IoT Box resources. What Selected Applicants Will Receive Selected SMEs and start-ups will receive: Access to Space-IoT Box resources, tools, datasets and documentation. Technical training on relevant Copernicus, Earth Observation and IoT resources. Business development and entrepreneurial support. Product and market validation support. Pitch and investment readiness support. Mentoring during the innovation experiment implementation period. Opportunity to present the innovation experiment during the final showcase. Financial support of up to EUR 5,000 for eligible costs linked to the approved innovation experiment.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The KijaniSpace Space-IoT Innovation Program will support selected SMEs and start-ups to improve existing agriculture-related products, services or applications using Copernicus and IoT resources. The program will support up to five selected SMEs or start-ups from Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. Selected teams will carry out innovation experiments using Copernicus, Earth Observation and IoT resources made available through the "Space-IoT Box". The Innovation Program will include onboarding, online training, mentoring, innovation experiment implementation, product and market validation, pitch preparation and an in-person final showcase in Kenya.

Who Can Apply

The open call is targeted at SMEs and start-ups that are legally established and operating in one of the following countries:

  1. Kenya
  2. Uganda
  3. Tanzania

Applicants may apply as a single organisation. Only one proposal will be accepted for funding per applicant or team member. Applicants must have an existing agriculture-related product, service or application linked to crop farming, fish farming or another relevant climate-smart agriculture use case.

Application Requirements

Applicants need to complete an online application form available at:

https://www.kijanispace.eu/space-iot-innovation-programme/

The proposals are submitted in PDF format using the provided proposal template. The proposal package will also include a declaration of honour and ethics self-assessment where required.

Financial Support

Each selected SME or start-up may receive financial support of up to EUR 5,000. The financial support will cover eligible actual costs incurred during the implementation of the approved innovation experiment. Costs must be directly linked to the approved activities, milestones and expected deliverables. The payment arrangement will include:

  1. One pre-financing payment of 20% of the approved project budget.
  2. One final payment covering the remaining approved eligible costs after approval of the final report and corresponding deliverables.

Selected beneficiaries will submit a financial statement at the end of the funded experiment for assessment by the KijaniSpace project coordinator.

Eligible Use of Funds

Financial support may be used for activities directly linked to the approved innovation experiment, including:

  1. Testing and improving the selected product, service or application using Space-IoT Box resources.
  2. Implementing new features or services based on Copernicus and IoT technologies.
  3. Collecting data, user feedback or stakeholder validation linked to the experiment.
  4. Preparing technical documentation, validation evidence and impact summaries.
  5. Participating in KijaniSpace virtual meetings, hackathons, showcase activities or related dissemination events.
  6. Communication and dissemination activities linked to the funded experiment.

Funding must be used only for the approved innovation experiment and in line with the sub-grant agreement.

Evaluation and Selection Process

Applications will first be checked for completeness and eligibility. Eligible applications will then be evaluated by three evaluators using the published evaluation criteria. The evaluation will use the following main criteria:

  1. Excellence: Quality of the proposal, understanding of the open call, relevance of selected Copernicus services and Space-IoT Box tools and suitability for the selected region.
  2. Impact: Expected contribution to KijaniSpace project objectives, relevance to climate-smart agriculture, expected value for users or stakeholders and potential for dissemination, communication and exploitation.
  3. Implementation: Feasibility of the proposed activities, quality of the implementation plan, team capacity, budget realism, expected deliverables and ability to complete the experiment within the program period.

The evaluation process will produce a ranked list of proposals based on the scores received. In case of tied scores, a consensus meeting will be held to select the proposals for funding. Selected applicants will be contacted after the evaluation. Unsuccessful applicants will also be informed of the evaluation outcome.

  1. Excellence: Quality of the proposal, understanding of the open call, relevance of selected Copernicus services and Space-IoT Box tools and suitability for the selected region.
  2. Impact: Expected contribution to KijaniSpace project objectives, relevance to climate-smart agriculture, expected value for users or stakeholders and potential for dissemination, communication and exploitation.
  3. Implementation: Feasibility of the proposed activities, quality of the implementation plan, team capacity, budget realism, expected deliverables and ability to complete the experiment within the program period.

The evaluation process will produce a ranked list of proposals based on the scores received. In case of tied scores, a consensus meeting will be held to select the proposals for funding. Selected applicants will be contacted after the evaluation. Unsuccessful applicants will also be informed of the evaluation outcome.
furtherInformation:
Obligations of Selected Beneficiaries

Selected SMEs and start-ups will:

  1. Sign a dedicated Sub-Grant Agreement with the KijaniSpace project coordinator.
  2. Use the financial support only for the approved innovation experiment.
  3. Participate in onboarding, training, mentoring, review meetings and final showcase activities.
  4. Submit progress updates during the program.
  5. Keep records of actual costs incurred.
  6. Submit a final report, financial statement and supporting evidence.
  7. Provide documentation of technical outputs, validation feedback, expected impacts and lessons learned.
  8. Support project communication and dissemination through approved non-confidential materials.

If funds are misused or costs are found to be ineligible, the beneficiary will repay the affected amount to the KijaniSpace project coordinator in line with the financial support conditions.

Intellectual Property, Confidentiality and Data Protection

Applicants will identify any pre-existing products, services, data, tools, software, know-how or materials they bring into the program. The applicant guidelines and sub-grant agreement will define the rules on intellectual property, data protection, confidentiality and liability. Public communication materials will use approved non-confidential information, summaries, photos, screenshots, presentations or demonstration materials provided by the selected beneficiaries.

Who can take part?

Regions: Bavaria (DE), Norte Region (PT), Castile and León (ES), Romania (RO) and Tuzla (BiH) only.

Consortia: 2–8 partners from at least 2–5 regions (depending on project size).

Type: Triple Helix (academia, business, public authorities).

Project sizes & budget

Flagship: up to €2.2 million (5–8 partners, all regions). Proposed by consortia composed by 5 to 8 partners covering all 5 participating SYSTEMEU regions and including at least one RTO/University, one company, and one public sector entity actively involved in public service delivery (e.g., municipal administrations or hospitals).

Medium: up to €1.1 million (3–5 partners, at least 3 regions). Proposed by consortia composed by 3 to 5 partners established in a minimum of 3 different eligible regions, and including, at least, one for-profit company as core partner.

Small: up to €750k (2–3 partners, at least 2 regions). Proposed by consortia composed by 2 to 3 partners established in a minimum of 2 different eligible regions and including, at least, one for-profit company (Startup or SME) from an eligible region as a core partner.

Note: Maximum funding of €600k per partner across all calls.

Funding rates

Start-ups: 100% (exception: Castile-León: 70%).

SMEs: 70 per cent.

Large enterprises: 50 per cent.

Public sector/NGOs/research: 100 per cent.

Evaluation phases (schematic)

  1. Eligibility check: Formal review.
  2. Expert evaluation: Assessment based on excellence, impact and implementation (by three independent experts).
  3. Ethics check: Review of compliance with the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), medical ethics, etc.

Final selection will be formalized by FEB validation (Final Evaluation Board) & ranking. There will be a 14-day appeal period in the event of rejection.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Submission procedures:

A two-stage procedure will apply to this Joint Transnational Call; at stage 1 the submission of pre-proposals is mandatory, and at stage 2, applicants must submit full proposals upon invitation. (Pre-)proposals must be submitted electronically using the Electronic Proposal Submission System (EPSS): https://proposals.etag.ee/sustainable-blue/2026.

The online system may experience high traffic volumes in the last hours before the submission deadline and it is therefore highly recommended to submit the final version of the pre / full proposal well in advance of the deadline to avoid any last-minute technical problems.

Requests for extensions of the deadline due to last-minute technical problems will not be considered. Any proposals not correctly submitted at this moment will be declared ineligible.

Evaluation procedures:

Detailed procedures are available in the call text.

A two-step evaluation procedure will apply: pre-proposal stage (Step 1) and full proposal stage (Step 2).

Pre-proposal stage (Step 1)

The eligible pre-proposals will be evaluated by a minimum of two independent evaluators of the IEC, and as far as possible, by three independent evaluators of the IEC who will be assigned by matching expert profiles with the need for pre-proposals evaluation, on two criteria:

-Excellence (Threshold: 3/5)

-Impact (Threshold: 3/5)

This Step 1 aims to identify the best proposals to proceed to step 2 and to ensure a balance between requested and available funds at the national level.

The ranked eligible pre-proposals will be sent to the CSC and be divided into 3 groups, according to their scores: Group A (highest evaluation scores), Group B (medium evaluation scores), and Group C (under the threshold scores). All pre-proposals in Group A will be invited to Step 2. Among the pre-proposals in Group B, proposals will be selected for step 2, considering the ranking list, the representativeness of all PFOs, and the funding ratio limits. Group C will be dismissed for their low ranking and unavailability of funding.

Full proposal stage (Step 2)

All eligible full proposals will be subject to a scientific evaluation by at least three independent reviewers of the IEC who will be assigned by matching expert’s profiles with the need for full proposals evaluation. One of the IEC members will be nominated as a rapporteur.

The evaluation of each full proposal will be based on the following criteria:

-Excellence (Threshold: 3/5)

-Impact (Threshold: 3/5)

-Quality and efficiency of implementation (Threshold: 3/5)

During the IEC meeting, the evaluators will present the evaluation results of each proposal. The IEC will discuss full proposals and agree on the final scores for each criterion.

The final ranking lists (one ranking list per priority area, four in total) will be forwarded to the CSC, which will meet to decide on the projects to be recommended for funding by PFOs.

furtherInformation:
Scope

The 2026 Joint Transnational Co-funded Call is the fourth under the Sustainable Blue Economy Partnership. It mobilises funding from 33 organisations across 28 countries plus EU contributions, aiming to foster a climate-neutral, sustainable, and innovative blue economy in Europe by supporting research, innovation, and collaboration across marine and maritime sectors. The call contributes to the European Green Deal, Digital Europe, the Ocean Pact, the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, the Marine Spatial Planning Directive, the 2030 Climate Target Plan and the Zero Pollution vision for 2050, as well as the EU Strategies on Coastal Communities and Islands, and the UN Decade of Ocean Science. Proposals must address one main priority area and foster cross-basin collaboration to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of the EU Blue Economy.

Priorities Areas

The fourth Joint Co-funded Call encompasses all the five Partnership Intervention Areas converted for this call into four priority areas as follows:

Priority area 1: Transitioning the blue economy sectors for sustainability and strategic autonomy

Priority area 2: Managing sea-uses by advancing digital and ecosystem-based approaches

Priority area 3: Promoting sustainable blue bioresources through innovation in production and harvesting

Priority area 4: Building resilience in coastal communities with infrastructure and businesses

Each of these areas contributes directly to one or more of the Ocean Decade Challenges, supporting actionable knowledge generation, policy uptake, capacity development, and inclusive innovation in the blue economy context.

Geographical coverage

The proposals are strongly recommended to consider a minimum of two EU sea basins which are: the Atlantic Ocean, Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Mediterranean Sea, and North Sea, and to assess the project proposal’s impact and potential replication/scalability on various sea basins. Proposals can target European regional seas such as Adriatic Sea, Aegean Sea, the Arctic, Barents Sea, Celtic Sea, etc. but they must be from a minimum of 2 different EU Sea basins.

FOR MORE INFORMATION:

The call is published on the Partnership website at https://www.bluepartnership.eu/funding-opportunity/sustainable-blue-economy-partnerships-fourth-joint-transnational-call.

Interested applicants must carefully read the relevant national regulations in Annex with the Call text. Each applicant to the call must ensure that its contribution to the overall project conforms to these regulations.​

description: Basic information AENAON implements two competitive Open Call rounds through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme. The Open Calls aim to maximise the uptake, integration, testing and validation of AENAON technologies and services, including the Federated Digital Twin-based Cyber Range Platform, cybersecurity training capabilities and cybersecurity preparedness services, in realistic offshore wind and related critical-infrastructure environments. The Open Calls are designed to engage SMEs and start-ups, large enterprises and technology providers, research organisations and universities, cybersecurity service and technology providers, offshore wind operators, manufacturers and supply-chain actors, energy and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, and other relevant innovation actors. Supported third-party projects are expected to contribute practical use cases, validation evidence, technical feedback and sector-relevant results that strengthen the cybersecurity and resilience of the offshore wind ecosystem. Open Call 1 focuses on the initial validation, integration and testing of AENAON technologies and services in realistic environments. Activities may include the development and validation of sector-specific cybersecurity scenarios, identification and assessment of offshore-wind-relevant vulnerabilities, integration with simulation and cyber range environments, cybersecurity testing and training activities, and validation of cybersecurity tools, services and preparedness capabilities. Open Call 1 sub-projects are expected to have an implementation period of 8 months, with clearly defined tasks, milestones, deliverables, KPIs and acceptance evidence. Applicants may propose activities related to cybersecurity testing and validation, cyber range training and scenario-based exercises, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat and risk assessment, risk monitoring, cyberattack management, digital twin-based validation and integration, or other cybersecurity resilience use cases that are demonstrably aligned with the objectives and technical capabilities of AENAON. Budget The total AENAON FSTP budget is €4,100,000. The indicative allocation is: €2,100,000 for Open Call 1 €2,000,000 for Open Call 2 Any amount not committed under Open Call 1 may be reallocated to Open Call 2, subject to budget availability, the applicable Open Call rules and the principles of transparency, equal treatment and sound financial management. Funding Constraints AENAON will provide sub-grants under two Open Calls (Open Call 1 and 2), with a total FSTP allocation of €4,100,000. In line with the call topic, the scheme derogates from the €60k ceiling, allowing up to €100,000 per individual third party (only in the case of offshore wind farm operators and manufacturers, which are considered large critical infrastructures/ operators of essential services) and up to €150,000 per action (in case of small consortia). Example 1 — SME A, Open Call 1 Entity A is a generic SME, applicable ceiling: €60,000 Funding requested/awarded in Open Call 1: €55,000 Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2 under AENAON: €5,000, if applicable) Example 2 — Offshore wind-farm operator B, Open Call 1 Entity B is an offshore wind-farm operator and therefore benefits from the derogated ceiling; applicable ceiling: €100,000 Funding awarded in Open Call 1: €87,000 Result: Eligible (Remaining funding capacity for Open Call 2: €13,000, if applicable) Example 3 — Small consortium B + C, Open Call 2 In Open Call 2, B and C form a small consortium. B = offshore wind-farm operator/manufacturer, and C = SME, thus, maximum funding per consortium action: €150,000. However, the individual ceilings must also be respected. Since B already received €87,000 in Open Call 1, B can receive only €100,000 − €87,000 = €13,000 C has received no previous AENAON funding. Therefore, C can receive up to €60,000 The total maximum eligible AENAON funding for the consortium (B+C) in Open Call 2 is therefore €73,000 (B up to €13,000, C up to €60,000) Consortium action (budget requested): €73k < €150k maximum per action The final lump-sum amount awarded to each selected third-party beneficiary will be fixed at the contracting stage through a needs-based, auditable right-sizing process, taking into account the proposed activities, technical complexity, budget needs, expected contribution to AENAON objectives, evaluation outcome, milestones, deliverables, and acceptance criteria. Payment Schedule AENAON applies a staged payment model of 30% – 40% – 30%: 30% initial payment upon signature of the Sub-Grant Agreement and completion of onboarding requirements 40% interim payment following successful completion of the mid-term review and acceptance of required interim reports, deliverables and supporting evidence 30% final payment following completion of the action and acceptance of the final report, final deliverables, performance evidence and required outputs Payments are conditional upon the satisfactory achievement of agreed milestones, deliverables and acceptance criteria. Payments may be suspended, reduced or recovered in cases of non-performance, breach of contractual obligations, false declarations, conflict of interest, ineligible activities or serious non-compliance with reporting, ethics, GDPR, visibility or audit requirements.

beneficiaryAdministration:
About NACHIP

The NACHIP is an I3 project financed under the Interregional Innovation Investments call I3-2023-INV2a, which aims to accelerate innovation related to the North Adriatic Hydrogen Ecosystem (NAHV), with a focus on investments in hydrogen technologies. The goal is to strengthen the integration of hydrogen technologies into the ecosystem, boosting sustainability and enhancing the development of the hydrogen market. This project targets three main value chains (manufacturing, urban areas, and mobility) through five pilot actions:

1.Green hydrogen production from wave energy – Pag, Croatia

This pilot explores the production of green hydrogen with a novel technology that captures wave energy through a system of underwater devices installed beneath the sea surface. The pilot will also feature the application of multifunctional breakwater technology, being deployed for the first time in Europe.

2.Hydrogen use in urban Areas – Velenje, Slovenia

This pilot aims to establish a system for decentralized supply of energy from onsite renewables to be developed, operated and validated on a public building. The pilot focuses on integrating clean technologies through sector coupling (electricity, heat and hydrogen), supporting the transformation of the district heating system as coal is phased out (Just Transition).. Supporting activities will include the formation of a “local hydrogen alliance” pursuing the efficient utilization of renewable hydrogen within an environmentally sustainable and economically viable model.

3.Dynamic Hydrogen Releasers – Torviscosa, Italy

This pilot develops and demonstrates Dynamic Hydrogen Releasers (DHR), based on Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier (LOHC) technology. This innovation supports safe and efficient transport, storage, and on-demand release of hydrogen, contributing to Europe’s green mobility and industrial decarbonisation strategies. Throughout the development phase, this pilot needs to define the technical requirements and dimensions of the DHR units.

4.Cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders – Udine, Italy

This pilot develops composite designs for cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders. The focus is on improving vessel designs to enhance the mobility of energy storage, reducing costs while ensuring the safe and efficient transport of compressed hydrogen.

5.Gasification plant for waste materials – Zagreb, Croatia

This pilot focuses on developing a prototype gasification plant for waste materials. The universal gasification system is designed to process municipal solid waste (MSW) and convert it into valuable products such as synthesis gas (syngas) and charred residue (ash), which can be further used.

Objectives financial support to third parties (FSTP) in NACHIP

Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP), also referred to as cascade funding, is a mechanism of the European Commission designed to distribute public funding to either increase uptake of innovations on the side of recipients such as Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) or to support project implementation in addressing specific challenges and advancements towards key objectives.

Under NACHIP, FSTP enables targeted support to companies proposing hydrogen-based solutions at a TRL>7, connected to pilot projects that can be validated and deployed in real life settings. The mechanism ensures fast access to funding, reduced administrative burden and a competitive, transparent selection process.

The FSTP reinforces NACHIP demonstration activities through the following specific objectives:

  1. enabling market adoption of hydrogen-related technologies, products and services developed within Nachip’s pilots, combining different Key Enabling Technologies;
  2. fostering new technological solutions driven by SMEs.

More in particular, the FSTP under the NACHIP project will:

1.enable testing, validation and demonstration of hydrogen technologies in real-life environments through NACHIP pilot sites (specific to the NACHIP);

2.support TRL advancement of innovative solutions toward market readiness[1];

3.accelerate commercial deployment and exploitation of hydrogen innovations, including cross-border business opportunities;

4.address technical bottlenecks and integration challenges in the hydrogen value chain, completing the value chains of the companies belonging to the NACHIP consortium;

5.strengthen safety, standardization and regulatory compliance of hydrogen technologies;

6.promote cross-sectoral replication and interoperability to enable wider adoption across industries;

7.contribute to the investment portfolio and key performance indicators (KPIs) of the project.

Applicants can submit proposal through the NACHIP website https://www.nachip.eu

All applications must be filled and submitted in English language.

The evaluation is conducted by 3 experts. For evaluation process and criteri will be described in https://www.nachip.eu/open-calls/

For more information or assistance with the application process, participants can contact the NACHIP project directly:

nachip@meta-group.com

Questions to the above-mentioned email address can be submitted until 9th of October 2026.

call_title: Open Call for Cutting-Edge Defence Solutions
description: The BattleVerse 1st Open Call aims to support the development and validation of innovative technological solutions that contribute to advanced mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence related environments. Selected applicants will implement a six-month experiment, developing and demonstrating their proposed solution and assessing its potential contribution to the BattleVerse ecosystem. Proposals shall address one of the following three technical topics: Topic 1: LLMs for strategic decision-making, symbolic reasoning, game theory and planning under uncertainty. Experiments under this topic will explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI-based approaches to support strategic decision-making and mission planning, including symbolic reasoning, game-theoretic modelling, planning under uncertainty and human-in-the-loop approaches. Topic 2: Multi-physics simulation capabilities for multi-domain defence environments. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate simulation approaches capable of modelling complex operational environments and interactions across multiple warfare domains. Topic 3: Distributed AI for autonomous systems (UxVs) with for coordinated swarm operations. Experiments selected under this topic should explore and demonstrate how autonomous systems powered by machine learning and distributed AI can support coordinated multi-UxV operations in complex operational environments. Across the three topics, proposed experiments should demonstrate a clear technological contribution, a credible implementation approach and the potential to advance the capabilities of the BattleVerse simulation environment. Experiments are expected to achieve at least TRL 5 by the end of the six-month implementation period. Selected beneficiaries will also have access to targeted coaching and guidance activities provided by the BattleVerse consortium. These activities will support applicants in addressing relevant technical challenges related to the development, integration, testing and validation of their solutions. The selected beneficiaries will remain fully responsible for the implementation and delivery of their experiments.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The BattleVerse project, a European Defence Fund Development Action co-funded under grant agreement No 101224034, foresees the provision of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP), also referred to as Cascade Funding, to support innovative experiments contributing to the objectives of the project.

The BattleVerse 1st Open Call is designed to support innovative experiments contributing to the development and validation of advanced technologies for mission planning, simulation, training and execution in defence-related environments. The Open Call primarily targets SMEs, including start-ups, and will provide selected beneficiaries with financial support to implement experiments over a period of six months.

The Open Call covers three technical topics designed to advance next-generation defence simulation capabilities. Applicants are invited to propose innovative solutions in AI-enabled decision support (including Machine Learning, LLMs, strategic decision-making and human-in-the-loop AI), advanced modelling and simulation (including MSaaS, Digital Twins and multi-domain simulation environments), or autonomous defence systems (including unmanned vehicles, distributed AI and swarm operations).

Proposal applications must be submitted exclusively via the BattleVerse Submission Portal.

Experiments may be implemented by a single SME or start-up, or by an eligible consortium of up to three beneficiaries. Participation of entities other than SMEs, including RTOs and academic institutions, may only be accepted where no suitable SME is available to provide the specific capacity or expertise required for the successful implementation of the experiment, and such participation must be duly justified in the proposal.

The proposal must be written in English in all mandatory parts to be eligible. The project description shall not exceed 15 pages as indicated in the Proposal Template. Only a proposal included in the Proposal Template will be reviewed by Evaluators. The evaluation will be performed per topics. Applications submitted by email, post, or any means other than the one described above will not be considered.

The assessment of the Call will follow transparent evaluation criteria, lump-sum funding modalities, and strict governance procedures in full compliance with the corresponding EDF's Model Grant Agreement.

The eligibility criteria applicable to the BattleVerse 1st Open Call reflect the relevant requirements of the European Defence Fund and the specific conditions established for Financial Support to Third Parties. To be eligible, applicants must:

  1. Be a legal private entity qualifying as Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise as defined by the European Commission. Entities other than SMEs may participate only in duly justified cases where the specific capacity or expertise required for the experiment cannot be provided by an available eligible SME.
  2. Applicants must be legal entities established in any of the countries eligible for this open call: A EU27 Member State or Norway or Ukraine. This follows country eligibility criteria under the EDF as well as the Commission Implementing Decision of 29 January 2025 (C(2025) 568 final
  3. EDF-funded activities are subject to specific ownership and control requirements in accordance with Article 9 EDF Regulation. To be eligible for this Call, entities must be established in an EU Member State, Norway or Ukraine. Applicants controlled by an entity from a non-eligible country will be excluded.
  4. Applicants must comply with all eligibility criteria defined in this Guide for Applicants, including requirements related to geographical scope, ownership control, security requirements, conflict of interest and data protection. These conditions are aligned with the applicable rules of the European Defence Fund, tailored to the reality of financial support to third parties.
  5. Applicants must have the know-how, qualifications and resources to successfully implement the projects and contribute their share (including sufficient experience in projects of comparable size and nature).
  6. Applicants to this Call must submit the Ownership Control Declaration.
  7. Comply with ethics requirements as defined in Article 7 of EDF Regulation.
  8. Comply with security requirements of the Call.
  9. Comply with financial capacity requirements of the Call.
  10. Comply with any other specificity of the Call.
  11. Not have any conflict of interest with BattleVerse consortium partners.

description: The EIT Regional Innovation Booster (EIT RIB) Hungary seven-month international market-access programme for Hungarian start-ups. With the support of the Hungarian National Innovation Agency, it supports mature, innovation-driven Hungarian companies to validate, enter and grow in a new European market. A single cohort of 8 companies will be selected and equipped with a validated market entry strategy, concrete connections in their target market, and the operational know-how to act on them. At the heart of the programme is a Buddy system that pairs each company with an experienced operator who already knows the chosen target market and sector. This is complemented by expert mentoring, a programme of workshops and guest speaker sessions, and a EUR 2.500 conference and travel grant to support in-person engagement in the target market. The programme runs from December 2026 to June 2027 and is structured in two consecutive phases. Phase 1: Market Preparation (Months 1–3) Selected companies validate their target market with 20 hours of 1:1 expert mentoring, assess their readiness for international expansion, and build an executable market entry strategy. Phase 2: Market Expansion (Months 4–7) Each company works up to 40 hours with its matched EIT RIB Buddy to start entering the chosen target market, supported by continued workshops and guest speakers, international matchmaking, and optional participation in EIT Community events. To be eligible, applicants must: -Be a for-profit SME (according to the EU definition) registered in Hungary -Have at least 3 full-time employees (FTEs) at the time of application -Hold full ownership of, or exclusive commercialisation rights to, the intellectual property behind the solution to be taken abroad -Have a novel product, service, technology or deep tech solution with demonstrated product-market fit in Hungary and proven commercial traction -Operate in one of the EIT thematic areas: Climate, Digital, Food & Agritech, Healthcare, Energy and Renewables, Raw Materials, Urban Mobility, or Culture & Creativity.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Proposals should be submitted through the official EIT Urban Mobility Programmes Portal (NetSuite), accessed here.

Further instructions for the submission of proposals are found in the EIT Regional Innovation Booster Hungary 2027 Call Manual, Section 7.2.

Proposals will first be checked for admissibility and eligibility, Call Manual Section 5. Proposals found admissible and eligible will be evaluated against the award criteria by an Evaluation Panel, consisting of two external expert evaluators and one internal expert evaluator from the KICs participating in this Call. See section 6.2 of the Call Manual. The external expert evaluators will produce a Summary Evaluation Report for each proposal assessed.

A ranking list will be created to select 8 Hungarian start-ups taking part in the EIT Regional Innovation Booster Hungary 2027 Programme, each of them equal and over 18 points out of 30. If the number of eligible, high-quality proposals exceeds the available places, a reserve list will be established.

description: 1. Purpose of the call The call is published as part of the implementation of the European RISTANC project, which is financed by the Horizon Europe programme. The project contributes to the implementation of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean and Waters by 2030”, with a focus on the Slovenian marine area, which is prt of the cross-border North Adriatic region. 2. Key challenges The call encourages projects that contribute to addressing the following thematic areas: The establishment and management of moorings in the Slovenian sea for recreational and tourist vessels that prevent damage to marine seabed habitats, The planning and implementation of interventions in the coastal zone of the Slovenian sea that harmonise the various needs and interests of people and the environment, Other measures in the Slovenian sea area (and potentially beyond) that contribute to the objectives of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, such as reducing pollution in the marine environment (including plastic and other waste), the conservation and restoration of marine ecosystems, and the development of a sustainable blue economy. 3. Eligible activities Activities eligible under the call are those that contribute to the objectives of the RISTANC project and the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, and address one or more of the challenges listed inthe call. The following types of activities, in particular, are eligible: Experimental activities (projects implementing innovative approaches in support of the Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, i.e. for the cleaning, protection, or restoration of the marine environment, or for the establishment of a zero-emission, circular, and sustainable blue economy). Prototype development (activities focused on developing prototypes to solve specific challenges related to marine ecosystems). Feasibility studies and scoping (assessing the feasibility of larger-scale measures). Research and innovation (initiatives to research new methods or technologies that contribute to reducing pollution and to the protection or restoration of biodiversity, including improvements to regulatory frameworks and governance structures). Artistic, cultural and community activities (initiatives and programmes that use art and culture to engage local communities in pollution prevention, nature protection and restoration, and awareness campaigns on ocean health and related human well-being). Educational activities and capacity-building initiatives (education, training and workshops for stakeholders, children, young people and adults, including professionals, to strengthen knowledge, competencies and skills in sustainable practices related to reducing pollution, the conservation or restoration of biodiversity, and the sustainable blue economy). Monitoring and citizen science activities (activities to assess the effectiveness and impacts of implemented solutions on marine ecosystems, citizen science activities). Knowledge brokering and transfer (activities that translate existing research results into actionable evidence for policy-making or practice, such as synthesis reports, policy recommendations, stakeholder dialogues, living labs, etc.; also includes institutions as focal points for transdisciplinary research and innovation activities with European reach). A combination of the above activities. Proposed projects must contribute to the development of sustainable and inclusive solutions for challenges facing the marine environment in the North Adriatic area. 4. Duration The project shall commence on the date the funding agreement is signed (no earlier than 1.1.2027) and may last for a minimum of 6 and a maximum of 12 months. Regardless of the project duration, it must be completed by 28 February 2028 at the latest.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Eligible applicants

The call is open to a wide range of applicants, including innovators, researchers, artists, individuals, representatives of civil society, non-governmental organisations, local communities, informal and local initiatives, start-up companies, schools, research teams and other individuals and organisations whose projects contribute to achieving the objectives of the call. The following entities are eligible to apply for the call:

  1. public and private legal entities (e.g. non-governmental organisations, associations, institutes, commercial companies, local communities, research organisations, educational institutions, social enterprises and other legal entities),
  2. natural persons.

Additional conditions:

  1. If the applicant applies as a (public or private) legal entity, the registered office or business address of the applicant must be located in a Member State of the European Union, its overseas countries or territories (OCTs), or in a country associated with the Horizon Europe programme. If the applicant applies as a natural person, they must hold a permanent residence address within the European Union Member States.
  2. Applications may be submitted individually or in partnership. If the applicant includes partners in the project implementation, they remain the project lead and responsible for the project implementation, including financial responsibility for its execution.
  3. Each (public or private) legal or natural person may participate in only one application under this call, either as an applicant or as a partner. In the event that the same applicant submits or participates in multiple applications, only the first application submitted will be considered, and the remaining applications will not be processed.
  4. The proposed project must address one or more of the challenges set out in the call, and the planned activities must be implemented in the Slovenian territorial sea, including the coast,or contribute to addressing challenges in this area.
  5. The selected applicant must have settled all outstanding tax liabilities and, where relevant, social security contributions before signing the funding agreement. The contracting authority will verify compliance with this condition prior to the signing of the contract. If the verification reveals that the condition has not been met, the contract shall not be concluded; the project may be rejected and financial support awarded to the next highest-ranked project.
  6. Consortium partners of the RISTANC project are not eligible to apply for this call, either as (public or private) legal entities or as natural persons.
  7. Informal or local initiatives may apply through a natural person acting as the applicant, who shall be responsible for the project implementation.
  8. The project or activities for which financial support is claimed under this call must not be funded by other European, national, or local public sources. The applicant shall provide a declaration to this effect in the application documentation.
  9. Applicants who are personally, professionally, economically, or otherwise linked to the RISTANC consortium partners must disclose their connections.

The valid Slovenian Maritime Spatial Plan is used to define the geographical scope of this call.

2. How to apply

The application for funding, together with all required attachments in PDF format, shall be submitted by email to the address ristanc-funding@zrs-kp.si. In the email subject line, please state: RISTANC – application for the call [name of applicant]. The application may be submitted in Slovenian or English.

The application submission deadline is from 28 September 2026 to 28 November 2026 until 23:59 (CET).

An application shall be considered timely if the email is sent by the deadline specified in the call. The application must include a completed and signed application form, including the required annexes as defined in the application form.

An information seminar will be organised for all (potential) applicants, which will take place on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, on the Zoom online platform. Applicants may send questions regarding the call to the email address ristanc-funding@zrs-kp.si no later than 31 October 2026. Answers to questions will be published on the project RISTANC website and will form an integral part of the tender documentation.

3. Selection procedure and project evaluation

The opening of Applications is not public. Following the expiry of the application submission deadline, the expert commission shall first verify the timeliness and formal completeness of the Applications received. If the commission finds that an Application is formally incomplete (e.g. unclear administrative data in Sections A and B; this does not apply to Section C), it may request the applicant to supplement it. Supplementing the Application is intended to rectify formal deficiencies and must not affect the project content, the requested amount of financial support, or its evaluation. The deadline for supplementation is five (5) working days from receipt of the call, which the commission shall send only once. If the applicant fails to supplement the Application within the prescribed period or if the supplementation is inadequate, the Application shall be rejected.

Only complete applications shall be admitted to the evaluation process. An application shall be considered complete if: it contains all required application forms, evidence, declarations, and annexes specified in this call for applications; it was submitted within the prescribed deadline and in the manner specified in the call; all mandatory information in the application forms has been completed; it is signed by the applicant's legal representative (or an authorised person) if the applicant is applying as a (public or private) legal entity; it is signed by a natural person if the applicant is applying as a natural person. Applications that do not meet all the above conditions will be considered incomplete.

Projects are evaluated by a five-member expert commission on the basis of pre-determined and published criteria. The applicant will receive the Evaluation criteria together with the application form. A priority list of projects is established on the basis of the scores achieved.

Before the evaluation starts, the expert commission adopts a formal decision on the prevention and management of conflicts of interest. Each commission member signs a declaration of confidentiality and absence of conflict of interest. A member with an actual or perceived conflict of interest with an applicant or its partners does not assess, discuss or rank the application concerned; such cases are recorded in the evaluation minutes.

To be eligible for funding, a project must achieve at least 55 points in the evaluation.

Where two or more applications obtain the same total score, priority is given to the application with the higher score under criterion 1 and, if still equal, under criterion 4.

The highest-rated applicants will be invited to a short oral presentation of the project idea, which is expected to take place on 10 December 2026, either in person or remotely. The purpose of the oral presentation is to provide a brief overview of the project idea and an opportunity for further clarification before the final project selection decision is made. No new content may be introduced and the requested amount may not be increased. The final scores are confirmed solely on the basis of the published evaluation criteria, and the final priority list is recorded in the evaluation minutes.

In the event that no submitted project reaches the minimum funding threshold or is selected for financing, the call organiser reserves the right to repeat and adapt the call.

4.Evaluation criteria

Applications are evaluated against the following award criteria (maximum score): 1. Consistency of the proposed project with the challenges set out in Call, clarity and appropriateness of the main project objective, and appropriateness of the approach for monitoring its achievement (20); 2. Quality and feasibility of the implementation plan and timeline (20); 3. Degree of innovation and originality of the proposed project idea (10); 4. Expected impact of the project, including the impact on target groups (20); 5. Sustainability plan for results (10); 6. Competencies and experience of the applicant in relation to the submitted project and the content of the call (10); 7. Cost-effectiveness of the budget (10). Total: 100 points.

5. Notification of results and funding agreement

Applicants will be notified of the results of the call by 15 December 2026 at the latest. The results of the call, including a description of the selected projects, award dates, project durations and the legal names and countries of the recipients, will be published on the RISTANC website and on the F&T portal.

The selected applicant shall be deemed not to accept the funding if, within 10 days of receipt of the selection notification, they fail to provide written confirmation of acceptance of the funds (written confirmation via the email address provided in the application form is also valid). In the event of withdrawal by the selected applicant, funding may be approved for the next applicant on the priority list.

6. Legal protection

No appeal or objection is admissible against the substantive decision, assessment, and evaluation of projects by the expert commission. An applicant may lodge an objection solely in the event of suspected procedural errors (breach of the public call procedure). An objection shall be lodged with the call organiser within 8 days of receipt of the notification of the outcome of the call. The head of the procedure shall decide on the objection within 15 days of its receipt. If the objection is upheld and a procedural error is identified, the challenged decision on selection or non-selection shall be set aside, and the applicant's application shall be returned to the expert commission for reconsideration and a new decision. The commission must rectify the identified error in the reopened procedure.

furtherInformation:
1. Call organiser and responsibility

The call is organised by the Science and Research Centre Koper (ZRS Koper), coordinator of the RISTANC project, on behalf of the RISTANC consortium. The consortium remains fully responsible towards the European Commission for the proper implementation of this financial support scheme and for compliance with Grant Agreement No. 101217089. Recipients of financial support under this call are third parties: they are not beneficiaries of the EU Grant Agreement and have no contractual relationship with the European Commission. Their rights and obligations are set out exclusively in the funding agreement concluded with ZRS Koper.

2. Amount of financial support

A total of EUR 60,000.00 is available for the implementation of this call.An individual project may receive financial support in the amount of EUR 7,500.00 to EUR 12,000.00. This maximum is below the EUR 60,000 threshold for financial support to third parties and, for projects implemented in partnership, applies to the project as a whole.

Funding is awarded at up to 100% of the project’s total costs, but must not exceed the maximum amount allowed per individual project as specified in this call.

It is anticipated that approximately 5 to 8 projects will be funded, depending on the amount of funding approved for individual projects.

Funding of projects within this call is implemented as lump sum funding – a lump sum is a flat-rate contribution towards the implementation of the project,paid out on the basis of results achieved or activities carried out, and not on the basis of proof of actual costs incurred.


3. Method for determining the amount

The amount of financial support is determined based on the estimated project budget submitted by the applicant in the application form, within the limits of available funds and the maximum allowed amount of financial support per individual project.

If the applicant meets all the conditions of the call and the project is eligible for funding based on the evaluation, financial support shall be set at the amount of funds requested by the applicant in the application form, up to a maximum of EUR 12,000.00. The expert commission may reduce this amount where individual items of the financial plan are clearly excessive or not necessary for the planned activities; the final amount is fixed as a lump sum in the funding agreement.

The lump sum covers costs that are directly linked to the implementation of the approved project and are necessary to achieve its objectives. Costs categories include: personnel costs (staff) for persons directly involved in the implementation of project activities (for the project duration, up to a maximum of 12 months), costs of materials and equipment strictly necessary for the implementation of project activities, service costs required for the implementation of the project (e.g. external contractors, expert reports, analyses, development services), costs of implementing activities such as pilot actions, experimental activities, workshops, training, field activities and similar, dissemination and communication costs related to public information, stakeholder engagement and the promotion of project results, indirect costs at a flat rate of 25% of personnel and purchase costs (A + C), as set out in the financial plan of the application form.

Projects shall be funded in the order of their ranking on the priority list, established on the basis of the evaluation, until the available funds have been exhausted. In the event that the available funds are insufficient for the funding of the last eligible project in full, partial funding or an amount lower than that requested may be approved, even if this is lower than the minimum specified amount of financial support.


4. Payments and reporting

The funds are paid out in three instalments: 20 % as an advance payment upon signing the funding agreement; 30 % following the approval of interim results and/or achieved milestones, as specified in the agreement; 50 % following the approval of final results, including the final project report and all required supporting documentation.

Recipients are required to submit substantive reports on project implementation and other evidence specified in the agreement within the deadlines specified in the funding agreement.

As the funding is implemented as lump sum funding, Recipients do not report actual costs using accounting documents, but instead report on the activities carried out, results achieved and the fulfilment of contractual obligations. At the request of the call for applications issuer, they must be able to demonstrate the implementation of activities and the achievement of results.

Mandatory reports include:

  1. an interim report covering a description of the activities carried out and milestones achieved;
  2. a final report including a description of the overall project implementation, the results achieved and the impact of the project;
  3. evidence of the activities carried out, such as reports, materials, photographs, documentation of workshops, prototypes or other project results.

5. Obligations of recipients

Projects participate in a research process guided by the RISTANC project Ethical Protocol, approved by the Scientific Council of ZRS Koper. Applicants commit to:

  1. adhering to ethical principles when planning project activities,
  2. indirect participation in the research process, subject to prior and informed consent.

Both aspects are covered in the Ethical Aspects document. A breach of ethical principles or failure to participate in the research process may result in the termination of funding.

Recipients are required to appropriately acknowledge funding under the RISTANC project and the Horizon Europe programme in all communication and dissemination activities related to the project. All materials produced as part of the project must contain: The RISTANC project logo, The 'Funded by the European Union' logo, and Disclaimer.

6. About the RISTANC project and the Mission

The call is published as part of the implementation of the European RISTANC project, co-financed by the Horizon Europe programme. The project contributes to the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean and Waters by 2030”, with a focus on the Slovenian marine area, part of the cross-border North Adriatic region. The Mission has three main objectives: 1) protect and restore marine and freshwater ecosystems and biodiversity; 2) prevent and eliminate pollution of our ocean, seas and waters; 3) establish a carbon-neutral and circular blue economy in the EU. More information: https://missionoceanwaters.eu/

RISTANC strives to achieve the goals of the Mission in the Slovenian sea, with an emphasis on social innovation. It develops solutions to specific local challenges through broad cooperation between stakeholders and aims to demonstrate the value of transdisciplinary collaboration, including by showcasing successful small projects. More information: https://www.ristanc.eu/

The call is specifically intended to encourage the participation of individuals, organisations and communities that have not previously participated, or have participated less frequently, in European research and innovation projects. Particular attention is paid to less common forms of activity, new interdisciplinary partnerships, the involvement of local communities and innovative solutions.

7. Call documents and contact

Full call documentation is available on the RISTANC website (section “Documentation and application forms”): https://www.ristanc.eu/en/news/call-for-small-project-funding-ristanc

Contact: ristanc-funding@zrs-kp.si

description: Együttható (Civil-Business)

beneficiaryAdministration:
Grants, knowledge sharing, networking – Aspektus+ is a complex four-year capacity building programme for rural NGOs in Hungary. The sub-program “Együttható” is for formal, independent, non-profit civil society organizations, established and operating in the 4 core regions of Aspect Group (South Trans-Danubia, South Plains, North Plains, North Hungary). The aim of this program is to motivate CSOs to cooperate with the private sector.

This program helps to find a common language between the two sectors and to engage for-profit organizations to act for social change on the community level. This means fostering active citizenship, stand up for inclusion, ensure represantation of marginalised groups, promoting equality and engaging in solving current challenges from environment protection to the access to services. Beside that, the cooperation will also help CSOs to reach their goals and to become more sustainable. The 16 supported projects set a good example, showing that it is possible to cooperate with the private sector in the countryside. We both support new cooperations and also organizations who have experience in working with companies.

The form of the grant is a lump sum. This amount cannot be less than EUR 3 000 or more than EUR 5 250.

“Együttható” is a multistage call. The first stage is about the formal eligibility of the applicant and the concept. The second stage is about the professional evaluation with 6 award criteria with maximum 5 points each. The awarded projects have to be over 20 points. The professional evaluation will be made by the joint Aspektus committee with 2 members from each organisation. Each concept note and full application will be read by 2 members (one from the region and one from outside). Once the committee has made its decision, the applicants are notified about the results. Applications must be submitted in Hungarian.
