beneficiaryAdministration:
1. About UPRAISE

UPRAISE – Virtual Worlds Innovation Masters: Shaping Future Digital Skills Europe is implemented under the Digital Europe Programme and coordinated by the University of Bologna. The project aims to strengthen advanced digital skills in Europe through innovative and interdisciplinary education and training related to Virtual Worlds and their applications in different economic and societal domains. Within UPRAISE, the University of Napoli Federico II contributes to the Public Administration application area, focusing on the organizational, managerial and institutional implications of digital transformation and emerging digital technologies in the public sector.

2. Purpose of the Call

The University of Napoli Federico II launches this Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) call within Task T5.2 – “Mobility, mentorship and (non-)financial support for students” of the UPRAISE project. The call aims to facilitate access to advanced education and training opportunities connected with UPRAISE and to reduce financial and socio-economic barriers to participation.

For Cycle 1, UNINA proposes to award financial support in the form of Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waivers to eligible students admitted to the educational pathway described in Section 3.

3. Educational pathway covered by the Call

For Cycle 1, the UNINA UPRAISE educational pathway will be developed in connection with the following postgraduate programmes offered by the Department of Economics, Management, Institutions (DEMI) for academic year 2025/2026:

-Master in Public Managerial Practice (Master in Pratica Manageriale Pubblica); -Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration (Master in Trasformazione Digitale della Pubblica Amministrazione).

FSTP beneficiaries will also be required to participate in a dedicated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module in the Public Administration area, entitled: “Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Worlds for Public Administration”.

The UPRAISE specialised learning activity will consist of 24 hours of online learning and will complement the educational activities of the relevant Master programme. It will focus on the application and organisational implications of advanced digital technologies in Public Administration, with particular reference to: Artificial Intelligence and data-driven public services; Virtual Worlds, immersive technologies and digital twins; organizational and managerial implications of emerging technologies; innovation in public services.

The activity is intended to enable participants to understand and critically assess the opportunities, organisational implications and governance challenges associated with the adoption of these technologies in the public sector, and to apply the knowledge acquired to relevant Public Administration contexts.

Completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity requires attendance of at least 70% of the scheduled activities and a positive final assessment. Participants who successfully complete the activity will receive a UPRAISE Certificate of Completion. For cycle 1 this activity does not award ECTS credits.

Participation in and successful completion of the UPRAISE specialised learning activity are mandatory conditions for FSTP beneficiaries and for maintaining the financial support awarded under this Call.

4. Financial support available

For Cycle 1, the UNINA allocation is:

• maximum number of beneficiaries: 4;

•      maximum FSTP support per beneficiary: EUR 5,000;

•      maximum total Cycle 1 allocation: EUR 20,000.

The support will take the form of a full or partial Tuition and Enrolment Fee Waiver. The maximum amount of support will depend on the tuition fee applicable to the selected programme: Master in Public Managerial Practice: tuition fee EUR 4,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 4,000; Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration: tuition fee EUR 10,000; maximum FSTP support EUR 5,000. In all cases, the amount awarded shall comply with the prohibition of double funding.

5. Eligible applicants

Applicants must:

·       meet the academic entry requirements of the relevant programme;

·       be formally admitted to or enrolled in the programmes identified in Section 3;

·       undertake the associated UPRAISE specialized learning activity/self-standing module;

·       satisfy the nationality/country eligibility conditions applicable under the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and Digital Europe Programme;

·       comply with the applicable administrative requirements of the University of Napoli Federico II;

·       not receive other EU financial support covering the same tuition/enrolment costs;

·       provide the documents and declarations required under this call.

Admission to the Master programme and selection for FSTP financial support are separate procedures. Admission to the Master does not automatically entitle an applicant to FSTP support.

6. Inclusion, widening participation and financial need

In accordance with the UPRAISE objectives and FSTP framework, the selection and determination of financial support shall take account, through transparent criteria, of financial need, socio-economic circumstances, geographical/widening considerations, diversity and inclusion, as applicable. Applicants may voluntarily provide information relevant to these criteria, including socio-economic circumstances, disability or other conditions relevant to widening participation. Such information will be processed in accordance with applicable data protection rules. The specific scoring mechanism is set out in Section 11. 

7. Language requirements

Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme and associated UPRAISE learning activities, in accordance with the requirements established by UNINA. Where applicable, some UPRAISE activities, learning materials, seminars or international sessions may be delivered in English. 

8. Application procedure

Applications shall be submitted electronically through the procedure specified by UNINA. The call shall remain open for at least two months. The published call will specify the opening and closing dates, submission platform and contacts for administrative and technical enquiries. Applications submitted after the deadline or through channels other than those indicated in the call will not be considered.

9. Required documents

In line with the FSTP Guidelines, applicants should provide, as a minimum:

1.     Transcript of Records or equivalent academic documentation;

2.     Curriculum Vitae, maximum 3 pages, without photograph, including academic history, relevant professional experience, skills and achievements;

3.     Personal Statement/Motivation Letter, maximum 3 pages, addressing motivation for participation, relevance to UPRAISE and the proposed educational pathway, and expected academic/professional impact;

4.     copy of a valid passport or identity document;

5.     any additional documents required by UNINA to verify eligibility.

Applicants may be required to provide a declaration concerning other financial support and compliance with the applicable double-funding rules. Where relevant to the published financial-need, widening or inclusion criteria, applicants may voluntarily provide the information and supporting documentation expressly identified in the final call. UNINA will not request sensitive personal data beyond what is necessary and legally permissible for the implementation of the published criteria.

10. Eligibility check

Following the deadline, UNINA will conduct an eligibility check. Only applications satisfying the eligibility requirements, submitted on time and accompanied by the mandatory documentation will proceed to evaluation.

11. Evaluation and selection criteria

Eligible applications will be evaluated by a Selection Committee appointed by UNINA on the basis of clear, objective and transparent criteria, in accordance with Section 5.3 of the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. Applications will be assessed on a maximum score of 100 points according to the following criteria

Criterion

Description

Weight

Academic background

Academic and Professional Background – academic records, previous qualifications, relevant professional experience and achievements, and overall preparedness for the proposed advanced digital skills learning pathway.

65 points

Motivation and proposed activity

Motivation and Expected Contribution – motivation to participate in the programme, interest in the thematic areas addressed by UPRAISE, expected contribution to the applicant’s professional and/or academic development, and potential contribution to the broader objectives and impact of the project

25 points

Curriculum Vitae

Additional Academic and Non-Academic Experience – additional relevant academic, professional and non-academic experience, skills and achievements documented in the Curriculum Vitae.

10 points



100 points

In accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines, the quality and relevance of the proposed participation in relation to the applicant’s educational and professional objectives will be considered within the above assessment criteria. Applicants must demonstrate an adequate level of proficiency in the language of instruction of the selected programme, in accordance with the requirements specified by UNINA. Diversity, equity, inclusion and widening participation considerations will be taken into account in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines. In the case of equal or comparable evaluation results, preference may be given to applicants from underrepresented groups, subject to applicable legal and institutional rules.

Applicants achieving an overall score of at least 70/100 may be considered for funding, subject to compliance with all eligibility requirements and availability of financial resources.

12. Selection committee

The Selection Committee will be appointed in accordance with UNINA rules. Its members shall act independently and impartially and comply with applicable confidentiality and conflict-of-interest requirements. The Committee will assess eligible applications against the published criteria, assign scores and establish the ranking.

13. Ranking, reserve list and award decision

Financial support will be awarded, subject to availability of funds, to the highest-ranked eligible applicants meeting the minimum threshold. A maximum of four beneficiaries will be funded under this Cycle 1 call. Eligible applicants above the threshold but not funded may be placed on a reserve list in ranking order. Where fewer than four applicants satisfy the eligibility and quality requirements, fewer than four applicants may be awarded financial support under this Call. If a selected applicant withdraws, declines the award, fails to accept it within the prescribed deadline or loses eligibility, UNINA may offer the support to the next eligible applicant on the reserve list.

14. Communication and acceptance of results

Applicants will be informed of the outcome of the selection procedure in accordance with the FSTP Guidelines. Successful applicants will receive information concerning the financial support awarded and the procedures for its acceptance. Applicants placed on the reserve list and applicants whose applications are declared ineligible or unsuccessful will be informed in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines.

15. Conditions for maintaining the support

Beneficiaries must maintain eligibility and participation in the relevant educational pathway, successfully complete the associated UPRAISE specialised learning activity in accordance with the attendance and assessment requirements set out in Section 3, comply with applicable academic and administrative requirements, provide information required for project monitoring and promptly communicate changes affecting eligibility or funding. Beneficiaries shall comply with the participation and reporting obligations established by the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and by the relevant UNINA educational programme.

16. Fee waiver and administrative arrangements

The FSTP support under this Call is intended to cover tuition/enrolment fees through a full or partial fee waiver. No part of the financial support, including any difference between the applicable tuition/enrolment fee waiver and the maximum FSTP support of EUR 5,000 per beneficiary, will be paid directly to beneficiaries or provided in another form. The maximum support is EUR 4,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Public Managerial Practice and EUR 5,000 for beneficiaries enrolled in the Master in Digital Transformation of Public Administration. The amount of the benefit will be individually recorded. The administrative and accounting mechanism will comply with UNINA procedures and the UPRAISE Grant Agreement.

17. Double funding

Financial support awarded under this Call shall comply with the applicable rules on double funding, in accordance with the UPRAISE Grant Agreement and FSTP Guidelines.

18. Monitoring, records and audits

UNINA will retain the documentation required to ensure an adequate audit trail for publication, applications, eligibility checks, evaluation, selection, award and implementation. 

19. Redress procedure

A redress procedure will be provided in accordance with the UPRAISE FSTP Guidelines and the applicable UNINA procedures.

20. Data protection 

Personal data submitted in connection with this Call will be processed in accordance with the applicable data protection legislation and the relevant University of Napoli Federico II privacy notice.

21. Publication and visibility

Following the required review and confirmation procedure, the call will be published simultaneously through the channels required by the UPRAISE/HaDEA implementation arrangements, including the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform (DSJP), the UPRAISE project website and the institutional website of the University of Napoli Federico II. The call will remain open for at least two months. The English version will be the reference version; an Italian version may also be made available.

22. Disclaimer

This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE. Any financial support awarded under this call will be granted directly by UPRAISE to the successful applicants, in its own name and under its sole responsibility. UPRAISE's own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of UPRAISE.

description: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV

beneficiaryAdministration:
The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach.

All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas.

3 NATIONAL CALLS 

Three national calls will support CSOs in Italy, Greece and Spain focusing on: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV. 

TARGET APPLICANTS 

The calls target small and medium-sized grassroots CSOs, particularly those operating in rural, peripherical or marginalised areas and legally registered in Italy, Greece or Spain. The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations. 

2 FUNDING WORKSTREAMS: 

1. Enhanced protection response for women, girls and children, victims of GBV, adopting an intersectional approach. This area focusses on providing tailored protection and support services, including safe houses, medical and psychological assistance for women and girls, in all their diversity, who are victims of domestic, sexual violence and other forms of GBV considering specific barriers for equal access to protection (Budget: 540,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 

2. Reduction of harmful practices, with a focus on improving interventions against harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, intersex genital mutilation, forced abortion, forced sterilisation, child and forced marriage, and honour-related violence, forced medicalisation of transgender women. Funded projects will aim at both 9 preventing and responding to these practices, with a particular focus on raising awareness, strengthening legal frameworks, and providing education to communities at risk (Budget: 360,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 

CALL TIMELINE  

First Round: 

  1. Opening: 24/08/2026 (11/09/2026 in Greece) 
  2. Deadline: 23/11/2026 at 15.00 CET 

Second Round: 

  1. Opening: 01/12/2026 
  2. Deadline: 01/03/2027 at 15.00 CET 

 

AVAILABLE GRANT PER COUNTRY: 

First Round - 6 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 

  1. Stream 1: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 
  2. Stream 2: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 25,000; one grant of EUR 5,000 

Second Round - 4 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 

  1. Stream 1: one grant of EUR 30,000; one grant of EUR 30,000; 
  2. Stream 2: one grant of EUR 20,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 

APPLICATION PROCESS:  

  1. Administrative check 
  2. Eligibility requirements verification and shortlisting 
  3. Final assessment and selection 
  4. Pre-notification and Due diligence 
  5. Confirmation and signing the agreement 
  6. Information session are foreseen online and in present in each country. 

For more information please visit: https://copower.oxfam.it/ 

Contact: infocopower@oxfam.it

Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.

The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. description: The two calls will be structured through two distinct funding strands. An SME may submit a maximum of one application per strand, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Consequently, an SME may submit one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, provided that the proposed activities are distinct and no double funding occurs. Strand A (Challenge-driven) follows a two-step process linked to predefined industrial challenges. In Step 1, up to three SMEs per challenge receive €10,000 (with minimum 20% private co-funding) to develop and validate a proof of concept (TRL 6-7). After evaluation and a final pitch, one SME per challenge advances to Step 2 and receives €50,000 (with minimum 40% co-funding) to further develop and scale the solution (TRL 8–9). Strand B (Open Call) follows a single-stage selection process. SMEs apply bottom-up and can request up to €10,000, €30,000, or €60,000 depending on project maturity, with increasing private co-funding requirements. Projects run up to six months. The RENEW-BOOSTER project aims at driving innovation and industrialization in three critical sectors that are vital for Europe’s green transition and energy security: Photovoltaics (PV), Offshore Wind Energy, and the associated Energy Networks. At the core of RENEW-BOOSTER is the Accelerator, providing tailored support for SMEs to identify opportunities and develop solutions, strengthening their role in the renewable energy value chain and enhancing resilience.

The project aligns with Europe’s strategic priorities, including reducing critical raw material dependency (Critical Raw Materials Act), advancing climate goals (Green Deal), and supporting re-industrialization (Net Zero Industry Act). RENEW-BOOSTER aims to empower SMEs and accelerate Europe’s twin green and digital transitions.

We reserve the right not to award all available funds or to redistribute them between the different calls, depending on the proposals received and the results of the evaluation.

For answers to frequently asked questions, please visit our FAQ.

call_title: Cyber Security Boost: Support for the development, pilot testing and wider adoption of solutions for cyber resilience.
description: The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas: The call is focused on three main thematic pillars: • Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages. • Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management. • Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting. Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.

beneficiaryAdministration:
The project proposal will be submitted by the applicant via the application form attached to this call for proposals. The proposal will include the mandatory annexes and any other annexes that the applicants decide to attach in order to demonstrate the eligibility, quality and applicability of the results, the suitability of the proposed mechanism for their application in the context of sustainability, or other parameters of the project.

For each project, a member of the NCC-CZ Council will be appointed by the NCC-CZ Council to manage the evaluation process, based on the submission and the sectoral focus of the project. As part of the evaluation, the NCC-CZ administrators will assess the formal compliance of the submitted project proposal with the requirements of the call and will carry out an assessment of the acceptability of the project in terms of the substantive requirements for projects. An independent evaluators will assess the quality and compliance with the material requirements of the projects in accordance with the Terms of Reference of the NCC-CZ and this call.

Further information available on: Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost - Výzvy

In accordance with the programme’s terms and conditions, the maximum amount of financial support is €100,000 and the minimum amount is €60,000 (in the form of a grant),depending on the current exchange rate of the Czech koruna. Projects will be funded at a rate of 50% of eligible costs, which means that the beneficiary will receive funding amounting to one half of the eligible costs incurred during the implementation of the project and substantiated in accordance with the established rules. Details regarding the frequency and format of reporting will be specified in the grant agreement. Applicants must ensure that the project proposal meets the conditions designed to prevent the project funding from resulting in unauthorised indirect state aid within the meaning of relevant European legislation, or from leading to double funding.

The following types of organisations are eligible to participate in this call and meet the criteria set out in the EU Digital Europe programme:

• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

• Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that demonstrate professional competence and the ability to produce and practically validate an output in line with the objectives of the call.

• Academic and research institutions are eligible only as members of a consortium that includes at least one small or medium-sized enterprise. They may not submit an application on their own.

Consortia may combine the above-mentioned entities. The application must specify the actual roles, responsibilities and budgets of the members; a formal partnership without evidence of added value is not sufficient.

Submission Application Documents

Necessary Application documents:

  1. Completed and signed UNIPAT UPRAISE Application Form.
  2. Curriculum Vitae, maximum 3 pages; no photograph required.
  3. Official Transcript of Records or equivalent academic record.
  4. Motivation Letter, maximum 3 pages, explaining academic background, expected learning outcomes, relevance to UPRAISE, and the proposed mobility activity.
  5. Copy of a valid passport or national identity card.
  6. Proof of current enrolment at some of the HEIs or companies of the Upraise consortium.
  7. Mobility or learning plan.
  8. Invitation, acceptance or confirmation from the University of Patras for the specific mobility stream.

Applications will be evaluated using the common UPRAISE model: 65 points academic background, 25 points motivation/proposed activity and 10 points CV. The recommended minimum quality threshold is 70/100, subject to the final approved call conditions.


Criteria Description

Criterion 2: Motivation and proposed activity: Quality, relevance, feasibility and expected contribution of the proposed mobility activity; motivation for advanced digital skills and UPRAISE themes. Weight: 25 points

Criterion 3: Curriculum Vitae: Additional academic, research, professional, practical, entrepreneurial or non-academic experience. Weight: 10 points

Total no of Grants

5 Grants will be approved. Financial support of 5.000,00 per grant. Eligible costs may include enrolment fees, travel, accommodation and living expenses during the approved mobility period. Double funding of the same cost is prohibited.

Inclusion and prioritisation

The prioritisation categories are applied only after eligibility and academic qualification have been established. They are not mutually exclusive and will support a balanced cohort while preserving merit-based selection. .

  1. Women and other genders underrepresented in ICT-related fields.
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds or experiencing significant financial hardship.
  3. Applicants with disabilities and applicants belonging to minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable groups.
  4. Applicants from countries or regions with lower advanced digital skills capacity.
  5. Applicants who belong to more than one priority category or who contribute to the overall balance of the selected cohort.

Information relating to priority categories is voluntary, confidential and processed only where necessary under applicable data protection rules. Applicants who wish to be considered under a priority category may provide only the minimum information needed to establish that category: optional gender self-identification; a brief statement of low socio-economic background or significant financial hardship, with income-related or financial-aid evidence where available and permitted under University procedures; a self-declaration that disability, minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable-group status applies, with non-diagnostic official confirmation only where strictly necessary; and country or region of residence, origin or prior study for geographical widening. Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules. If two or more applicants have the same final score, the Selection Committee may use the above factors, financial need and the overall cohort balance as tie-breakers and must document the rationale.

Award, payment and obligations

  1. All applicants will be informed of the outcome. Successful applicants must accept the award within the period stated in the notification.
  2. Before payment, selected applicants may be required to sign a grant agreement, learning agreement, declaration of honour, double-funding declaration and other University of Patras documents.
  3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.
  4. Withdrawal or cancellation must be communicated promptly in writing. Financial support already received may have to be reimbursed when the activity is not implemented or eligibility conditions are not fulfilled.
  5. The selected activity should be academically recognised through ECTS or another appropriate certification where applicable, according to the rules of the University of Patras .


Redress procedure

Applicants may request a review only in relation to an alleged procedural or administrative error affecting the evaluation. furtherInformation:
Eligible applicants

  1. Be formally enrolled at the University of Patras in a doctoral, postgraduate or undergraduate program appropriate to the selected mobility stream.
  2. Meet the academic and administrative requirements of the proposed host institution, program, summer/winter school, internship or learning activity.
  3. Have an academic profile and proposed activity aligned with UPRAISE themes, such as Virtual Worlds, XR, AI, digital twins, advanced digital innovation, or relevant applications in healthcare, education and creativity, and food.
  4. Have adequate command of English, normally at least B2 level, or the language required by the host activity.
  5. Hold the nationality of an EU Member State or another country eligible under the Digital Europe Program, in accordance with the applicable call rules.
  6. Be able to complete the proposed activity within the eligibility period established in the award documentation.


Eligible activities and costs

Financial support may cover only the cost categories specified below and directly related to the approved mobility activity:

  1. Enrolment or participation fees for an eligible program, module, summer/winter school or other approved learning activity.
  2. Travel and accommodation costs.
  3. Living expenses and subsistence during the approved mobility period, including local transport where permitted by institutional rules.

Double funding of the same expense is strictly prohibited. The grant may be combined with another compatible source, such as Erasmus+, only where the funding sources cover different eligible costs and all applicable institutional rules are respected.


Inclusion and prioritisation

The prioritisation categories are applied only after eligibility and academic qualification have been established. They are not mutually exclusive and will support a balanced cohort while preserving merit-based selection. .

  1. Women and other genders underrepresented in ICT-related fields.
  2. Applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds or experiencing significant financial hardship.
  3. Applicants with disabilities and applicants belonging to minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable groups.
  4. Applicants from countries or regions with lower advanced digital skills capacity.
  5. Applicants who belong to more than one priority category or who contribute to the overall balance of the selected cohort.

Information relating to priority categories is voluntary, confidential and processed only where necessary under applicable data protection rules. Applicants who wish to be considered under a priority category may provide only the minimum information needed to establish that category: optional gender self-identification; a brief statement of low socio-economic background or significant financial hardship, with income-related or financial-aid evidence where available and permitted under University procedures; a self-declaration that disability, minority, migrant, refugee or other vulnerable-group status applies, with non-diagnostic official confirmation only where strictly necessary; and country or region of residence, origin or prior study for geographical widening. Applicants may also indicate that more than one priority category applies. Applicants are not required to disclose medical diagnoses, detailed health information, ethnicity, religion or other sensitive details beyond what is necessary to establish the claimed category. Where official evidence is unavailable or requesting it would be inappropriate, self-declarations may be accepted in accordance with University procedures and applicable data protection rules.   3. Recipients must implement the approved activity, provide evidence of participation and eligible expenditure where requested, and cooperate with monitoring, reporting, audits and checks.
  4. Withdrawal or cancellation must be communicated promptly in writing. Financial support already received may have to be reimbursed when the activity is not implemented or eligibility conditions are not fulfilled.
  5. The selected activity should be academically recognised through ECTS or another appropriate certification where applicable, according to the rules of the University of Patras and the host institution.

description: Under the UPRAISE project (Virtual Worlds Innovation Masters, Digital Europe Programme, Grant Agreement No. 101225920), Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (URJC) offers Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) to its enrolled students for outgoing international learning and mobility activities within the UPRAISE consortium. Cycle 1 comprises three modalities (9 grants; total FSTP budget €15,000): C1.1 — PhD outgoing mobility: 2 grants of up to €2,500 each. C1.2 — Studies, internship or thesis (student outgoing): 2 grants of up to €2,500 each. C1.3 — Winter/Summer School & BIP (outgoing): 5 grants of up to €1,000 each. Each grant covers 50% of the total eligible cost of the activity (enrolment/registration fees, travel, accommodation, living expenses and travel insurance/medical coverage); the remaining 50% is co-financed by the student from own or other compatible, non-EU sources (no double funding). Selected students carry out an international mobility or learning activity aligned with UPRAISE themes (Virtual Worlds, XR, AI, digital twins, advanced digital innovation) and report on its completion. The support takes the form of a lump sum, paid 80% at the start of the activity and 20% after positive verification of the final justification.

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim of the grant.
  2. The UPRAISE project, co-funded by the European Union under the Digital Europe Programme, strengthens Europe's advanced digital skills capacity in innovation, entrepreneurship and Virtual Worlds technologies.
  3. Through its Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) scheme, Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (URJC) invites its students to apply for financial support for outgoing international learning and mobility activities within the UPRAISE consortium.
  4. The scheme promotes international academic collaboration, employability and inclusive participation in advanced digital education.
  5. Available funding. This Cycle 1 call offers three modalities (9 recipients; total FSTP budget €15,000):
  6. C1.1. PhD outgoing mobility: 2 recipients; up to €2,500 per recipient; FSTP budget €5,000.
  7. C1.2. Studies, internship or thesis (student outgoing): 2 recipients; up to €2,500 per recipient; FSTP budget €5,000.
  8. C1.3. Winter/Summer School & BIP (outgoing): 5 recipients; up to €1,000 per recipient; FSTP budget €5,000.
  9. Eligible activities and costs.
  10. Financial support may cover only costs directly related to the approved activity: enrolment or participation fees; travel and accommodation; living/subsistence during the activity; and travel insurance or international medical coverage.
  11. Durable equipment, expenses unrelated to the activity, and costs incurred before the grant award are not eligible.
  12. Financial support.
  13. The FSTP covers 50% of the total eligible cost of the activity (up to €2,500 per recipient in C1.1/C1.2; up to €1,000 in C1.3).
  14. The remaining 50% is co-financed by the student from own resources or other compatible, non-EU sources.
  15. Under no circumstances may the same costs be financed twice through EU funding (no double funding).
  16. The total eligible budget of Cycle 1 therefore amounts to €30,000 (€15,000 FSTP + €15,000 student co-financing).
  17. Payment mechanism
  18. The grant is paid in two instalments: 80% at the start of the activity and the remaining 20% after positive verification of the final justification.
  19. As the UPRAISE grant takes the form of a lump sum, justification is based on the completion of the activity (host certificate of participation/completion + brief final report); no itemised cost documentation is required.
  20. Failure to carry out the activity or to comply with reporting may lead to partial or full recovery of the grant.
  21. Eligibility criteria
  22. Academic status: be formally enrolled at URJC in a doctoral, master's or bachelor's programme eligible under UPRAISE, appropriate to the selected modality.
  23. Nationality: hold the nationality of an EU Member State or of a country eligible under the Digital Europe Programme.
  24. Thematic alignment: an academic profile and proposed activity aligned with UPRAISE themes (Virtual Worlds, XR, AI, digital twins, advanced digital innovation).
  25. Language: adequate command of the language of the activity (normally at least B2, or as required by the host).
  26. Double funding: the grant may be combined with Erasmus+ or other compatible support only where the sources cover different eligible costs.
  27. How to apply and required documents
  28. Applications must be submitted electronically, as the sole valid channel, through the online application form available on the project website (https://ciberimaginario.es/project/upraise-urjc/). Completing and submitting the form, with electronic confirmation of the declarations, constitutes the equivalent signature admitted by the Bases (Art. 9.4).
  29. Together with the form, applicants attach the following documents (PDF, in Spanish or English):
  30. valid national ID, NIE or passport;
  31. proof of current enrolment or admission at URJC (enrolment receipt / justificante de matrícula, admission document, or equivalent);
  32. academic transcript with subjects, ECTS credits, grades and grade-point average (first-year applicants with no URJC grades yet submit the transcript of the degree giving access);
  33. motivation letter (max. 1,000 words);
  34. CV (max. 3 pages);
  35. activity plan (Annex II);
  36. estimated budget (Annex III);
  37. responsible declaration of co-financing, commitments and honour (Annex IV, incl. no-double-funding);
  38. by modality, the modality-specific documentation of section 3 of the corresponding call (acceptance/learning agreement, or confirmation of admission to the school/BIP)
  39. Evaluation and selection criteria
  40. Applications passing the eligibility check are scored out of 100:
  41. Academic background. 65 points (weighted average grade, adjusted by the ratio of earned to expected ECTS).
  42. Motivation and expected contribution. 25 points (motivation letter; alignment with UPRAISE themes and expected contribution).
  43. Additional academic and non-academic experience. 10 points (CV).
  44. Minimum quality threshold: 70/100.
  45. In cases of equal merit (ex aequo), and solely as a tie-break that does not affect the equal treatment of applications, preference is given to promote diversity, in the following order: female applicants; applicants with a non-ICT background; applicants from low socio-economic backgrounds; applicants with a disability; applicants from low-DESI countries; applicants belonging to minority groups; the selection committee documents the rationale.
  46. Information on gender, age and socio-economic background is provided voluntarily and processed confidentially under the GDPR, solely for diversity monitoring and inclusive selection.
  47. Results notification
  48. A provisional resolution is published on the URJC project website (https://ciberimaginario.es/project/upraise-urjc/) with scores, reserve list, and non-selected/excluded), with individual notification by e-mail.
  49. After the appeals period, a final resolution is published on the same channels, stating the decision, the amount awarded and next steps.
  50. Redress procedure
  51. Interested parties may file an internal complaint to the URJC UPRAISE project team within one month of notification and, in any case, may resort to the competent courts.
  52. Mandatory legal notice and disclaimer
  53. This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by UPRAISE.
  54. The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by UPRAISE, in its own name and under its own responsibility.
  55. UPRAISE's own responsibility includes the preparation and drafting of this call as well as the selection of successful applicants that will receive the said financial support.
  56. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of UPRAISE.
  57. Information pursuant to the GDPR
  58. Data controller: Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (C/ Tulipán s/n, 28933 Móstoles, Spain).
  59. Data Protection Officer: protecciondedatos@urjc.es.
  60. Personal data are processed to manage the FSTP-UPRAISE-URJC programme (evaluation, resolution, payment, justification and reporting to the consortium and the European Commission), under Articles 6.1.a/b/c GDPR.
  61. Recipients: HaDEA, the European Commission, UPRAISE beneficiaries and host institutions where applicable. Retention: throughout implementation and five years after the final balance.
  62. Rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection may be exercised before URJC; complaints before the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es).
  63. Contacts
  64. URJC UPRAISE project team — info@ciberimaginario.es.
  65. Official website: https://ciberimaginario.es/project/upraise-urjc/ · https://upraiseproject.eu/

description: AI4CI - Fee waivers for Ulm University

beneficiaryAdministration:
1. Aim, Project, Background and Objective

The AI4CI project, co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123524, provides financial support to students enrolled in the continuing education master’s programme “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” at Ulm University (UUlm), Germany.

The objective of this call is to increase accessibility to advanced digital skills education, support up- and reskilling of professionals, and promote diversity and inclusion in computer science education.

Within this call, up to 80 fee waivers (with a total amount of max. 80.000 EUR), for individual modules in winter term 2026-2027 (October 2026-March 2027) will be awarded.

A fee waiver covers 80 % of the tuition fee of a module in the AI4CI programme. The module fees range from 585 to 1800 Euros. depending on module size in ECTS and specific characteristics of modules (e.g. inclusion of lab times or high amount of tutoring). Fee waivers therefore range between 468 and 1440 Euros.

Fee waivers apply only to modules taken in the semester for which the waiver is granted.

Applicants may apply for fee waivers for multiple modules, provided they are enrolled in these modules.

2. Eligibility

Applicants must fulfil all the following criteria:

1.   Be a citizen of an EU Member State, an EEA country, or a country associated with the Digital Europe Programme (https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/digital/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf),

2.     Be admitted and enrolled in the master’s programme Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries at Ulm University.

3.     Be registered as a student of the programme in winter semester 2026/2027.

4.     Apply only for modules that

a.  are part of the AI4CI curriculum and

b.     can still be credited toward the final grade and degree.

5.     A fee waiver may be granted only once per module per student.

3. Scope of the Support

  1.       A maximum of 80 module fee waivers will be awarded in this call.
  2.       Each fee waiver reduces the tuition fee of the respective module by 80 %.
  3.       Fee waivers apply only to the semester in which the module is taken.

Students may receive multiple fee waivers, provided they apply for different modules and ranking positions allow it.

4. Application Procedure

4.1 Call Announcement

By 1 October, all admitted students will receive information about:

  1.       the availability of fee waivers,
  2.       the eligibility requirements,
  3.       the application procedure,
  4.       and the application deadline.

4.2 Application Deadline

Applications must be submitted by 1 December 2026.

Applicants must submit:

  1.       a completed application form indicating
  2. other modules they will attend in winter semester 2026-2027, and
  3. other modules for which a fee waiver is requested.
  4.       proof of nationality.
  5.       consent allowing the programme administration to access relevant student data in the HIS student administration system and the App4Master admission system.

Applicants may additionally submit supporting documentation relevant to diversity criteria described in Section 7.

5. Evaluation Procedure

Applications will be evaluated by the Study Programme Committee of the AI4CI programme at Ulm University and the corresponding talent scouting team.

The evaluation will take place within 10 working days after the application deadline.

Each module application is evaluated independently.

Applications will be ranked according to the evaluation criteria defined in Section 6 and the tie-breaking and diversity considerations criteria in section 7.

The highest-ranked module applications will receive a fee waiver.

All remaining eligible applications will be placed on a reserve list.

Applicants will be informed about the outcome within five working days after the evaluation.

6. Evaluation Criteria

The fee waiver scheme supports up- and reskilling in advanced AI competencies.

Applications are evaluated based on the curriculum category of the module.

Points are assigned as follows:

Module Area

Points

A2 Mandatory Area – Artificial Intelligence

3

B1 Systems and Networks

2

B2 Automatics and Robotics

2

B3 Processes and Data Management

2

B4 Free Elective Module

1

All module areas are defined in the Subject-Specific Study and Examination Regulations of the AI4CI programme (10 June 2025) and its additional documents.

The maximum score per module application is 3 points.

7. Tie-Breaking and Diversity Considerations

If multiple applications receive the same score, the following criteria will be applied sequentially to determine priority:

  1. Women and gender minorities
  2. Applicants with disabilities
  3. Applicants with family responsibilities or caregiving duties

Supporting documentation may be provided during the application process.

If applications remain tied after applying the above criteria, the final ranking will be determined by random draw conducted by the study programme committee and the talent scouting team.

8. Award and Implementation of the Fee Waiver

Students selected for a fee waiver will receive an updated tuition fee notice reflecting the 80 % reduction for the respective module.

Receiving a fee waiver does not prevent students from applying for other scholarships, unless the conditions of those programmes prohibit it.

However, double funding from EU sources for the same purpose is not permitted.

If a student receives additional funding, the student must provide a written declaration confirming the absence of EU double funding.

If double funding is identified, the fee waiver may be reduced or withdrawn.

9. Appeals

Applicants may submit an appeal only in cases of procedural errors or factual inaccuracies in the evaluation.

Appeals must:

  1. be submitted in writing within five working days after notification of the results;
  2. clearly indicate the alleged procedural error or incorrect data.

The study programme committee will review the appeal and provide a decision within 10 working days.

10. Termination of the Fee Waiver

The fee waiver may be withdrawn if the student:

  1. withdraws from the programme,
  2. takes academic leave,
  3. transfers to another study programme,
  4. or violates academic integrity or ethical standards.

Students may voluntarily withdraw from the fee waiver by submitting a written request.

Unused funding may be reallocated in a future fee waiver call within the AI4CI project.

11. Publication of Results

The final list of fee waiver recipients will be published no later than 15 December 2026.

Personal data will be processed and published in accordance with applicable data protection regulations.

call_title: NOSTRADAMUS - Open Call #1: Funding Digital Applications for Sustainable and Efficient Agriculture
description: NOSTRADAMUS Open Call #1 invites system actors and innovators (SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps, RTOs, end-user organisations) to design, develop, test, and validate multi-functional, open-source digital applications for farm decision-making and agribusiness. Selected Third Parties will build upon the NOSTRADAMUS data infrastructure - including multi-dimensional Open Data Cubes, Analysis Ready Data (ARD) Earth Observation pipelines, real-time IoT Observatory streams, and socio-economic datasets - to deliver data-driven tools that optimize agricultural inputs (water, fertilizers, pesticides), improve energy balance, and enhance production resilience in cereal-based agricultural systems. The call covers 5 designated topics: Topic 1 (T1): Sustainable crop production and optimisation of cereal-based systems under changing climate and soil conditions. Topic 2 (T2): Nutrient and soil health management, integrating soil fertility indicators, organic matter dynamics, and precision fertilisation models. Topic 3 (T3): Water resource efficiency and drought resilience, using Early Warning System outputs and IoT-based soil moisture monitoring. Topic 4 (T4): Smart and predictive pest and disease management to support the EU objective of reducing pesticide dependency. Topic 5 (T5): Open topic (integrated, cross-domain decision-support applications combining at least two topics T1–T4). Awarded Third Parties must participate in a 12-month 4-Sprint program (Training, Design, Development & Validation, Demonstration & Assessment), physically demonstrate their application at 1 primary NOSTRADAMUS pilot site (DE, RS, CH, SI, or CY), deliver at least 1 user training session, release their source code as open-source, and author an EIP-AGRI Practice Abstract.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Applications must be submitted electronically via the F6S platform: https://www.f6s.com/nostradamus-open-call-1/apply by 02 December 2026 at 17:00 CET.

All Open Call #1 documents are available for download at: https://nostradamus-project.eu/open-call-1/

Evaluation Workflow:

  1. Admissibility & Eligibility Check: Verification of submission criteria, official templates, language (English), single submission rules, country eligibility (EU Member States & Horizon Europe Associated Countries), and applicant eligibility (individual SMEs/start-ups/small mid-caps or 2-partner consortia).
  2. External Remote Expert Evaluation: Each eligible proposal is reviewed independently by two external experts against 4 criteria: Alignment (score 0–5), Excellence (score 0–5), Impact (score 0–5), and Implementation (score 0–5). Thresholds: min. 3/5 per criterion, min. 12/20 overall.  
  3. Consensus & Ranking: Expert review panel establishes a consensus report and topic ranking lists (one list per topic, 5 in total).  
  4. Online Interviews: The top 3 ranked proposals per topic undergo a 30-minute pitch and Q&A session with an Interview committee to finalize scores and ranking.  
  5. Final Selection & Contracting: Selection of 5 sub-projects (guaranteeing min. 1 project per topic T1–T5) followed by formal KYC verification and Sub-Grant Agreement signature.

call_title: LLM-BRIDGE – Venture Incubation Programme - Open Call for Incubators – 2nd Call
description: The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to: Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance. Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets. Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem. Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will: Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups. Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures. Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem. The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Proposal submission:

All proposals shall be submitted at: https://share.hsforms.com/133VDDomZReqeyGTex0VYRwf4os

Proposal template and supporting documents:

The proposal template and supporting documents are available at: https://www.llm-bridge.eu/open-calls-2/

Evaluation process:

Eligible proposals will be evaluated by independent external experts, appointed by the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium, to ensure objectivity and impartiality.

Each proposal will be assessed by at least two experts using the criteria and scoring system defined in the Evaluation Criteria.

Applicants will be notified of the evaluation results within four weeks after completion of the panel ranking.

Each applicant will receive an Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) containing individual scores, comments, and the final consensus assessment.

The successful applicant will be invited to sign a Financial Support Agreement with 28DIGITAL on behalf of the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium.

Evaluation criteria:

The evaluation is based on the following criteria, each with a maximum score and a minimum threshold:

Relevance (maximum score: 10; threshold: 6): Assessment of how well the proposal aligns with the objectives of LLM-BRIDGE, including its capacity to support early-stage Generative AI startups and contribute to European GenAI strategic goals.

Track record (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Evaluation of the applicant’s proven experience in incubating and scaling AI or deep-tech ventures, with demonstrated results in terms of startup growth and innovation.

Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential.

Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector.

Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance.

Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money.

Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels.

Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed.

Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail.

Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain.

Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed.

Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings.

Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses.

Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.

Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential.

Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector.

Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance.

Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money.

Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels.

Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed.

Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail.

Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain.

Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed.

Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings.

Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses.

Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.

call_title: ZMINA:Resilience. Second call for co-creation funding of international cooperation projects
description: ZMINA:Resilience. Second call for co-creation funding of international cooperation projects

beneficiaryAdministration:
The IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK), together with Trans Europe Halles (SE), announce the second call for proposals for the co-creation funding of international cooperation projects.

The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience.

Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner.

Purpose of the call:

  1. To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual.
  2. To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine)

Budget:

— Total funding available 187,500€

— Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs.

— Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution.

— Expected number of grants 7-10

Eligible applicants:

Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country (EU countries, non-EU countries). For Ukraine, they must be registered in a zone effectively controlled by the Ukrainian government. Projects must include at least two partners from at least two countries, of which one is Ukraine. Individual artists and freelancers cannot apply directly; they must take part through an eligible organisation acting as a project partner.

List of activities that are eligible for financial support:

— All activities necessary for the co-creation project implementation and development.

— Presentation of the co-creation in the locality of each project partner.

— Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, artistic, presentation purposes.

Duration of the project:

— project duration period: up to 7 months within the indicative implementation window of February–August 2027;

— earliest start of the project after the signature of the grant agreement.

Technical eligibility criteria:

  1. all required attachments (as described in the Application Procedure below) are uploaded to the platform in separate files and in the formats specified for this call;
  2. all required attachments are uploaded to the platform following standard templates that can be downloaded on the platform;
  3. all required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable;
  4. all the project partners meet the eligibility conditions specified for this call;
  5. the registration of all the project partners meets the conditions specified for this call;
  6. the application form is complete and contains all the requested information;
  7. the total subgrant amount requested in the budget is within the maximum subgrant amounts determined for this call;
  8. the total project partners contribution meets the conditions specified for this call;
  9. project implementation period is within the project implementation period defined for this call;
  10. the start of project implementation meets the conditions specified for this call.

Selection criteria:

Relevance:

— relevance of the project to the objectives of the call;

— relevance of potential co-creation to act as a basis for intercultural dialogue.

Quality:

— quality of extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital, green, inclusion) are addressed, including barrier-free access to project results;

— quality of the partnership: the equal importance of the roles played by project partners;

— quality of scale of engagement, measured by the expected audience size and number of local presentations.

Impact:

— Impact and the sustainability of the project, including plans and possibilities for future presentations of the co-creation.

Selection procedure:

Applications will first undergo a technical eligibility check by the ZMINA:Resilience team to verify that they meet all formal requirements, including admissibility and eligibility criteria. Proposals that pass this stage will then be assigned to two independent evaluators each.

Evaluators will assign scores to applications. Then, the applications will be rated according to the average score.

The final selection will be made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity, within the available budget of the call.

The application budget will be assessed for cost-effectiveness and plausibility, and may be adjusted before the grant agreement is signed. The final grant amount will be determined based on a combination of lump sum units and actual costs incurred: costs such as artist fees, travel, accommodation, and per diems are paid at the fixed unit rates listed under "Eligible costs covered by the grant" below, regardless of the exact amount spent, while costs such as equipment rental, production services, and shipping are reimbursed based on actual costs incurred.

Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual feedback for selection decisions. All decisions are final.

Application Procedure

— Applications must be submitted via the IZOLYATSIA online platform no later than 04.12.2026, 23:59 Kyiv time / 22:49 Central European Time on https://platform.izolyatsia.org/en/contest/zmina-resilience-cocreation-two .

— Applicant: The application shall be submitted by a single representative of the consortium/project partners (Lead Applicant).

Required Documents:

  1. The application form and budget (completed directly on the platform),
  2. Supporting documents regarding capacity, eligibility, and admissibility. The following must be uploaded to the platform in .pdf format separately for each partner:
  3. A scanned copy of the Letter of Guarantee, completed and signed by the head of the applicant organization (template available for download on the platform);
  4. Registration documents for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: national registration documents with English translation in case the document is issued in another language.
  5. Registration documents for organisation from Ukraine: Full Extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Physical Persons-Entrepreneurs, and Public Formations dated on or after 5 October 2026 - in their original language.
  6. The current version of the Statutes or equivalent (if mandatory for the legal entity) – all pages: for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: with English translation in case the document is issued in another language, for organisation from Ukraine: in their original language.
  7. Language of application: The application must be submitted in English.
  8. Support: During the application period, assistance will be provided through Q&A sessions and a dedicated email helpline.
  9. Subgrant Agreement Template

Funding Conditions

— Financial support: 70% is disbursed upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining amount is paid upon submission and approval of the report.

— Co-financing is mandatory and must be at least 10% of the total project budget.

— Double funding within the EU budget is not allowed.

— All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and within the project implementation period.

— Compliance with EU branding and visibility requirements is mandatory.

Eligible costs covered by the grant include

  1. Daily fee for artistic work: 75€/artist/day
  2. Travel: International: 350€/return trip or Local (e.g. participation in trainings): 65€/return trip
  3. Support to green travel (in addition to the travel rate above, for one-way trips over 600km not made by air): 300€ 
  4. Accommodation & per diem: 75€/overnight 
  5. Visa cost, if needed: 80€ 
  6. Shipping/Transport (of equipment), incl. insurance: at cost;
  7. Supplies & equipment (for equipment depreciation costs only): at cost;
  8. Services required for project implementation (production, rental of equipment, rental of space for project events, etc.): at cost;
  9. Communication, marketing and documentation: at cost.
  10. Management and administration costs: Max. 20% of the overall project budget (grant amount plus own contribution/co-financing combined).

Estimated dates:

— Launch of the Call for Proposals: 5 October 2026

— Deadline for Submission of Applications: until 23:59 4December 2026 (Kyiv time)

— Evaluation Period: December 2026

— Announcement of Results: January 2027

— Signing of Grant Agreements: February 2027

— Implementation of Selected Projects: February 2027 – August 2027 (each project runs up to 7 months within this window, depending on its grant agreement signing date)

description: Every Open Call applicant must select one challenge of one of the project pilots – (i) port automation, (ii) smart safety of workers and (iii) cohesive vehicle monitoring and diagnostics. Proposals must contribute to the ASSIST-IoT paradigm by validating some of its technologies in one challenge of one pilot. All the previous can be summarised, in general, in: · Design, implementation and integration of interoperable device layer components, based on different low-level communication standards or on ad-hoc proprietary device solutions. · Design, implementation and integration of interoperable networking layer components, based on different standards higher-level communication standards or on ad-hoc proprietary networking solutions to be tested in ASSIST-IoT pilots. · Design, implementation and integration of interoperable middleware layer components. These need to deal with the different middleware services such as discovery, management, querying, coordination and interaction. · Design, implementation and integration of interoperable application service components. These should exploit major standards and be integrated with ASSIST-IoT API. · Design, implementation and integration of interoperable data and semantics components. Specifically, semantics layer components have to deal with heterogeneous IoT ontology matching. · Design, implementation and integration of virtualization mechanism for smart objects, including context aware mechanisms and transfer of virtual objects between servers and cloud platforms. · Design, implementation and integration of fog/edge/cloud support mechanisms, including support for different services, inter cloud mechanisms applied to IoT and support for virtualization. · Design, implementation and integration of AI/ML libraries and tools addressing ASSIST-IoT pilots.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Deadline:

January 15th 2023, 17:00 CET

Submission:

The application must be done Via visiting the form: https://form.jotform.com/221812189680358, fulfilling mandatory fields and properly submitting the Proposal using the Proposal Template.

The submission will be open and available to receive proposals from November, 14th, 2022 to Janaury, 15th, 2023, 17:00 CET. Incomplete proposals will not be evaluated. Notifications on funding or rejections will be sent out to applicants, together with any feedback, by January 31st, 2023.

Evaluation process:

Every proposal will go through a transparent evaluation process carried out by two external experts and an observer to guarantee impartiality. Proposals will be scored up to 25 points based on the criteria: (i) Relevance to ASSIST-IoT, (ii) Impact and sustainability, (iii) Technical Excellence, (iv) Quality of Implementation and (v) Quality of Team. All proposals will receive an evaluation report (ESR) attached to the letter of acceptance/rejection.

Funded proposals:

A total number of 8 proposals with a maximum foreseen contribution of 60.000€ per proposals will be funded in this second open call

description:
Every Open Call applicant must select one challenge of one of the project pilots – (i) port automation, (ii) smart safety of workers and (iii) cohesive vehicle monitoring and diagnostics.

Proposals must contribute to the ASSIST-IoT paradigm by validating some of its technologies in one challenge of one pilot. All the previous can be summarised, in general, in:

·        Design, implementation and integration of interoperable device layer components, based on different low-level communication standards or on ad-hoc proprietary device solutions.

·        Design, implementation and integration of interoperable networking layer components, based on different standards higher-level communication standards or on ad-hoc proprietary networking solutions to be tested in ASSIST-IoT pilots.

·        Design, implementation and integration of interoperable middleware layer components. These need to deal with the different middleware services such as discovery, management, querying, coordination and interaction.

·        Design, implementation and integration of interoperable application service components. These should exploit major standards and be integrated with ASSIST-IoT API.

·        Design, implementation and integration of interoperable data and semantics components. Specifically, semantics layer components have to deal with heterogeneous IoT ontology matching.

·        Design, implementation and integration of virtualization mechanism for smart objects, including context aware mechanisms and transfer of virtual objects between servers and cloud platforms.

·        Design, implementation and integration of fog/edge/cloud support mechanisms, including support for different services, inter cloud mechanisms applied to IoT and support for virtualization.

·        Design, implementation and integration of AI/ML libraries and tools addressing ASSIST-IoT pilots.
