description: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) in Petten intends to replace the existing Air Handling Units (AHUs) and associated HVAC infrastructure located in buildings 308 and 309. The current ventilation systems are obsolete and have reached the end of their operational lifespan. Furthermore, preliminary technical assessments have indicated that the existing air renewal capacity is insufficient to maintain optimal indoor air quality for the occupants. To ensure a healthy, safe, and productive working environment, this procurement aims to upgrade the facilities. The primary objective is to improve indoor air quality, while simultaneously improving the overall energy efficiency of the buildings. The scope of this contract encompasses the supply, installation, and comprehensive commissioning of the new air handling systems and related infrastructure to provide a fully functional delivery. This includes the safe removal and disposal of the existing AHUs, roof support frames, humidification systems, and redundant cabling or piping, ensuring continuous operation of the buildings during the transition. The technical project involves replacing the units with new, highly energy-efficient equipment featuring heat recovery systems. Additionally, the contract covers the complete adaptation of the hydraulic system to operate under a new, lower-temperature regime, the installation of humidification systems, installing structural supports on the roofs, and the execution of all necessary electrical works. Finally, it requires the full integration of the new instrumentation and controls with the existing Siemens Building Management System (BMS), alongside essential auxiliary tasks such as ductwork cleaning.

description: Through this procurement, Frontex is seeking to acquire specialised Services based on the use of High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to support its border surveillance and management activities. In particular, Frontex wants to conduct a Pilot Project to demonstrate the abilities, efficiency and effectiveness (primarily in terms of accuracy, reliability and cost-efficiency) of HAPS in providing persistent surveillance, data fusion, RFI monitoring, and wireless connectivity capabilities over the designated wide Area of Interest. For this purpose, the services requested by Frontex shall consist in the deployment of at least one HAPS over the Area of Interest for a period of 15 consecutive days of continuous operation during the Deployment and Operational Phase of this project.

description: Through this procurement, Frontex is seeking to acquire specialised Services based on the use of High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to support its border surveillance and management activities. In particular, Frontex wants to conduct a Pilot Project to demonstrate the abilities, efficiency and effectiveness (primarily in terms of accuracy, reliability and cost-efficiency) of HAPS in providing persistent surveillance, data fusion, RFI monitoring, and wireless connectivity capabilities over the designated wide Area of Interest. For this purpose, the services requested by Frontex shall consist in the deployment of at least one HAPS over the Area of Interest for a period of 15 consecutive days of continuous operation during the Deployment and Operational Phase of this project.

description: IMPORTANT INFORMATION All entities who want to participate in the future negotiated procedure, either as a sole tenderer or as a member of a consortium must be invited. Since only candidates who expressed their interest during the ex-ante publicity phase will be invited, a group of economic operators intending to form a consortium must express their interest jointly, as a single group, at this stage. In other words, candidates should already know their consortium composition from the beginning of the procedure, before submitting their interest, as no additional candidate can be added at a later stage. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCEDURE Stocktaking and assessment of EU-funded social innovation projects under EaSI and ESF+/EaSI strand The contractor will consolidate and assess evidence from approximately 200 completed and ongoing social innovation and social experimentation projects financed under EaSI and the ESF+/EaSI strand between 2014 and 2027. The contractor will first prepare an inventory of the full project portfolio and develop a project typology, meaning a structured classification of projects according to their potential for policy uptake, transfer and scaling up. Using transparent and consistently applied criteria, such as the strength of available evidence, maturity of implementation, policy relevance, transferability and feasibility of expansion, each project will be classified as having low, medium or high potential. Based on this classification, the contractor will produce harmonised fiches and policy-oriented narratives for 25 projects assessed as having high or medium potential. For 15 projects, the contractor will carry out light-touch credibility checks, comparing reported results with existing statistics, benchmarks and, where useful, information from short interviews. These checks will assess the plausibility of the reported results without establishing causality. For 5 other projects, the contractor will prepare quasi-experimental evaluation designs explaining how existing data could be used to compare participants with similar non-participants and estimate project effects. The contractor will design and demonstrate the approaches but will not conduct full impact evaluations. The contractor will also produce an operational toolkit for transfer and scaling up, containing practical criteria, steps, templates and checklists to help public authorities determine whether and how successful approaches could be adapted, transferred, replicated or expanded in other policy and geographical contexts. The results will support policy learning, Member State implementation and programming under the MFF 2028–2034.

description: The Joint Research Centre (JRC) contributes to validating Copernicus Sentinel-2 and -3 aquatic data products with several autonomous above-water systems, such as those included in the Ocean Colour component of the Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET-OC; Zibordi et al., 2009, 2022). The validation of Copernicus Sentinel-2 and -3 data products with AERONET-OC in-situ measurements is crucial for the assessment and eventual minimisation of uncertainties both in satellite data products and in the algorithms applied to their processing, thus ensuring a maximized return of investment for the Copernicus Programme. The present service request concerns the computation through accurate radiative transfer simulations of operational water-surface reflectance factors for above-water radiometric data obtained with the measurement and data reduction protocols implemented in AERONET-OC.

description: Das JRC Karlsruhe ist einer der sechs wissenschaftlichen Standorte der Gemeinsamen Forschungsstelle der Europäischen Kommission (Joint Research Centre, JRC) und ist der Hauptsitz der wissenschaftlichen Direktion für nukleare Überwachung und Sicherheit. Es befindet sich auf dem Campus Nord des Karlsruher Instituts für Technologie (KIT) in Karlsruhe, Deutschland. Im Rahmen des nuklearen Arbeitsprogramms des JRCs widmet sich der JRC-Standort Karlsruhe der nuklearen Überwachung und Sicherheit, um die wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen für den Schutz des europäischen Bürgers vor den Risiken zu schaffen, die mit dem Umgang und der Lagerung hochradioaktiver Stoffe einhergehen. Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist die Erbringung von Objektsicherungsaufgaben an dem JRC Standort in Karlsruhe. Die Aufgaben richten sich nach den geltenden Vorschriften und Vorgaben sowohl auf europäischer (BESCHLUSS (EU, Euratom) 2015/443 DER KOMMISSION vom 13. März 2015 über Sicherheit in der Kommission) wie auf nationaler Ebene (Anforderungen an den Objektsicherungsdienst und an Objektsicherungsbeauftragte in kerntechnischen Anlagen und Einrichtungen der Sicherungskategorie I). Der Vertrag umfasst den Zugang zu als „RESTREINT UE/EU RESTRICTED“ eingestuften Verschlusssachen und deren Bearbeitung und/oder Aufbewahrung bzw. Speicherung, worauf der Beschluss (EU, Euratom) 2015/444 und dessen Durchführungsbestimmungen Anwendung finden. Besondere Sicherheitsanforderungen sind Bestandteil des Vertrags (Geheimschutzklausel im Anhang des Vertrags). Die Vergabe von Unteraufträgen unterliegt der schriftlichen vorherigen Genehmigung durch den öffentlichen Auftraggeber und der Einhaltung aller Sicherheitsvorschriften durch den Unterauftragnehmer und dessen Mitarbeiter.

description: ECHA is tasked with publishing scientific reports concerning the prioritisation of substances for the watchlists, the priority substance list, and the groundwater pollutant list under the Water Framework Directive, Environmental Quality Standards Directive and the Groundwater Directive. The legal text indicates specific tasks for ECHA relevant to the watchlist process. One of these relates to the potential inclusion of indicators for anti-microbial resistance (AMR) on the next watchlists for surface water and groundwater. On the basis of scientific reports prepared by ECHA, indicators of anti-microbial resistance, evolution or transmission are to be included in the watch lists provided that reliable methods of sampling and analysis not entailing excessive costs are available. AMR cannot be kept on the list for a second consecutive period of three years unless a harmonised and reliable risk assessment methodology is available which, when applied, shows that the monitoring data collected during the first monitoring period are insufficient to assess the risk they pose to or via the aquatic environment. This specific study will focus on developing such a harmonised and reliable risk assessment methodology, also taking into account recent studies and recommendations on monitoring of AMRs in the aquatic environment. The study will include collecting and reviewing scientific information and data that would support the assessment of EU-wide risk from AMRs including the development and justification of appropriate thresholds/limits to support the risk assessment. description: The JRC and the European Commission's Competence Centre on Participatory and Deliberative Democracy (CC-DEMOS) have built a specific training offer on citizen engagement processes based on co-creation and deliberation for public administrations at local, regional and national level across the EU. The training offer targets three levels of competence (basic, advanced and train-of-trainers) and is available in EN, DA, PL. It includes a full package of resources: for each competence level, it provides a course-book, annotated PowerPoint presentations, roll-out of the course, agenda of the course, self-assessment questionnaire, in-class exercises, and case collection.The goal is to upscale the use of this training package and to reach out to a large number of administrations.

description: The Representation of the European Commission in Bulgaria organizes and participates in numerous events throughout the year as part of its annual communication strategy. In order to cover these activities and better communicate the priorities of the European Commission, the Representation requires high-quality photographic and video materials. These materials will be used across various communication channels, including press releases (and subsequently by different media outlets); the website of the European Commission Representation in Bulgaria; social media (Facebook, Twitter); printed publications and information materials; presentations; collages; and others.

description: La Cour de Justice de L'U.E. est en quête d’un concessionnaire pour un point presse sur son site à Luxembourg pour une durée initiale de 3 ans, prorogeable tacitement 2 fois au maximum, chaque fois pour 3 ans. La valeur estimée hors TVA du marché est basée sur le chiffre d’affaires estimé du magasin de journaux sur la durée maximale de la concession (9 ans). Le local mis a disposition a une surface actuelle d’environ 45 m² et sera vraisemblablement agrandi jusqu'à 68m². Les documents de marché seront publiés avec l’avis de marché et incluront notamment les spécifications techniques, le plan du local, et le modèle de contrat de concession.

description: This project aims both to enhance Türkiye’s digital transformation policy ecosystem and its alignment with EU, and also to improve the digital technology, innovation and adoption capabilities of the sectors. Within the scope of the project, technology users and providers, primarily within the manufacturing and health sectors, and relevant public institutions and NGOs will be targeted. Digital transformation pathways will be defined and applied, related capacities will be enhanced by the Contractor. To realize project’s purposes, the project has been designed under two components. Under the first component, Policy and Strategy, initially current state of the digital transformation policy and strategy will be analysed on national and global level. Later on, a governance model with implementation framework, digital transformation policies, strategy and roadmaps which are integrated with EU policies, will be developed to guide digital transformation of Türkiye. Moreover, disaster resilience plans against pandemics and natural disasters integrating the use of digital technologies will be prepared. Within the second component, being Pilot Implementation, under the framework and guidance of outputs of Component 1, capacity and service quality of digital transformation structures and enterprises will be enhanced. At the same time, a functioning digitalization structures network will be developed to increase their sustainability and capacity to provide up-to-date, relevant services. An online platform will be developed, which will facilitate coordination, communication, awareness raising, visibility activities will be carried out during the lifespan project.

description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.

description: Provision of a scheduled air transport service for passengers and light cargo with the operational capacity and flexibility to implement ad hoc flights in the region as and when needed. The aim of the contract is to provide air transport services to and within Somalia to support the continued cooperation and engagement of the EU, EU Member States and other stakeholders. The services are open to humanitarian and development stakeholders therefore contributing to the humanitarian-development-peace nexus. description: El trabajo específico de este contrato forma parte de un proceso organizativo institucional en evolución. description: Aviation is changing, and so are the skills needed to keep it flying safely and sustainably. Through the EPAS 2025 Task “Future Workforce Challenges”, EASA is working to inspire, attract, and prepare the next generation of aviation professionals while supporting today’s workforce in adapting to new technologies and opportunities. As part of this effort, GEN Days 2025 will take place at EASA in Cologne from 26–28 November 2025, gathering students from EUROAVIA, EASA experts, and industry professionals to explore aviation’s future skills, competencies, and careers. The initiative will produce engaging videos, articles, and visuals to raise awareness and showcase how Europe can build a strong, diverse, and future-ready aviation workforce. The contractor shall provide technical content and direction input for workshops and discussions at GEN Days. During the event, the contractor shall film and afterwards edit and create the visual and digital media.

description: This action aims to support ambitious climate action in IMO by strengthening the Pacific Island States (PIS) in the organisation and their effective co-operation with the EU. The objective is to enable PIS to prepare for and participate in IMO, so they can actively support an ambitious revision of the IMO GHG strategy and contribute to the assessment of mid- and long-term IMO climate measures. For this, the project will fund a study to identify and analyse data on PIS which will be used to assess the impacts of future measures. A shortage of data from the region complicates the assessment of the effects of the measures, which the study will remedy. Secondly, this project will organise regional workshops and high-level meetings to facilitate shared EU-Pacific position in the negotiations on IMO, and provide technical assistance for PIS. The meetings will take place in 2023 and 2024. The action supports existing and successful EU-Pacific co-operation.

description: Provision of a scheduled air transport service for passengers and light cargo with the operational capacity and flexibility to implement ad hoc flights in the region as and when needed. The aim of the contract is to provide air transport services to and within Somalia to support the continued cooperation and engagement of the EU, EU Member States and other stakeholders. The services are open to humanitarian and development stakeholders therefore contributing to the humanitarian-development-peace nexus. The Flight services will be between Nairobi and Mogadishu, and between Mogadishu and hubs within Somalia. The contractor is expected to handle the bookings, including the collection of ticket fares as part of a cost recovery mechanism.

description: In order to ensure effective, reliable and consistent monitoring and control of compliance with EU road transport legislation there must be an adequate enforcement mechanism in place. In recognition of the importance of law enforcement, the EU introduced certain minimum requirements for carrying out controls of compliance with the relevant rules during controls at roadside and checks at premises of the road transport undertaking. Despite developments made at national, European and international levels to step up enforcement, the complexity of the rules applicable to highly mobile road transport sector remains a huge challenge. The general objective of the project is to initiate the process of creating a regulatory and technological environment for for checking compliance with the EU road transport rules in the smartest and most efficient possible way, using the potential of the existing and emerging digitalisation, automation and communication technologies.

description: The government of the Republic of Tunisia, through the promoter (STEG), has requested the EIB to finance its distribution network rehabilitation programme (the ‘Project’) for the period 2020-2025, with the aim of upgrading and modernising its MV/LV network. For Tunisia, the general objective of the Project is to strengthen the national electricity transmission and distribution system, for better coverage of the demand for electricity. For STEG, the objective is to reduce technical and commercial losses and improve reliability of electricity supply in seven distribution areas (Central region, Greater Tunis, Northern region, North-Western region, Southern region, South-Western region and Sfax). To conclude the overall objective d the technical assistance is: 1) to align project implementation with EIB’s environmental and social (E&S) standards, and; 2) to aid and support STEG in the implementation of the project.

     — ICT coordination services;

lots: [{"number":"1","title":"Provision of ICT Coordination Services","description":"Lot 1 will result in an award of a direct service contract. Services to be provided to SESAR 3 JU shall be performed in English and include, but not be limited to: (a) technical expertise: documenting for approval, an evolving technology and information strategy by identifying the technical solutions to put in place; understanding and challenging the services of the ICT suppliers/service providers and their proposed solutions in the context of meeting agreed user needs, system configuration constraints, alignment with Eurocontrol ICT system configuration where possible, data protection and security obligations by intervention at architecture, system design and implementation levels as well as support (first and second line); (b) governance and communication: implementing SESAR 3 JU governance rules by preparing and actively participating in the QICT Committee, monitoring ICT infrastructure and service delivery performance and reporting on it to the QICT Committee. Where needed preparing user communication and training activities; (c) supplier management: coordinating the ICT activities between SESAR 3 JU, representing its users, and the external ICT suppliers/service providers who deliver the operational services; (d) service configuration/delivery management: Preparing service agreements, independently validating and measuring the services delivered by the external SESAR 3 JU ICT suppliers/service providers and liaising with and communicating to SESAR 3 JU management and users; (e) contract management: under the supervision of SESAR 3 JU, act as technical expert to monitor SESAR 3 JU ICT contracts and to participate in the procurement activities; (f) project management: acting as technical expert of SESAR 3 JU ICT project activities, whether the projects are led by external ICT suppliers/service providers or result from internal corporate initiatives requiring the involvement of SESAR 3 JU ICT; The individual dismantling and disposal projects continuously produce radioactive waste whose radioactive inventory (including nuclear material content) must be accurately and reliably determined using N coincidence counters and gamma spectroscopy in order to dispose of them properly. description: In the frame of its Nuclear Decommissioning and Waste Management programme, the JRC Ispra has designed and qualified a final waste package (FWP) to be used for conditioning low-level and very low-level solid radioactive waste. The FWP is based on a prismatic container made of carbon steel, referred as ‘CP-5.2’ according to the UNI Italian standard. The JRC Ispra will have to acquire a significant amount of CP-5.2 containers in the coming years.Additionally to the supply of the CP-5.2 containers, the JRC Ispra needs to purchase adjustable steel pallets, in order to temporarily store cylindrical containers (‘CC-220’ to ‘CC-440’) containing radioactive waste.The FWPs and the pallets are to be safely stored in the interim storage facility of the JRC Ispra. Ultimately, the FWPs will be transferred to the Italian final repository.The purpose of the tendering procedure is to purchase the CP-5.2 containers and the pallets by mean of a multi-annual framework contract.

description: Development of product environmental footprint category rules (PEFCRs) and acquisition of relevant environmental footprint (EF) compliant datasets for hotel accommodation sector.With this call for tenders, the European Commission aims to develop PEFCRs for the hotel accommodations (as defined by NACE classification, section 55.10), in order to enable the measurement of their environmental impacts by using the Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) methodology. As a second objective of this call, the Commission aims to acquire the necessary EF compliant datasets for the above PEFCR. description: One priority of the 2022-2023 Multi Annual Action Plan of the ‘Global Challenges’ thematic programme is to strengthen the role of Local Authorities in the implementation and localisation of Sustainable Development Goals, following a Territorial Approach to Local Development (TALD). To promote this agenda, INTPA, through its thematic unit in charge of Local Authorities (G2), requires technical assistance, namely highly qualified sectorial expertise to provide strategic and operational support to the European Commission (EC) staff in European Union Delegations and at headquarter level. The Technical Assistance team will support the translation of the EC’s vision on Local Authorities as developmental actors through a territorial approach in EC-supported programs and projects. This support is provided in line with the EC COM 2013“Empowering Local Authorities in partner countries for enhanced governance and more effective development outcomes” and with the EC Reference Document n°23.

description: Käesoleva hanke eesmärk on valida sobiv töövõtja Tallinna Vabaduse väljakul toimuva Euroopa päeva tähistamise ürituse ala korraldamiseks ja haldamiseks. Üritus toimub 9. mail 2027 kell 15.00–18.00 osalevate ELi saatkondade soovil. Hankija on Euroopa Komisjoni esindus Eestis. 2027. aasta mais tähistatakse Eestis taas Euroopa päeva suurte avalike üritustega Tallinnas ja Narvas, rõhutades 9. maid kui Euroopa rahu ja ühtsuse päeva. Tuginedes varasemate aastate edukale kogemusele, sisaldab programm kaasahaaravaid tegevusi, mis on suunatud venekeelsele noorsoole ja noortele peredele. Ülevaate 2026. aasta üritustest leiab veebilehelt www.euroopapäev.ee. Tallinnas toimub Euroopa päeva keskne üritus „Meie Eesti, meie Euroopa“ Vabaduse väljakul. ELi saatkonnad ja nendega seotud organisatsioonid korraldavad näitusi ja tegevusi, pakkudes külastajatele võimalust tutvuda Euroopa kultuuridega, osaleda interaktiivsetes programmides ning saada rohkem teavet Euroopa riikide ja Euroopa Liidu kohta. Üritus hõlmab erinevatele vanuserühmadele ja sihtrühmadele – sealhulgas peredele ja lastele – sobivaid tegevusi ning võimalusi kogeda Euroopa kultuure muusika, tantsu, toidu ja muude kultuuriväljenduste kaudu. Üritus toimub kell 15.00–18.00. Toimumisaeg on kokku lepitud osalevate ELi saatkondade soovil, et hõlbustada nende osalemist ning võimaldada neil Euroopa päeva kesksete pidustuste ajal oma riike ja kultuure avalikkusele tutvustada. Programmi elluviimise eest vastutab Euroopa Komisjoni esindus koostöös Euroopa Parlamendi büroo ja osalevate saatkondadega. Lava- ja esinemisprogrammi koostab hankija koostöös saatkondadega, eesmärgiga pakkuda mitmekesist kava, mis sisaldab Euroopa kultuure tutvustavat muusikat, tantsu ja muid etteasteid. Esinemised võivad toimuda ürituse vältel regulaarsete ajavahemike järel, näiteks igal täis- ja pooltunnil. Üritus on kavandatud tasuta avaliku pidustusena, millega edendatakse Euroopa ühtsust, kultuurilist mitmekesisust ja kuuluvustunnet Euroopa kogukonda.

description: This contract forms part of the actions foreseen under the “Economic Governance Support Programme (EGSP)” – Financing Agreement (FA) ZM/FED/040-801, funded under the 11th European Development Fund (EDF). The project will provide support to; the finalisation of the methodology for the Zambian National Land Audit (NLA), building institutional capacity and; implementing a part of the NLA. The project will be implemented nationwide and will contribute to enhancing the administration and management of state land in Zambia. The expected outcomes of this contract are; 1) the NSDI (National Spatial Data Infrastructure) is improved, updated and data is made publicly available; 2) innovative land audit methodologies are tested and validated; 3) key results of the NLA are available and; vi) improved knowledge and experience for carrying out a full NLA are documented and used to draft a post-audit action plan.

Individuals (submitting joint tenders, for example), organisations and other groups of economic operators can apply. description: As part of the MIP’s support measures, the project will contribute to the state-building and stabilisation efforts in Somalia. It will complement the EU development cooperation portfolio and will provide capacity to the EU Delegation and enhance the Government's capacity needs, policy and political dialogue, development of sectoral policies and support to their implementation within the priority areas of the MIP 2021-2027. The specific objectives are: strengthen the capacity of the government of Somalia to deliver on the National Development Plan; ii) strengthen identification, formulation, implementation and monitoring of EU funded programmes in Somalia, including the coordination of Team Europe Initiative covering renewable energy, climate change adaptation and natural resources management and iii) enhance partnerships and facilitate policy dialogue.

description: The study has the following specific objectives:1. to provide an objective qualitative and quantitative assessment of the implementation of the Union’s current 2 GHz MSS framework, to give an overview of the 2 GHz MSS spectrum usage and services offered. description: The study will assess how certain measures provided by IPRED are used in the different Member States, considering the EU COM (2017) 708 final. It will provide policy recommendations on improvements to ensure that full advantage is taken of IPRED in the fight against counterfeiting. The study will address the Commission ́s commitment in the IP action plan to ensure that injunctions are applied uniformly and efficiently across Member States, especially on the proportionality principle. Emphasis will be put on e.g., dynamic injunctions. The study will complement to the study on dynamic blocking injunctions in the EU published by the EUIPO in March 2021. The study will assess how to further strengthen the efficiency and effectiveness of the current enforcement framework, which could serve as a basis for the EU Toolbox against counterfeiting. It will also identify legal differences, gaps and any other obstacles precluding an effective cross border enforcement and cooperation within the EU.

description: A current flagship in the EU’s portfolio in South Africa, the “Dialogue Facility” will be continued in the form of the Dialogue Facility 3.0. This much-hailed programme enables demand-driven knowledge exchange and dialogues towards strengthened policy development capacities. The Dialogue Facility successfully brings the aspirations of the EU-SA Strategic Partnership to a very concrete level as it brings together institutions and individuals. description: The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) is the keystone of European Union (EU) risk assessment regarding food and feed safety.The Risk Assessment Logistics Unit (RAL Unit) aims to facilitate the scientific production by connecting with people, tools and processes towards future EFSA. The RAL Unit provides support services to EFSA scientific staff and experts along the risk assessment processes of all mandates. The unit contributes to the optimisation and harmonisation of the risk assessment.The objective of this call is to identify a contractor to assist EFSA with launching public and targeted consultations through EFSA’s IT tools (Appian and Salesforce), retrieving reports, processing comments, and performing an initial analysis on their content. The contractor shall also be able to retrieve statistics on consultations used by EFSA internally or for external communications.

description: Integration of Turkish Research Area (TARAL) into European Research Area (ERA) by increased participation in Framework Programmes is a critical pillar supporting innovation and technology development in Türkiye. Further to Türkiye’s previous participation in EU programmes, there is still need to increase awareness, explore funding mechanisms and increase project applications in EU programmes among potential beneficiaries. Within the scope of the project, Türkiye’s performance in H2020 will be analysed through current situation assessment and roadmaps will be developed to increase participation in Horizon Europe. According to results of assessment and roadmaps, capacity development trainings will be provided for the target groups, which will play an active role for the improvement of the R&D sector and ecosystem in Türkiye. Also, several knowledge diffusion and networking activities will be organized to increase awareness on Horizon Europe.

description: Many emerging and developing countries point to the need for capacity building for transparency and for modelling needed for the development of climate strategies, policies and NDCs. The first and second iteration of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) submitted to the UNFCCC, suggest that many countries would benefit from improved data and modelling, to better understand the potential for domestic climate action and policies and for evidence-based policymaking. This contract intends to alleviate a part of this gap by supporting experts based in relevant institutes in selected developing countries to enhance the national capacity to model climate policy, project national greenhouse gas emissions, prepare targets and estimate the impacts of domestic policies and measures, as well as to track progress towards the achievement of their NDCs.The contract should also support experts’ participation in meetings that are of interest to the modelling community.

description: This pilot project is a continuation and budget extension of the existing pilot to provide assistance for the development of citizen energy communities and renewable energy communities in the field of building energy renovation. This pilot project aims to overcome financial, legal and technical barriers to citizen-led renovation projects. A specific Union support service should be created for Citizens Energy Communities (CEC) and Renewable Energy Communities (REC), which are new actors enshrined in the Union legislation able to catalyse citizens’ engagement in various aspects of the ecological transition, including renovation projects. Phase II aims to support a much wider deployment of the assistance, support and monitoring activities. It will also ensure the coordination between Phase I, Phase II and relevant initiatives financed under Horizon Europe and LIFE programmes. Phase II will take over the exchange platform upon completion of the work carried out in Phase I.

description: EUROMOD is a tax-benefit microsimulation model, which covers in a consistent manner the Member States of the European Union. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features a great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 13 country-specific modules: Belgium (lot 1), Bulgaria (lot 2), Cyprus (lot 3), Finland (lot 4), Hungary (lot 5), Ireland (lot 6), Italy (lot 7), Latvia (lot 8), Lithuania (lot 9), Malta (lot 10), Poland (lot 11), Spain (lot 12), Sweden (lot 13).

description: The general objective of this action is to improve health and safety of consumers in line with the EU product safety rules and Türkiye’s accession progress in the area of product safety.Specifically, this contract is expected to strengthen Turkish market surveillance authorities’ (MSAs) capacities to carry out efficient market surveillance (MS) activities for products sold online, support the establishment of an effective cooperation mechanism with regard to e-commerce surveillance activities and the increase awareness level of online sellers with regard to their legal obligations concerning the safety of products and increase the awareness level of consumers who purchase goods online. Within the scope of the project, the contractor is expected to provide various services such as strategy and action plan and software development, trainings, preparation of visibility materials, realization of seminars and workshops.

description: The aim of this project is to develop an automated database that collects and structures information on new approach methodologies (NAMs) in use for biomedical research. NAMs correspond to in vitro methods based on human cells and engineered tissues or in silico approaches employing computer modelling and simulation. Using automated approaches, such as Machine Learning or Artificial Intelligence, to mine the vast body of published literature will enable the creation and maintenance of an up-to-date, state of the art knowledge source collating NAMs applied to biomedical research, allowing the extension of already collected models both in time and in scope with the addition of new diseases categories.

Esinduse kommunikatsiooniosakonna juhendamisel suhtleb teenuseosutaja (sotsiaalmeedia konsultant) sotsiaalmeedia kogukonnaga Eestis, vastab nende küsimustele ja sõnumitele eesti ja vene keeles, jälgib meie kanalites esilekerkivaid suundumusi või ohte, meie veebipubliku suhtumist eri teemadesse ja esitab selle kohta ülevaateid ning annab soovitusi, kuidas sisu inimeste paremaks kaasamiseks optimeerida.

description: The European Parliament needs to update its range of furniture in order to meet new space requirements, be in line with changes in technology and working methods, follow developments related to occupational well-being and provide a suitable working environment for its staff. The European Parliament has, via a formal consultation, asked the other institutions and bodies on the Brussels and Strasbourg sites whether they intend to participate. The European Court of Auditors, the Court of Justice of the European Union, the Committee of the Regions, the European Economic and Social Committee, the European Ombudsman, the European Data Protection Supervisor and the Translation Centre for the Bodies of the European Union have responded positively.

description: The objective of the project is contribute to a better environmental status and life quality of citizens by strengthening capacities for implementation of waste management systems in line with the national requirements and EU environmental acquis. This service contract will support the operation of the newly established waste management company, build the company's capacities, as well as strengthen the capacity of the City of Novi Sad, the municipalities in the Novi Sad Region, and other stakeholders, to ensure quality realization of investments and to establish and manage a proper waste management system. Finally, the project will improve public awareness about waste management practices, in line with national and EU requirements.

description: The European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA) is planning to launch a call for tender for the provision of OSH Wiki articles related to the Health and Social Care (HeSCare) sector and focusing on psychosocial risks and mental health issues. OSH Wiki articles related to the Health and Social Care (HeSCare) sector and focusing on psychosocial risks and mental health issues. The overall objectives of the contract to be awarded are: To provide easy-to-understand articles, suitable for a non-technical audience, that provide information contributing to better understanding of how psychosocial risks and mental health issues in the HeSCare sector can be recognised, prevented and managed. The articles will be suitable to be published on the OSH Wiki platform ( https://oshwiki.osha.europa.eu/en ) and as such, they are not meant as comprehensive overviews of the topics, but should provide concise theoretical explanations, summary of the most relevant research data, information about practical implications and conclusions, including existing gaps and needs for future actions. The articles will focus on insights mainly from the European Union. Expected deliverables are: 9 OSH Wiki articles on the following topics: - PSRs and mental health issue in the HeSCare sector – What EU surveys tell us? - Prevention (and management) of PSRs in the HeSCare sector. - Violence and harassment in the HeSCare sector – risk factors, preventive measures - Return-to-work after sick leave related to mental health issues / retention of HeSCare workers suffering from mental health issues (focus on secondary and tertiary prevention) - Burnout and other mental health issues in the HeSCare sector: preventive measures (primary, secondary and tertiary prevention) - PSRs and organizational risk factors and accidents in the HeSCare sector - PSRs and organisational risk factors and MSDs in the HeSCare sector - Promoting mental health in the HeSCare sector - Occupational health and safety of HeSCare workers and and quality of services / patient safety The maximum total budget available for the contract to be awarded is 60.000 EUR (excluding VAT). It is possible to express interest as an individual organisation or a consortium. However please note that invited candidates can submit a joint tender with other economic operators only if they have expressed interest in the planned procedure as a consortium. More information regarding the participation rules can be found in the link "More information can be found here". Please find the technical and proffesional capacity criteria for this procedure in the following address: https://osha.europa.eu/en/about-eu-osha/procurement/osha2025lvp0006-exa-development-osh-wiki-articles-focusing-psychosocial-risks-and-mental-health-issues-health-and-social-care-hescare-sector-low-value-procedure

OSH Wiki articles related to the Health and Social Care (HeSCare) sector and focusing on psychosocial risks and mental health issues.
The overall objectives of the contract to be awarded are:
To provide easy-to-understand articles, suitable for a non-technical audience, that provide information contributing to better understanding of how psychosocial risks and mental health issues in the HeSCare sector can be recognised, prevented and managed.
The articles will be suitable to be published on the OSH Wiki platform ( https://oshwiki.osha.europa.eu/en ) and as such, they are not meant as comprehensive overviews of the topics, but should provide concise theoretical explanations, summary of the most relevant research data, information about practical implications and conclusions, including existing gaps and needs for future actions. The articles will focus on insights mainly from the European Union.
Expected deliverables are:
9 OSH Wiki articles on the following topics: 
-	PSRs and mental health issue in the HeSCare sector – What EU surveys tell us? 
-	Prevention (and management) of PSRs in the HeSCare sector. 
-	Violence and harassment in the HeSCare sector – risk factors, preventive measures 
-	Return-to-work after sick leave related to mental health issues / retention of HeSCare workers suffering from mental health issues (focus on secondary and tertiary prevention)
-	Burnout and other mental health issues in the HeSCare sector: preventive measures (primary, secondary and tertiary prevention) 
-	PSRs and organizational risk factors and accidents in the HeSCare sector 
-	PSRs and organisational risk factors and MSDs   in the HeSCare sector
-	Promoting mental health in the HeSCare sector 
-	Occupational health and safety of HeSCare workers and and quality of services / patient safety

The maximum total budget available for the contract to be awarded is 60.000 EUR  (excluding VAT).
It is possible to express interest as an individual organisation or a consortium. However please note that invited candidates can submit a joint tender with other economic operators only if they have expressed interest in the planned procedure as a consortium. More information regarding the participation rules can be found in the link "More information can be found here".

description: This project aims to increase the capacity of various stakeholders, including all relevant national institutions, to access and utilize climate finance. The project has 5 components: 1. Inception activities; 2. Drafting of a National Climate Finance Strategy; 3. Sustainable Finance Ecosystem and Taxonomy; 4. Institutional Capacity Building; 5. Visibility Activities. Taking international and national sustainable finance context and development into account, the project will improve national capacity to mobilise and effectively manage climate finance flows to support Türkiye's national climate change targets.

description: Preparation and implementation of a cross-national company survey examining the use and impact of artificial intelligence at the workplace. The contractor will conduct a mixed-mode telephone and online survey of establishments in Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Poland and Sweden, targeting 1,000 completed interviews per country. Services include sampling, register enrichment, questionnaire scripting, pilot testing, fieldwork, data processing, weighting, quality control and methodological reporting, producing comparable evidence on AI adoption, productivity, wages, workplace practices and job quality.

caName: Kogukonna haldur 2026 (eesti ja vene keeles)
description:
See konkursikutse hõlmab kogukonna halduri teenuseid eesti ja vene keeles. 

Euroopa Komisjoni Eesti esinduse kommunikatsiooniosakonna juhendamisel suhtleb teenuseosutaja (kogukonna haldur) venekeelse kogukonnaga Eestis, aitab jagada ELi teemalist infot, jälgib venekeelset meediat ning korraldab üritusi ja kohtumisi, et tugevdada suhteid venekeelses kogukonnas.
Kogukonna haldur suhtleb esinduse sotsiaalmeedia jälgijatega, vastab nende küsimustele ja sõnumitele eesti ja vene keeles, jälgib meie kanalites esilekerkivaid suundumusi või ohte, meie veebipubliku suhtumist eri teemadesse ja esitab selle kohta ülevaateid ning annab soovitusi, kuidas sisu inimeste paremaks kaasamiseks optimeerida.

description: This call for tenders is for an external independent study for the end-term evaluation of the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work 2021–2027 and to support the contracting authority in relation to the open public consultation in preparation of the post-2027 strategic framework. The strategic framework sets out three crosscutting key objectives and a range of actions for promoting workers’ health and safety. The three objectives are: anticipating and managing change in the new world of work brought about by the green, digital and demographic transitions; improving prevention of workplace accidents and illnesses; increasing preparedness for any potential future health crises. The implementation of these three objectives is underpinned by: (i) social dialogue; (ii) strengthening of the evidence base; (iii) strengthening of enforcement; (iv) awareness raising; and (v) funding. At its plenary meeting in December 2025, the tripartite Advisory Committee on Safety and Health at Work (ACSH) adopted an opinion on the state of play and future impulses regarding the EU strategic framework on health and safety at work4. Moreover, in June 2026, the Commission adopted the Report on the screening of the EU acquis in the area of health and safety at work5, and its accompanying Staff Working Document6 [TBC]. The results of this screening exercise study will inform the process of developing new EU OSH priorities in the strategic framework on health and safety at work after 2027.

description: AO 06D20/2025/M035 USUFRUIT D’ESPACES IMMOBILIERS POUR LE PARLEMENT EUROPEEN À BRUXELLES Le présent avis est destiné à informer les acteurs du marché immobilier ainsi que toute autre partie intéressée, sur les prévisions des besoins immobilier du Parlement européen à Bruxelles et à recueillir les noms des opérateurs susceptibles d’être intéressés par la procédure de prospection immobilière. Le Parlement européen pourra ensuite recueillir à une/des procédures « négociées » sans publication préalable d’un avis de marché, conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (UE, Euratom) 2024/2509 U PARLEMENT EUROPÉEN ET DU CONSEIL du 23 septembre 2024 Lors de cette négociation, les pré-équipements à inclure dans le cadre de l’usufruit, seront déterminés. Description du besoin: Afin de répondre à ses besoins d’espaces de stockage à l'horizon de 2026, le Parlement européen est à la recherche d’un immeuble logistique à pré-équiper pour être prêt à être utilisé par le Parlement européen, L’immeuble pourra faire partie d’un complexe immobilier pour autant que la partie destinée au Parlement et le terrain concerné, soient sécurisés et techniquement indépendants. L’immeuble ou le complexe immobilier sur un seul site, est destiné à abriter des fonctions de stockage, un espace d’accueil et de bureaux et une zone de parking. L’immeuble est situé à Bruxelles ou à sa périphérie et répond aux caractéristiques suivantes : • Entrepôt avec quais de déchargement : Surface brute de plancher hors sol totale comprise entre 7.000 m2 et 10.000 m2. • Espace de bureau : entre 150 et 200 m² • Début d’occupation entre juin 2026 et septembre 2026 • Situé à l’Est de Bruxelles. • Situés dans un rayon de maximum 35 km à vol d’oiseau de l’entrée camion du bâtiment SPINELLI (Rue d’Ardenne, B1040 Bruxelles) • Proche d’une sortie d’autoroute ou d’une nationale menant à Bruxelles. • La zone de parking comprend une zone de parking pour camions et remorques ainsi qu’une zone de manœuvres pour camions, et une zone de parking pour camionnettes et voitures. • Durée contractuelle usufruit de minimum 18 ans avec options de renouvellement • Les bâtiments devront être existants. Candidatures Les personnes physiques ou morales peuvent soumettre leur candidature dans le cadre de la présente prospection par courriel à l'adresse électronique suivante: inlo.bru.ao@ep.europa.eu. La date limite pour la clôture de la phase de prospection immobilière est fixée au 06 novembre 2025 . Les manifestations d’intérêt envoyées après cette date ne seront pas prises en considération.

description: Cette assistance technique s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’Action Approche Territoriale Intégrée dans le Nord de la Côte d’Ivoire (ATINORD), qui démarrera en 2026 et vise à contribuer à la stabilité de la Côte d’Ivoire via une approche territoriale intégrée dans la zone d’intervention. Face aux nombreuses initiatives gouvernementales et internationales, les autorités ivoiriennes et les Partenaires Techniques et Financiers (PTF) qui interviennent dans les régions du Nord font le constat partagé du besoin d'une coordination renforcée entre les interventions. Les objectifs spécifiques (réalisations) du marché seront les suivants : • OS 1 – Soutenir les capacités et les outils de la Commission Nationale des Frontières en Côte d'Ivoire (CNFCI) en matière de gouvernance, de gestion, de planification, de suivi et de coordination des acteurs aux frontières • OS 2 – Renforcer les capacités et les outils des autorités locales (préfectures, sous-préfectures, conseils de régions) en matière de gouvernance, de planification, de suivi et de coordination • OS 3 – Mettre en œuvre la logistique pour la gouvernance et le pilotage de l’action ATINORD

Face aux nombreuses initiatives gouvernementales et internationales, les autorités ivoiriennes et les Partenaires Techniques et Financiers (PTF) qui interviennent dans les régions du Nord font le constat partagé du besoin d'une coordination renforcée entre les interventions.

description: This is the renewal of the first Simpl PSO Framework contract, which was awarded in 2023 following the publication of calls for tenders CNECT/2023/OP/0050: https://etendering.ted.europa.eu/cft/cft-display.html?cftId=14888 . The objective of PSOII call for tenders is to procure services to support and improve Simpl programme quality management system built to ensure a high and stable quality level of the IT products related to Simpl programme. It is also meant to strengthen the project management support and horizontal coordination tasks across the involved stakeholders, boosting efficient processes inspired by open-source best practices while complying to European Commission procurement rules. The PSO II framework contract will follow up on the existing PSO framework contract after it ends of delivery of the third specific contract (September 2026).

description: In order to replace obsolete equipment, JRC-Petten intends to procure a new motion control system for its neutron diffractometer HB4 at the High Flux Reactor Petten. This project comprises the motor controllers and power amplifiers, if separated from the former, the motors themselves (14 or 15), the cabling, a switch box where the electronics are installed – or equivalent – mechanical adapters for the motor axes if needed, configuration of the controllers and a simple software facilitating demonstration of the functions and acceptance testing. The motion control system shall be delivered in a turnkey state, such that only connection to electric power and to the instrument computer is needed to operate.

description: The European Defence Agency (EDA), through its Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), is launching a ‘Prize Contest’* as part of the Operational Experimentation Campaign 2026 (OPEX261 PT) in Portugal. The initiative aims to accelerate the development, testing, and operational validation of advanced loitering munition and precision strike systems. Hosted by the Portuguese Army and integrated with the ARTEX26 exercise, the campaign will allow selected participants to demonstrate their technologies in realistic, controlled military environments alongside other emerging systems such as unmanned aerial and ground platforms. The Prize Contest seeks to produce objective performance data aligned with EU Member States’ operational needs, helping identify and mature promising defence technologies for rapid operational adoption. By enabling realistic experimentation, collaboration between industry and military stakeholders and structured technical assessments, the initiative supports informed capability development and future procurement decisions. Ultimately, it aims to strengthen Europe’s defence innovation ecosystem, improve interoperability and enhance the technological readiness and operational effectiveness of European armed forces. As part of the forthcoming Contest, EDA is organising an information session on 17 March 2026 from 14:00 till 16:00 (see hereunder Additional Information) .......................................................................................................................................................................... *Disclaimer: The European Defence Agency (EDA) launches a Prize Contest under Title IX of the Financial Regulation (Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509, Articles 209–210); a Prize Contest is a distinct instrument, separate from procurement or grants. To ensure visibility and market participation, the EDA publishes the contest notice in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJEU/TED). Participation will be governed by the Rules of Contest, which will be published on the EDA website at the launch of the contest, and which will set out eligibility, exclusion and award criteria, prize amount, and payment arrangements. This Prize Contest does not constitute a call for tenders, procurement procedure or contractual offer.

description: Framework contract for scientific, technical and project-management support to ECDC for a multi-year, cross-sectional point prevalence survey (PPS) of healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), antimicrobial use and infection prevention and control / antimicrobial stewardship structure and process indicators in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) in EU/EEA countries. The services will build on the previous HALT/LTCF PPS approach including: preparation and organisation of the PPS; development/adaptation of training materials, case studies, feedback-report templates and data-collection questionnaires; support to national PPS preparation and training; helpdesk, methodological and technical support to national contact points; support to data collection and data-quality checks; production of validated national databases; country- and LTCF-level feedback reports; analysis plans; early and final European survey reports; presentations/minutes for meetings; and related dissemination outputs including open-access fees for manuscripts. The contract also includes validation and additional analytical work to assess whether HAIs reported in LTCFs are correctly reported according to agreed case definitions, whether infections can be assessed as associated with healthcare in the LTCF context, and the impact of potential misclassification on PPS estimates. This may include protocol development for validation sub-studies, training and standardisation of validators, review of source documentation where available, inter-rater agreement analyses, sensitivity analyses, and methodological recommendations for future European LTCF PPS. Interested economic operators are encouraged to provide their feedback by completing the market analysis survey under the following link: https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/e5c0d4bf-4900-f38e-3601-8268f775aa58

description: The aim of this contract is to strengthen the analytical capabilities of the Joint Research Centre (JRC)'s modelling tools for assessing accessibility to relevant destinations (including employment, healthcare, and education services). This enhancement shall focus on active mobility modes, such as walking and cycling, which are integral to developing sustainable transport systems and which complement public transport models and analyses. By improving the characterisation of active modes and transport networks in the European Union (EU), the project shall enable analyses for specific vulnerable profiles and enhance the accuracy of results, to effectively inform related policy decisions. The contract will have to provide methodological support to the JRC for generating high-resolution (down to a 100-metre-by-100-metre scale) indicators that capture the multidimensional nature of transport poverty. Such indicators shall incorporate affordability considerations and help assess, for instance, vulnerability to increases in fuel prices or public transport fares across the EU. Finally, the contract shall support the development of the Transport Poverty Hub. External support allows the JRC to draw on the state-of-the-art knowledge of researchers active in the emerging field of characterisation of active mode networks and the integration of affordability into transport poverty indicators. The methodologies, scripts and documentation produced under the contract remain with the JRC so that the resulting capability can be maintained, extended, and re-used in-house.

description: External Consultants as ICT Standardisation Experts for DG CNECT in targeted standardisation groups across ITU-T and other relevant technical bodies in ISO & IEC Background and objectives: The International affairs and Policy outreach Unit (DG CNECT.DDG2.1) is the Unit in DG CONNECT in charge of international issues, including the coordination of matters related to information and communication technologies (ICT) standardisation, and representing the EU in the International Telecommunication Union standardisation sector (ITU-T). The objective of the EU regarding international standardisation, as stated in the Communication setting an EU Strategy on Standardisation[1], aims at reinforcing EU’s leading position as forerunner in key technologies and promoting core EU values in global standardisation. The International Digital Strategy[2] of the European Union also calls for shaping a global digital governance and standards with a network of partners, promoting its values-based approach on digital standards to shape a global digital transformation that is human-centric, trustworthy, and respects human rights and fundamental freedoms, acting decisively to become a driving force of responsibly guided technological advancement on the global stage. The EU acknowledges the important role of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) in the context of global standardisation and believes that the EU and its Member States must promote a more strategic approach to international standardisation activities, namely in the ITU. The purpose of this tender is to contract the services of standardisation experts to follow closely the ITU-T standardisation work in key sensitive topics defined by CNECT.DDG2.1 Unit, and report regularly to CNECT.DDG2.1 on relevant findings and trends with respect to EU digital policies, and proactively suggest potential strategic actions for DG CNECT to consider, in particular the need of more involvement of EU experts in technical bodies, study groups and working groups of ITU-T. The consultants will act as observers on behalf of DG CNECT in targeted standardisation groups across ITU-T. They will follow closely ITU-T standardisation work in key sensitive topics defined by DG CNECT.DDG2.1. Maximum total value of the contract:135.000 EUR.

description: I servizi di un pediatra sono necessari nell'asilo nido con orari definiti. Il ruolo del pediatra è esclusivamente di medicina preventiva: assicurarsi che ogni bambino sia idoneo a frequentare la comunità e monitorare il suo sviluppo staturale e psicomotorio. In termini di rischio per la comunità, il pediatra è responsabile della gestione delle malattie contagiose e delle epidemie. In collaborazione con gli altri servizi competenti, stabilisce e controlla le varie norme di sicurezza e di igiene.

I servizi di un pediatra sono necessari nell'asilo nido con orari definiti. Il ruolo del pediatra è esclusivamente di medicina preventiva: assicurarsi che ogni bambino sia idoneo a frequentare la comunità e monitorare il suo sviluppo staturale e psicomotorio.
In termini di rischio per la comunità, il pediatra è responsabile della gestione delle malattie contagiose e delle epidemie. In collaborazione con gli altri servizi competenti, stabilisce e controlla le varie norme di sicurezza e di igiene.

description: Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2282 (the ‘HTAR’) provides for the preparation of reports on emerging health technologies that are expected to have a major impact on patients, public health or healthcare systems. The preparation of those reports shall be based on existing scientific reports or initiatives on emerging health technologies, as well as on information from relevant sources, including those listed in Article 22, paragraph 2. Those reports shall, in particular, address the estimated clinical impact and the potential organisational and financial consequences of Emerging Health Technologies (EHT) for national healthcare systems. A public version of the reports in accordance with Article 30(3)(m) of the HTA Regulation including anonymised, aggregated, non-confidential information should also be produced. The preparation of these reports is entrusted by the Member States Coordination Group on HTA (HTACG) to its EHT Subgroup (EHT SG). Only appointed representatives of the EHT SG may access and process relevant confidential data in accordance with the applicable legal framework (HTAR and Implementing Regulations). As a result, only appointed representatives of the EHT SG may participate and express interest in this negotiated procedure. This call for tender seeks to procure services under which the successful tenderer, as contractor, will be primarily responsible for the preparation and finalisation of the EHT reports for the coming three-year period, in close consultation and coordination with, and on behalf of, the EHT SG.

To increase the accessibility and impact of these services, the JRC will develop Drought Chatbot.

description: The present contract aims to implement two in vitro ADME methods for the determination of intrinsic hepatic clearance and plasma protein binding (PPB), and to generate high-quality experimental data for a defined set of selected chemicals in accordance with the JRC-provided Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). The primary objective is to produce robust and reliable in vitro ADME data implementing these assays under controlled and harmonised laboratory conditions. The JRC-provided SOPs serve as the methodological foundation for the technical implementation of the assays and contain all critical procedural elements required to ensure assay integrity and data quality during data generation. A secondary objective is to evaluate the implementation of the SOPs in the tenderer's laboratory in order to identify laboratory-specific critical steps and opportunities for protocol refinement, thereby supporting the development of more robust and transferable protocols.

description: The purpose of the Invitation to Tender is to select one (1) economic operator (hereafter “Contractor”) for the component acquisition, delivery, assembly, hardware and software installation and maintenance of an AI-ready EuroHPC machine (“Supercomputer”) to establish an associated “AI Factory” and that will be owned by the EuroHPC JU. The EuroHPC JU will conclude one contract with the successful tenderer in order to acquire, deliver, install and maintain the High-End Supercomputer hosted by the respective Hosting Entity. Therefore, the prospective Contractors should have proven experience of acquiring, delivering, installing and maintaining Supercomputers in similar environments as the ones required in this procurement procedure. The solutions to be procured are expected to outperform existing solutions regarding several of the following aspects: • Performance/TCO; • Programmability and usability; • Versatility; • System stability; • Power and energy efficiency; • Computing density.

description: The purpose of the Invitation to Tender is to select one (1) economic operator (hereafter “Contractor”) for the component acquisition, delivery, assembly, hardware and software installation and maintenance of an AI-ready EuroHPC machine (“Supercomputer”) to establish an associated “AI Factory” and that will be owned by the EuroHPC JU. The EuroHPC JU will conclude one contract with the successful tenderer in order to acquire, deliver, install and maintain the High-End Supercomputer hosted by the respective Hosting Entity. Therefore, the prospective Contractors should have proven experience of acquiring, delivering, installing and maintaining Supercomputers in similar environments as the ones required in this procurement procedure. The solutions to be procured are expected to outperform existing solutions regarding several of the following aspects: • Performance/TCO; • Programmability and usability; • Versatility; • System stability; • Power and energy efficiency; • Computing density.

description: The provider will offer specialized investment-oriented support and advisory services and will provide a set of skills for comprehensive international and/or local technical assistance focused on institutional capacity building, policy advice and knowledge-sharing to improve green finance and banking practices and bring access to sustainable and inclusive financial services. This will ensure an integrated technical advice and capacity building for the institutions and beneficiaries, and the coordination between the two components and the national counterparts. This contract aims to contribute to a more robust and inclusive financial ecosystem that drives sustainable economic growth, promotes equitable opportunities, and enhances resilience to environmental (and social) challenges in Honduras. This contract supports three State-Owned Development Banks (SDBs) in Honduras, their networks of Intermediary Financial Institutions, including Microfinance Institutions (MFIs), and final beneficiaries with Technical Assistance focused on the following Strategic Objectives (SO): SO #1: Strengthen State-Owned Development Banks’ strategic role in green finance and green investments targeted for MSMEs and Households. SO #2 Increase the operational efficiency, market access, institutional knowledge and capacities of State-Owned Development Banks, Financial Intermediaries, and MSMEs, integrating sustainable, gender-responsive, and green practices and standards. SO #3: Increase socially and environmentally responsible European private sector investments in Honduras.

This contract aims to contribute to a more robust and inclusive financial ecosystem that drives sustainable economic growth, promotes equitable opportunities, and enhances resilience to environmental (and social) challenges in Honduras.

This contract supports three State-Owned Development Banks (SDBs) in Honduras, their networks of Intermediary Financial Institutions, including Microfinance Institutions (MFIs), and final beneficiaries with Technical Assistance focused on the following Strategic Objectives (SO):

SO #1: Strengthen State-Owned Development Banks’ strategic role in green finance and green investments targeted for MSMEs and Households.

SO #2 Increase the operational efficiency, market access, institutional knowledge and capacities of State-Owned Development Banks, Financial Intermediaries, and MSMEs, integrating sustainable, gender-responsive, and green practices and standards.

SO #3: Increase socially and environmentally responsible European private sector investments in Honduras.

description: The objective of the call for tenders is to set up a framework contract with a provider in order to rent (housing) a secured data center space (Disaster Recovery site) for the needs of the General Secretariat of the Council (GSC). The purpose of the contract is also to provide data center services regarding the Disaster Recovery site (including office space, assembly room and storage room). Today, the GSC runs its infrastructure in 2 data centers, one in the Justus Lipsius building (175 rue de la Loi — 1048 Brussels, Belgium) and the other one in the LEX building (145 rue de la Loi — 1048 Brussels, Belgium). The 2 data centers are too close to each other and therefore the present call for tenders has been launched to move the data center situated in the LEX building to the new Disaster Recovery site. Following the call for tenders, a framework contract will be awarded with an initial duration of 4 years, with the possibility of 4 extensions of 1 year each.

description: The JRC intends to sign 4 insurance contracts covering fire, natural and industrial hazards and material damage to nuclear and non-nuclear installations at 4 JRC research sites (Geel, Ispra, Karlsruhe and Petten). The insurance must cover the buildings (inactive nuclear reactors, nuclear laboratories, offices, welfare services, non-nuclear laboratories) and their content (machinery and equipment, laboratory instruments and consumables, fissionable material, furniture and other goods). There is one lot for each JRC site: the premium is calculated with the "replacement cost value", the current cost to replace an item or structure as new. Each candidate can submit a request to participate for one or more lots.

[{"number":"1","title":"Travel agency services relating to missions and authorised trips","description":"This contract is for the provision of all travel agency services, including the provision of an online booking tool, relating to the business trips of any person travelling on behalf of or at the request of the Institutions, regardless of their geographical location. This in particular relates to the heads of mission (including the president of the European Council, the president and the members of the European Commission, including the Union’s high representative for foreign affairs and security policy, and vice-president of the European Commission), experts, and competitive examination winners or candidates.
                  These services will be performed at the contractor's own premises, provided for this purpose. Since the majority of trips are from Belgium, an operating entity of the contractor will be located in Belgium, in order to take into account the need for close coordination, rapid intervention in emergency or crisis situations, monitoring and control in close cooperation with the Institutions that are mainly located in Belgium. The agency must provide a staff member who will be required to work on the premises of the European Commission to act as liaison officer. He/she will be located on the premises of the Office for the Administration and Payment of Individual Entitlements (PMO), in charge of managing the contract in Brussels (Belgium).
                  The contract, which will be based on payments per transaction, has an estimated annual volume of:
                  — 77 000 airline tickets,
                  — 38 000 train tickets,
                  — 80 000 hotel reservations (of which approximately 93% are made directly by the traveller through accommodation facilities or reservation websites).
                  This corresponds to approximately 134 000 business trips for a population of 24 000 travellers. In 2017, the adoption rate of the on-line booking tool (OBT) at the European Commission was around 7%. The balance corresponds to reservations by phone or email.
                  This invitation to tender is organised on an interinstitutional basis. The contracting authority responsible for the procedure is the European Commission. The European Commission, representing the institutions, will make a single award decision for all of them. Afterwards, a framework interinstitutional service contract will be signed by the European Commission, represented by the Director of the PMO. The European Commission will be the main contractor, responsible for managing the framework contract, and representing in this regard all the participating contracting authorities. The operational aspects of the contract will be the responsibility of each participating contracting authority, acting in complete autonomy.
                  This framework contract will apply to all the institutions designated as contracting authorities below which have given a mandate in this regard. This list will not be altered except in the event of the creation or acquisition of financial autonomy of an institution subsequent to the publication of this contract notice in the Official Journal of the European Union.
                  In such cases, the new institution may also benefit from the services under the framework contract on condition that, on the one hand, it is authorised by the Commission on the basis of information regarding its legal personality and the legal basis of its creation and, on the other hand, that the value of any future contracts would not exceed 10% of the contract volume as indicated in the technical specifications (all institutions, bodies and agencies taken together). The rider enabling the new institution to adhere to the framework contract will be signed and managed by the European Commission.
                  A reserve of 10% for unforeseen needs and additional services will also be taken into account to define the contract volume (full description available via the link mentioned in point I.3).","nuts":[],"additionalCpvs":[],"estimatedValue":null,"awardMethod":"1","lng":null},{"number":"2","title":"Travel agency services relating to the organisation of meetings and events","description":"The subject of the contract includes the coordinated provision of all travel agency services relating to the organisation by the Institution of meetings or events, for the business trips of all persons, including, if the case may be, those external to the organising Institution, travelling on behalf of or at the request of said Institution, regardless of their geographical location.

description: The European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) is issuing a call for expression of interest in order to compile a list of vendors to provide independent and on-hand expertise on specialised services in the field of intellectual property (IP) rights. This list will aim to assist the EUIPO, in particular the European Observatory on Infringements of Intellectual Property Rights (the Observatory), and the International Cooperation Service (IC), which is a service within the Institutional and Cooperation Department (ICD), to foster IP cooperation in both EU and non-EU countries.

description: Deliver a study on 'The cost of decarbonising and renewing the EU fishing fleet – Assessment of investment needs, technical constraints, and policy barriers' (A) General objective: to provide PECH Committee Members with a specialised, up-to-date assessment of the financial and regulatory conditions under which fleet decarbonisation and renewal can be achieved, while maintaining fisheries sustainability (B) Research product: Study of up to 60 pages to be finalised by 8 April 2027 and to be presented to PECH Committee Members. (C) Minimum requirements: (1) minimum four researchers with sound educational/professional qualifications and experience that are clearly relevant to the delivery of the research project. (2) For each of the three main subtopics of the study (EU public funding, fishing vessel technology and CFP policy), at least one team member must have a proven publishing record in the academic journals of reference within the past ten years, or must have undertaken studies and reports for public authorities (such as the European Commission or ministries) on issues relevant to the topic of the research project within the past ten years. (3) At least one team member should have at least seven years of experience in managing projects. (D)Participation to this procedure is open exclusively to natural and legal persons coming within the scope of the EU Treaties, to natural and legal persons established in a third country which has a special agreement with the EU in the field of public procurement, and to international organisations. This means that access to this procedure is granted to entities based in EU Members States; Overseas Countries and Territories; EEA Members: Iceland, Norway and Liechtenstein; Countries under SAA: North Macedonia, Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo; and EU nationals living in a third country. Others can participate only as subcontractors.
