description: The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX­classified area containing the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several external components: ­ An MV/LV transformer ­ A thermal management system (dry cooler) ­ A low­pressure hydrogen storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 ­ A gas blender installed on the outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts, and a 3­year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually 3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant to power the electrolyser for self­consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co­generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co­generators across current and future PV expansion scenarios

description:
The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton
Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system 
is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure 
of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: 
a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX­classified area containing
the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several 
external components: ­ An MV/LV transformer ­ A thermal management system (dry cooler) ­ A low­pressure hydrogen
storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 ­ A gas blender installed on the 
outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the
Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts,
and a 3­year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce 
green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) 
plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually
3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant 
to power the electrolyser for self­consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas 
pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co­generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded 
that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available
PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co­generators across current and future PV
expansion scenarios

title: Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra
Supply, Installation and maintenance of a PEM Electrolyser for Hydrogen Production at JRC Ispra

description: The procurement entails the design, manufacturing, delivery, installation, and commissioning of a Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis system for hydrogen production at the JRC Ispra site. The core of the system is a 50 Nm3/h electrolyser (which must be upgradable to 100 Nm3/h) that delivers hydrogen at an outlet pressure of 30 barg. The main equipment will be delivered in a containerized/skid version divided into three specific areas: a control panel area with the AC/DC converter, a water purification unit, and an ATEX-classified area containing the stacks and gas purification treatment. In addition to the containerized unit, the scope of supply includes several external components: - An MV/LV transformer - A thermal management system (dry cooler) - A low-pressure hydrogen storage system consisting of a cylinder rack at 30 bar with a total volume of 5 m3 - A gas blender installed on the outlet piping after the storage Finally, the procurement includes a comprehensive service package covering the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), Site Acceptance Test (SAT), ATEX verification, staff training, two years of spare parts, and a 3-year maintenance contract. Reason for Purchasing The primary objective of this procurement is to produce green hydrogen by harnessing the renewable energy generated from the JRC Ispra site's internal photovoltaic (PV) plant. Currently, the site has a 1.35 MWp PV installation, which is planned to be expanded to 2 MWp and eventually 3 MWp in the future. Instead of using battery systems, the JRC intends to use the excess energy from this PV plant to power the electrolyser for self-consumption. The hydrogen produced will then be blended into the natural gas pipeline (up to a 10% volume blend) to feed the site's co-generators. A dedicated technical sizing analysis concluded that a modular 2x250 kW electrolyser is the optimal choice, as it offers the best compromise between the available PV power, the number of operating hours, and the demand from the co-generators across current and future PV expansion scenarios.

description: This call for tenders aims at enhancing the accessibility and availability of Medical Counter-Measures (MCMs) in the EU/EEA. The subject of this call for tenders is to conclude contracts for the reservation of manufacturing capacity and of contractor-managed stockpiles of nitrile examination gloves (lot 1) and FFP2 respiratory masks (lot 2) (hereinafter ‘EU FAB+ PPE Pilot’). The contractor with manufacturing capacity in the EU/EEA will be requested to set up contractor-managed stockpiles with an associated priority right to purchase. Purchased stocks will have to be either replenished in the stockpile or will give rise to an equivalent reservation of manufacturing capacity for the remainder of the contract. The contracting authority and/or the European Commission must have the right to activate the right to purchase the stockpiled or manufactured MCMs, when deemed necessary for preparedness or crisis purposes. Each lot will be awarded to a maximum of three tenderers with each contract awarded lasting for 3 years (36 months). Purchase of the products in scope of this call for tenders shall be done by the contracting authority and/or the European Commission, if needed on behalf of any EU/EEA countries or any EU4Health associated countries, via a separate procedure.

description: This call for tenders aims at enhancing the accessibility and availability of Medical Counter-Measures (MCMs) in the EU/EEA. The subject of this call for tenders is to conclude contracts for the reservation of manufacturing capacity and of contractor-managed stockpiles of nitrile examination gloves (lot 1) and FFP2 respiratory masks (lot 2) (hereinafter ‘EU FAB+ PPE Pilot’). The contractor with manufacturing capacity in the EU/EEA will be requested to set up contractor-managed stockpiles with an associated priority right to purchase. Purchased stocks will have to be either replenished in the stockpile or will give rise to an equivalent reservation of manufacturing capacity for the remainder of the contract. The contracting authority and/or the European Commission must have the right to activate the right to purchase the stockpiled or manufactured MCMs, when deemed necessary for preparedness or crisis purposes. Each lot will be awarded to a maximum of three tenderers with each contract awarded lasting for 3 years (36 months). Purchase of the products in scope of this call for tenders shall be done by the contracting authority and/or the European Commission, if needed on behalf of any EU/EEA countries or any EU4Health associated countries, via a separate procedure.

These procedures are governed by the provisions of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union (hereinafter: the ‘FR’). In order to identify law firms on the market that may be interested in representing the European Parliament before Danish courts and providing legal assistance in non-contentious cases under Danish law, the Legal Service of the European Parliament is launching a call for expressions of interest in accordance with point 13.1(b) of Annex I to the FR.

description: Le présent marché vise à servir la direction D «Lieu de travail intermédiaire» de prestataires de services individuels, de groupements de prestataires de services individuels, cliniques, cabinets médicaux ou associations momentanées de médecins habités dans les domaines du contrôle médical des absences pour accident et maladie. La médecine de contrôle préalable est définie par l’activité médicale exercée par un médecin autorisé et pour le compte d’un employeur en vue de contrôler l’impossibilité pour un travailleur de fournir son travail par suite de maladie ou d’accident. CET appel d’offres concertées des prestations liées aux contrôles médicaux des absences pour accident et maladie du personnel de la Commission européenne affectée en Belgique, Luxembourg et Italie depuis, ement, les sites de Bruxelles, Luxembourg ville et Ispra (Varese, Italie).

description: Le présent marché vise à servir la direction D «Lieu de travail intermédiaire» de prestataires de services individuels, de groupements de prestataires de services individuels, cliniques, cabinets médicaux ou associations momentanées de médecins habités dans les domaines du contrôle médical des absences pour accident et maladie. La médecine de contrôle préalable est définie par l’activité médicale exercée par un médecin autorisé et pour le compte d’un employeur en vue de contrôler l’impossibilité pour un travailleur de fournir son travail par suite de maladie ou d’accident. CET appel d’offres concertées des prestations liées aux contrôles médicaux des absences pour accident et maladie du personnel de la Commission européenne affectée en Belgique, Luxembourg et Italie depuis, ement, les sites de Bruxelles, Luxembourg ville et Ispra (Varese, Italie).

description: Regulation (EU) 2023/1322, which establishes the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA), strengthens the Union’s preparedness for, and response to, drug-related health and security challenges. Article 15 in particular provides for a dedicated network of forensic and toxicology laboratories to enhance analytical capacity, harmonise methods, support quality assurance and facilitate the exchange of data and expertise across Member States. This strengthens and supports the timely detection, assessment and response to drug-related risks. Within this policy context, systematic investigation of drug metabolism is a cornerstone of clinical and forensic toxicology. Overall, the objective of this contract is to reinforce collective capacity across the EU to interpret toxicological findings and, critically, to improve the detection, identification, and timely reporting of exposure to NPS and other illicit drugs. description:
Regulation (EU) 2023/1322, which establishes the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA), strengthens the Union’s preparedness for, and response to, drug-related health and security challenges. Article 15 in particular provides for a dedicated network of forensic and toxicology laboratories to enhance analytical capacity, harmonise methods, support quality assurance and facilitate the exchange of data and expertise across Member States. This strengthens and supports the timely detection, assessment and response to drug-related risks.
Within this policy context, systematic investigation of drug metabolism is a cornerstone of clinical and forensic toxicology. 
Overall, the objective of this contract is to reinforce collective capacity across the EU to interpret toxicological findings and, critically, to improve the detection, identification, and timely reporting of exposure to NPS and other illicit drugs. By generating robust metabolic, pharmacological, and analytical data, and by consolidating these outputs into a centralised, accessible EU database, the project aims to strengthen timely reporting, harmonise practices, and ensure that toxicological evidence can be translated more effectively into monitoring, early warning, and public health responses to emerging NPS threats.

description: The requested services cover analytical, capacity building and strategic advisory activities, structured around the following elements: • Regional mapping and analysis of the current state of play of women’s initiatives within Western Balkan border police authorities, including desk research and targeted stakeholder consultations, with the identification of best practices and institutional gaps. • Design and delivery of a tailored 5 day training course for members of the Network of Women from Western Balkan border police agencies, focusing on personal development, leadership related soft skills, and technical skills related to policy drafting, gender mainstreaming and gender equality mechanisms in law enforcement contexts. • Evaluation and reporting activities, including an ex post course report assessing knowledge transfer, participant feedback and lessons learned. • Strategic forward looking recommendations, including a roadmap outlining suggestions and future activities to support the sustainability and further development of women’s initiatives and the Network at both national and regional level.

caName: Consultancy services supporting women’s initiatives and gender equality in Western Balkan border police
description:
The requested services cover analytical, capacity building and strategic advisory activities, structured around the following elements:
•	Regional mapping and analysis of the current state of play of women’s initiatives within Western Balkan border police authorities, including desk research and targeted stakeholder consultations, with the identification of best practices and institutional gaps.
•	Design and delivery of a tailored 5 day training course for members of the Network of Women from Western Balkan border police agencies, focusing on personal development, leadership related soft skills, and technical skills related to policy drafting, gender mainstreaming and gender equality mechanisms in law enforcement contexts.
•	Evaluation and reporting activities, including an ex post course report assessing knowledge transfer, participant feedback and lessons learned.
•	Strategic forward looking recommendations, including a roadmap outlining suggestions and future activities to support the sustainability and further development of women’s initiatives and the Network at both national and regional level.

description: The contractor shall provide, upon request, technical assistance services in support of the following activities: • Checks of the test vehicles (light-duty and/or heavy-duty) to verify their suitability for testing (integrity of the exhaust system, absence of error messages in the electronic control unit, good mechanical condition, etc.). • Preparation of the vehicles for testing (adaptation of the exhaust gas system and other components, preparation for the installation of sensors and measuring equipment, vehicle conditioning and driving, etc.), as well as assistance during the execution of the tests. • Restoration of the vehicles to their original condition after the tests and repair of any damage or failures, including dedicated interventions at the contractor's premises. • Specific experimental set-up for vehicle testing requiring advanced expertise in on-board diagnostics (OBD) and high-voltage systems.

caName: Technical assistance for vehicle testing at VELA (Vehicle Laboratories)
description:
The contractor shall provide, upon request, technical assistance services in support of the following activities:
•	Checks of the test vehicles (light-duty and/or heavy-duty) to verify their suitability for testing (integrity of the exhaust system, absence of error messages in the electronic control unit, good mechanical condition, etc.).
•	Preparation of the vehicles for testing (adaptation of the exhaust gas system and other components, preparation for the installation of sensors and measuring equipment, vehicle conditioning and driving, etc.), as well as assistance during the execution of the tests.
•	Restoration of the vehicles to their original condition after the tests and repair of any damage or failures, including dedicated interventions at the contractor's premises.
•	Specific experimental set-up for vehicle testing requiring advanced expertise in on-board diagnostics (OBD) and high-voltage systems.

description: Disclaimer: the description of the nature and scope of the services and supplies of the Multi-Component Security Monitoring System for the EU Space SOC procurement is only indicative, aimed at outlining the concept in broad terms and it may need substantial adjustments. Therefore, it shall not be considered final nor binding. The objective of this procurement procedure is to conclude a Contract for the development, deployment, qualification and support to accreditation of the Multi-Component Security Monitoring System (“MC SECMON”), based on a pre-existing SECMON development baseline, as relevant. The MC SECMON will contribute to the establishment of the EU Space Security Operations Centre (SOC) enabling the provision of harmonised and state-of-the-art security monitoring capabilities across all components of the Union Space Programme. The Contract may also include optional activities, in particular the maintenance and support to operations of the MC SECMON. The activities to be performed under the Contract include, at high level, the following: - Development and integration of the MC SECMON; - Deployment and qualification of the MC SECMON; - Support to accreditation activities; - Where the relevant options are exercised, maintenance and support to operations of the MC SECMON; - Where the relevant options are exercised, development and deployment of additional MC SECMON enclaves and other system evolutions.

description: This project foresees implementation of activities focused on climate adaptation measures addressing both, river and torrential floods separately, taking into account their distinct characteristics and specificities, as outlined below: River Floods 1. Renewal of the Hydrological Information System (HIS) for the main sub-basins in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including flood events from 2010 to the present. 2. Analysis of the impact of existing reservoirs on the water regime, with proposals for improving the management of high-water waves and enhancing water retention during dry periods. 3. Development of guidelines for flood protection of agricultural land. 4. Preparation of the manual “Living with Floods”, providing an overview of necessary measures and best practices for flood risk management. Torrential Floods 1. Development of a cadastre of torrential basins, including a sensitivity model based on existing erosion maps. 2. Preparation of a study on increasing basin water retention capacity through measures aimed at reducing runoff and sediment transport, accompanied by a catalogue of applicable interventions.

description:
This project foresees implementation of activities focused on climate adaptation measures addressing both, river and torrential floods separately, taking into account their distinct characteristics and specificities, as outlined below:
River Floods
1.	Renewal of the Hydrological Information System (HIS) for the main sub-basins in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including flood events from 2010 to the present.
2.	Analysis of the impact of existing reservoirs on the water regime, with proposals for improving the management of high-water waves and enhancing water retention during dry periods.
3.	Development of guidelines for flood protection of agricultural land.
4.	Preparation of the manual “Living with Floods”, providing an overview of necessary measures and best practices for flood risk management.
Torrential Floods
1.	Development of a cadastre of torrential basins, including a sensitivity model based on existing erosion maps.
2.	Preparation of a study on increasing basin water retention capacity through measures aimed at reducing runoff and sediment transport, accompanied by a catalogue of applicable interventions.

description: Kazakhstan is the largest economy in Central Asia and an important trade partner for the EU. In the context of growing prominence and international attention placed on Central Asia, Kazakhstan has the potential to become the key hub for investment and regional trade thus securing its sustainable economic growth and resilience. Achieving this target requires removal of trade barriers as well as sustained efforts to diversify the export basket to non-resource tradable products and services and to improve technical competences and quality-assuring services. The EPCA which guides the relations between EU and Kazakhstan has also a role to play in this endeavour. Once fully implemented, the EPCA with its ambitious Trade and Sustainable Development Chapter, will facilitate foreign investment and diversification while ensuring sustainable economic growth benefiting the Kazakh society as a whole. Against this backdrop, this service contract will aim to support the EU-Kazakhstan trade and economic cooperation by supporting the implementation of the EPCA, enhancing the business and investment climate, improving access to quality infrastructure and promoting SME-oriented and non-resource oriented export strategy.

Kazakhstan is the largest economy in Central Asia and an important trade partner for the EU. In the context of growing prominence and international attention placed on Central Asia, Kazakhstan has the potential to become the key hub for investment and regional trade thus securing its sustainable economic growth and resilience. Achieving this target requires removal of trade barriers as well as sustained efforts to diversify the export basket to non-resource tradable products and services and to improve technical competences and quality-assuring services. 
The EPCA which guides the relations between EU and Kazakhstan has also a role to play in this endeavour. Once fully implemented, the EPCA with its ambitious Trade and Sustainable Development Chapter, will facilitate foreign investment and diversification while ensuring sustainable economic growth benefiting the Kazakh society as a whole.
Against this backdrop, this service contract will aim to support the EU-Kazakhstan trade and economic cooperation by supporting the implementation of the EPCA, enhancing the business and investment climate, improving access to quality infrastructure and promoting SME-oriented and non-resource oriented export strategy.

description: The purpose of this study is to assess the availability of technologies, services and business models which could potentially act as alternatives to regulated retail voice, SMS and data roaming services. It will examine the competitive pressure that existing and emerging alternatives, technological developments and traffic flows may exert on roaming services. The study will support the EC’s analysis of the functioning of the roaming market, including the provision of roaming services at retail and wholesale level. The assessments and conclusions will feed into the EC’s 2027 review of the roaming market and inform the report to be submitted to the European Parliament and Council in accordance with the Roaming Regulation. The technologies and services covered by the study shall include mobile networks and other electronic communication network, such as fixed and satellite networks. The study shall analyse the impact of these services (referred to as “Alternative Services”) on roaming in the EU/EEA and the way it is regulated. The study should consider, inter alia, the following developments: • eSIM and iSIM technologies; • 5G Stand Alone, 5G Advanced and Early 6G Developments; • Satellite communication services; • Mobile virtual network operators; • Network evolution; • Wi-Fi offloading/ Wi-Fi aggregation; and • OTTs and messaging evolution. Maximum value of the procurement: 139.999 EUR - Contract duration 5 months.

description: Současné služební vozidlo Zastoupení dosáhlo v květnu letošního roku stáří deseti let a najelo více než 70 000 km. Z tohoto důvodu splňuje podmínky pro jeho obměnu. V souladu s požadavky na ekologizaci vozového parku Komise bude nové vozidlo zvoleno tak, aby mělo nízké emise – tedy buď s hybridním pohonem, nebo plně elektrické. Vzhledem k tomu, že v České republice nelze vydávat diplomatické poznávací značky pro vozidla v operativním leasingu, rozhodlo se Zastoupení pro přímý nákup nového automobilu.

description: The European Commission (Directorate-General for Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion) intends to procure for a study to analyse national sick leave policies and assess their impacts on workers’ health and productivity to identify good practices, in line with the Action Plan on labour and skills shortages (COM(2024) 131 final). Sick leave policies are defined as organisational rules, procedures, and entitlements, in place at national level, that govern how employees take time off and return to work following illness or injury. This procurement request aims to provide an up-to-date analysis of national sick leave policies, including their main features and effectiveness. In 2016, the Commission procured for a study to analyse Member States’ sick leave policies and sickness benefits, which showed significant differences across Member States in eligibility conditions, duration of leave and payment rates (doi: 10.2767/531076). The European Agency EU-OSHA has also carried out research on sick leave policies, focusing on rehabilitation and return to work policies across all the EU Member States and the four EFTA countries (doi: 10.2802/48176), as well as on measures that support return to work following severe illness. These studies highlighted the need for holistic approaches and better coordination among stakeholders, including medical professionals, employers, and vocational services. This procurement has three main objectives. First, it shall provide an up-to-date mapping of sick leave policies (including rehabilitation and return to work policies) across EU Member States, analysing their main features and policy changes since 2020 or over past 10 years as relevant, and identifying upcoming reforms. Second, the study shall examine the effects of sick leave policies on workers’ health and well-being, as well as on productivity. The task should also consider complementary measures that enhance the effectiveness of sick leave polices, such as those focused on health risk prevention, mitigation of sickness-related risks, and the promotion of workers’ health and productivity. Third, the study shall also assess the implementation and outcomes of sick leave policies to identify good practices that benefit workers and businesses, notably those that support workers’ gradual return to work following extended sick leave. These practices can facilitate an effective recovery of workers while maintaining their labour market attachment, and help companies retain human capital and reduce staff turnover costs. The role of relevant stakeholders in the implementation of sick leave policies shall also be considered. To achieve the purposes of this study, the tenderer shall deliver a report that synthesises findings from the literature review, economic analyses and comparative policy research at both EU and Member State levels. The report will include comparative in-depth analysis, evidence-based conclusions and policy recommendations. An executive summary suitable for dissemination to a non-specialist audience will also be prepared. The results of this study will inform the design of sick leave policies that safeguard workers’ health, support a gradual reintegration into the labour market, promote longer and sustainable working lives, and contribute to a healthier and more resilient workforce, in line with the European Pillar of Social Rights.

description: In verband met de leeftijd van de brandmeldinstallaties die in gebouwen 308/309 en 312/313 zijn geinstalleerd, dienen deze vervangen te worden. Met name het verkrijgen van vervangende hardware is problematisch / onmogelijk geworden. Het bestaande system in 312/13 zal worden vervangen door twee nieuwe systemen en één systeem voor de blusgas in 313. Het bestaande systeem in 308/309 zal worden vervangen door 1 nieuw systeem. De gebouwen 308 en 309 bestaan ieder uit 3 bouwlagen en bestaan hoofdzakelijk uit kantoren, met enkele technische ruimten. Gebouw 312 heeft 5 bouwlagen en bestaat uit kantoren, laboratorium ruimtes en technische ruimtes. Gebouw 313 heeft één bouwlaag en bestaat uit kantoren, een werkplaats, een fitnessruimte en technische ruimtes. Tevens zijn hier serverruimtes aanwezig waar een blusgasinstallatie is aangebracht. Bij gebouw 313 staat gebouw 324 dat gebruikt wordt voor opslag van chemisch afval. De gebouwen 308, 309, 312, 313 en 324 vallen allen onder deze aanbesteding.

description: In verband met de leeftijd van de brandmeldinstallaties die in gebouwen 308/309 en 312/313 zijn geinstalleerd, dienen deze vervangen te worden. Met name het verkrijgen van vervangende hardware is problematisch / onmogelijk geworden. Het bestaande system in 312/13 zal worden vervangen door twee nieuwe systemen en één systeem voor de blusgas in 313. Het bestaande systeem in 308/309 zal worden vervangen door 1 nieuw systeem. De gebouwen 308 en 309 bestaan ieder uit 3 bouwlagen en bestaan hoofdzakelijk uit kantoren, met enkele technische ruimten. Gebouw 312 heeft 5 bouwlagen en bestaat uit kantoren, laboratorium ruimtes en technische ruimtes. Gebouw 313 heeft één bouwlaag en bestaat uit kantoren, een werkplaats, een fitnessruimte en technische ruimtes. Tevens zijn hier serverruimtes aanwezig waar een blusgasinstallatie is aangebracht. Bij gebouw 313 staat gebouw 324 dat gebruikt wordt voor opslag van chemisch afval. De gebouwen 308, 309, 312, 313 en 324 vallen allen onder deze aanbesteding.

description: Frontex produces a wide range of communication products to successfully address its large number of stakeholders. The Agency strives to meet the needs and expectations that each specific target audience has, by tailoring content, form and means of distribution accordingly. To achieve success, it is key that the information is shared in a clear, timely and relevant way, meeting the highest professional quality standards. All communication products, regardless of their kind and medium, must be of excellent language quality to strengthen the Agency’s image. Many of the Frontex communication products are drafted and copy-edited in MS Word while the required templates and layouts are usually done or adapted in dedicated layout software such as Adobe InDesign or MS Publisher. Once the layout process is concluded, a significant number of the communication products are checked again towards language correctness and style. The proofreading, editing and writing services are therefore needed on virtually everyday basis – hence the need for the new contract for such services. In addition, the proofreading and editing services are essential for the production of large training and other manuals with long shelf life, and which are shared with EU member states and other key partners, forging the image of Frontex as the agency setting the highest professional standards in border management.

Many of the Frontex communication products are drafted and copy-edited in MS Word while the required templates and layouts are usually done or adapted in dedicated layout software such as Adobe InDesign or MS Publisher. Once the layout process is concluded, a significant number of the communication products are checked again towards language correctness and style. The proofreading, editing and writing services are therefore needed on virtually everyday basis – hence the need for the new contract for such services. In addition, the proofreading and editing services are essential for the production of large training and other manuals with long shelf life, and which are shared with EU member states and other key partners, forging the image of Frontex as the agency setting the highest professional standards in border management.

description: Description: The scope of this procurement is to provide specialized organizational, server-based documentary, and logistic support services in the context of very strategic testing-campaigns that will be carried out by the JRC. Specifically, these campaigns concern pre-normative testing of bidirectional charging technology, involving bidirectional charging column prototypes, electro-technical and ICT-analysis devices, and bidirectionally charging EV-prototypes, and thus require a high degree of specialists’, technological competence of the service provider in this field. The JRC intends to undertake these pioneering experimental campaigns from 2026 until 2028, in order to do successful pre-normative research on new, bidirectional charging technology dedicated to the EU market, and thus directly serving future standardization input, as well as EU-legislative and regulatory policy support in this field.

description: An automated DNA/RNA extraction system, based on the use of the magnetic bead technology, would allow to increase the speed and throughput capacity of the lab, but also, and more importantly, to improve the consistency of the extraction of the nucleic acids, increasing precision and reducing variability and pipetting errors. Another important aspect is the minimal risk of cross-contamination. The laboratory will also have the magnetic bead technology as an additional procedure to be able to compare with the currently implemented manual and kit-based DNA extraction methods based on DNA purification using columns. Performing DNA extraction of all the samples to be analysed during homogeneity studies of proficiency test materials will also be advantageous for ensuring the repeatability conditions of such experiments.

description: The Security Directorate (DS) is in charge of ensuring the security of European Commission staff, premises and information. It carries out a variety of protective tasks, which include safeguarding the institution's staff, premises and information against hostile intelligence services. Unit DS.1 is responsible for operational security services, which include close protection of the European Commissioners while in the premises of the Commission but also during their missions in and outside the Commission. Staff members of the Close Protection team should therefore be well equipped with weapons and be able to practise shooting. The aim of the contract resulting from this call for tenders is to provide sufficient supply of hand guns for DS.1's operations and CPO trainings in Belgium. Tenderers must be authorised to transport and deliver weapons to Belgium.

Chopperen en verwijderen monotone zones met Kraaiheide om heide te revitaliseren en begroeiing met Struikheide te bevorderen;

More in detail, the specific objectives of this Call are as follows: - Selection of AIGF Consortia: Following a rigorous evaluation of the tenders by the EuroHPC JU with the support of independent experts, the Governing Board will make an award decision, establishing a ranked list of successful AIGF Consortia. - Procurement of Compute Access Time: To establish a framework for the joint acquisition of a guaranteed share of AI compute access time from the selected AIGF Consortia, formalised through the signature of a Framework Contract and a number of subsequent Specific Contracts with the successful AIGF Consortia. description: I servizi di un pediatra sono necessari nell'asilo nido con orari definiti. Il ruolo del pediatra è esclusivamente di medicina preventiva: assicurarsi che ogni bambino sia idoneo a frequentare la comunità e monitorare il suo sviluppo staturale e psicomotorio. In termini di rischio per la comunità, il pediatra è responsabile della gestione delle malattie contagiose e delle epidemie. In collaborazione con gli altri servizi competenti, stabilisce e controlla le varie norme di sicurezza e di igiene.

description: The Caribbean Electricity Integrator Facility (CEIF) will provide integrated technical, engineering and transaction-advisory support to advance priority electricity-integration investments in the Caribbean from analysis and project identification towards investment and tender readiness. The specific objective of the contract is to validate regional Caribbean electricity-interconnection options and prepare, through an integrator approach, a St Kitts and Nevis-anchored Northern Corridor package that can reach at least tender or contracting readiness where feasible, while developing a replicable mechanism for future Caribbean electricity-integration corridors. The initial focus will be on St Kitts and Nevis, including the interconnection between St Kitts and Nevis and the associated generation, grid and enabling infrastructure required to support a viable integrated electricity system. The assignment will also assess the potential extension of the Northern Corridor towards Antigua and Barbuda and other Northern Leeward receiving/readiness nodes, subject to technical, economic and commercial validation. The contractor will assess the relevant technical, economic, financial, legal, commercial, environmental, social, institutional and procurement dimensions and develop viable business, financing, risk-allocation and procurement structures for priority investments. The work will also support the development of a scale-up and replication mechanism for a wider pipeline of Caribbean electricity-integration investments. The direct beneficiaries and geographical focus will include Caribbean partner countries covered by the EU-Caribbean Cooperation Facility+ and, where relevant to the electricity-interconnection agenda, Caribbean Overseas Countries and Territories and French Outermost Regions, with the precise geographical scope of subsequent corridors to be determined through the analysis. The contractor will provide an engineering-anchored transaction advisory team, combining strong power-system, grid and submarine-interconnection capability with expertise in market and demand analysis, economics, financial structuring, legal and commercial design, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and stakeholder engagement.

description: Le présent marché vise d’une part l’exécution de prestations forfaitaires de services en brigade (poste 1) dans le domaine de la restauration qui consistent en l’exécution de tâches opérationnelles comprenant la mise en place, la préparation et la réalisation de plats et menus en support aux équipes existantes dans la gestion des exploitations self-services et cafétérias, et d’autre part l’exécution de prestations de services de type gestion complète (poste 2) ayant pour objet la gestion (supervision du personnel, gestion des stocks et des coûts, planification des menus, etc.) et l’exploitation (la mise en place, la préparation des repas, la réalisation de plats et menus, l’accueil des usagers ainsi que la résolution de problèmes divers de terrain) des infrastructures de restauration et des services associés dans les bâtiments de la CE. Ces prestations incluent également le service de « boissons & réunions » et le service de « banqueting ».

description: The EUAA is planning to purchase modification, transportation and installation services to deploy 16 container units to Cyprus and Greece. The containers are currently located in Greece. Out of the 16 units, 8 of those are 100% completed and 8 are 60% completed. The modification services shall be distributed as follows: • From the container units that are approximately 60% completed: 4 units to be completed as accommodation units, 4 units to be completed as office units • From the container units that are 100% completed: 4 accommodation units to be converted into office space, 2 corridor units to be converted into office space, 2 sanitary units to be deployed either in Greece or Cyprus. The EUAA envisages awarding a single Framework Contact. The maximum estimated duration of the contract will be 12 months. This ex-ante publicity is the first stage of the negotiated procurement procedure with at least 5 economic operators through which the EUAA may award the above-mentioned contract. This ex-ante publicity has an indicative value and is in no way binding on the EUAA. The EUAA may decide not to launch the procurement procedure without candidates being entitled to claim any compensation. Only candidates invited by the contracting authority to take part in the procedure concerned can submit a tender. Economic operators interested in being invited to participate in this procedure may express their interest via F&T portal.

description: The aim of this procurement is to establish two direct service contracts for the provision of design, development and testing of a prototype of a next-generation DFMC SBAS and H-ARAIM receiver, implementing navigation message authentication (NMA) functionalities, including OSNMA, to increase user segment resilience to radio frequency interference (RFI). The receiver prototypes will aim at the supporting the validation of the EUROCAE ED-259 Rev. B standard and determine the feasibility of its implementation on a representative civil aviation hardware platform. ED-259B is envisaged to be first DFMC receiver standard that will be referenced in an EASA ETSO and FAA TSO standards for user terminal equipment certification, with particular importance for both Galileo and EGNOS. ED-259B will be the first standard to enable the operational use by civil aviation users of Galileo OS, and EGNOS V3.2 (DFMC). The Receiver shall have a sufficient level of maturity to (as a minimum) carry out flight tests in a representative environment (i.e. Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7). The Receiver will integrate Navigation Message Authentication (NMA) functionalities (for SBAS and Galileo Open Service (OS)).

description:
The aim of this procurement is to establish two direct service contracts for the provision of design, development and testing of a prototype of a next-generation DFMC SBAS and H-ARAIM receiver, implementing navigation message authentication (NMA) functionalities, including OSNMA, to increase user segment resilience to radio frequency interference (RFI). 

The receiver prototypes will aim at the supporting the validation of the EUROCAE ED-259 Rev. B standard and determine the feasibility of its implementation on a representative civil aviation hardware platform. ED-259B is envisaged to be first DFMC receiver standard that will be referenced in an EASA ETSO and FAA TSO standards for user terminal equipment certification, with particular importance for both Galileo and EGNOS. ED-259B will be the first standard to enable the operational use by civil aviation users of Galileo OS, and EGNOS V3.2 (DFMC). 

The Receiver shall have a sufficient level of maturity to (as a minimum) carry out flight tests in a representative environment (i.e. Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 7). The Receiver will integrate Navigation Message Authentication (NMA) functionalities (for SBAS and Galileo Open Service (OS)).

description: The current procurement process aims to develop a high maturity prototype receiver for GPS/GAL DFMC SBAS + H-ARAIM. This prototype will help validate the Minimum Operational Performance Standards (MOPS). This validation will be useful to promote the MOPS as an acceptable means of compliance with regulatory documents for operational use, such as the European Technical Standard Order (eTSO). Additionally, the contract aims to incorporate Navigation Message Authentication capabilities into the receiver for both Galileo OS and SBAS. The goal is to define the necessary resources and develop minimum requirements for airborne equipment using these authentication features. These minimum requirements will be proposed for inclusion in the EUROCAE/RTCA MOPS.

description: REASON FOR PURCHASING The Commission has to maintain a stock of at least 250.000 doses of live attenuated Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) vaccine in storage in order to make it rapidly available in case it is needed. In addition, this stock of 250.000 doses of live attenuated vaccine should be replaced quickly, within 4 weeks, when depleted, in order to maintain the Union’s capability to respond to an emergency. PROCUREMENT DESCRIPTION The purpose of the contract is: • The purchase of maximum 1.000.000 doses of live attenuated homologous vaccine against LSD. This will be executed with one initial purchase of 250.000 and up to three (3) replenishments, of maximum 250.000 doses each, upon request from the Commission. • The storage of a stock of 250.000 doses, readily available for delivery to any of the destinations listed in the technical specifications, that can be replaced, if depleted, partially or totally, up to 5 times until the end of the contract, upon request from the Commission. • The timely delivery of maximum 2.000.000 doses divided in as many consignments as needed to any of the destinations listed in the technical specifications • The storage of any vaccines in stock at the end of the contract for the remainder of their shelf life • The proper destruction and disposal of any unused vaccine at the end of its self life.

The Commission has to maintain a stock of at least 250.000 doses of live attenuated Lumpy Skin Disease  (LSD) vaccine in storage in order to make it rapidly available in case it is needed.

•	The timely delivery of maximum 2.000.000 doses divided in as many consignments as needed to any of the destinations listed in the technical specifications
•	The storage of any vaccines in stock at the end of the contract for the remainder of their shelf life

description: These PCs are essential to replace our current GIS workstations, which are no longer performing adequately on the VDI platform. Critically, the existing PCs are running on Windows 10, which reaches End-of-Life (EOL) in October, posing a significant security and compatibility risk. Furthermore, they can't integrate with the new JRC DELTA domain. The specifications for these new PCs have been thoroughly reviewed and agreed upon with the T6 unit, as they will be placed in the DELTA domain.

description: The EEA management has decided to implement quality management in the EEA based on the ISO9001 standard and methodology. Implementation started January 2025. The overall process framework and methodology have been established, and the project is now in the phase of establishing all the main EEA processes within the quality management framework. Coaching and training are needed to build the internal competencies to implement and run quality management. The training and coaching should be designed to meet the needs for different roles and targets groups in relation to the implementation and running of the quality management. The EEA envisages awarding a direct service contract to a service provider for the provision of bespoke training and coaching on quality management. This support must be based on the ISO9001 standard and methodology. The key components are: 1. Transitioning to a quality management approach to the EEA main processes clarifying the management role including the change management aspect and leading the cultural change towards continuous improvements. This training and coaching components focus on management role of QMS at the strategic level. 2. Building internal capabilities for quality management at the management level, for key staff and for the end user. More specifically, this includes dedicated training programs for internal EEA teams in: a. Business process management and business process modelling for the BPM team b. Process management for process owners and process teams c. Change management for personal managers d. Overall QMS training for key staff members engaged in implementing the QMS e. QMS training for end users understanding the basic principles of QMS and the hands of using the and maintaining the QMS

description: The objective is the signature of multiple framework contracts with experienced service providers capable of delivering specialised operational support services to the functions performed by the corporate support teams of the contracting authorities. The services will be provided to the following EU agencies based in Paris: European Banking Authority (EBA) as lead contracting authority, European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), and European Union Institute for Security Studies (EUISS). The below list is indicative and non-exhaustive and is intended solely to illustrate the scope of services that may be requested under the future framework contracts: • reception and front desk services; • management of internal and external mail; • facility management support and coordination; • light technical interventions related to furniture and equipment installation, maintenance or repair; • inventory and physical asset management; • helpdesk and administrative support services; • occupational health and safety, and security-related support; • travel and mission arrangements for staff; • meeting and event planning and organisation; • data processing, reporting and administrative coordination tasks; • environmental management and EMAS-related support activities. These services are expected to be grouped into four general categories: 1) Reception services 2) Integrated reception and security services 3) Corporate support administrative services 4) Corporate support technical services

description: EFSA has received two mandates from the European Commission for the revision of the terrestrial ecotoxicology guidance document and development of an approach for the assessment of indirect effects. In this context, EFSA should support risk managers in setting Specific Protection Goals (SPGs). EFSA has identified four different lines of evidence (LoE) which should serve this purpose[1]. One of those lines of evidence concerns the building of ecological networks based on trophic interactions (i.e. food webs) to holistically explore propagation of direct effects into indirect ones. This call is intended to seek support for this specific topic. The activity will draw from previous data collections related to control plots in field studies with non-target arthropods, earthworms, and soil mesofauna as well as from vegetation surveys in arable lands. Such data include information in terms of species presence, abundance, and biomass. Furthermore, specific trait information (body size, feeding preference, habitat/stratum use, level of specialisation and dispersibility) from existing databases or public literature will be considered. Objectives: Objective 1: implementing the construction of ecologically meaningful networks, or food webs representing different EU agroecosystems (regulatory zones, crop type). Objective 2: selecting and applying appropriate metrics, to assess the background variability range of the constructed networks. Objective 3: investigating– by means of simulations - the effect of different perturbations to food networks by incrementally manipulating energy flows. This should allow evaluating holistically the indirect effect caused by certain magnitude of direct effects, thereby potentially identifying thresholds at which networks deviate from their background state due to external pressures. Selection criteria: The tenderer overall must have the ability to provide an individual or a team with extensive and demonstrable experience in the area of community ecology and/or ecotoxicology, traits-based approaches, and network analysis. Evidence requested: A list of three (3) major projects or publications related to the above-mentioned area of research carried out over the course of the past 10 years. All team members must have an excellent level of spoken and written English. For non-native speakers, this should be demonstrated by an official certificate of English proving a B2 level or at least 3 years of work or study in an English-speaking environment or by proof of (co)authorship of 7 scientific publications and/or reports in English language.

description: The proposed procurement concerns the design, production, and delivery of a custom beta/gamma shielding window for the JRC Karlsruhe. This component is required to enable safe visual monitoring of operations in a high-radiation environment while preserving the shielding integrity of the hot cell. As this is a specialised component designed for nuclear applications, it is not an off-the-shelf item and must be specifically engineered for the installation.

description: Based on the organisation of already five successful workshops (THEORY-1 to THEORY-5) in different countries (Romania, France, Croatia, Bulgaria and Italy), a 6th workshop is anticipated to be organised in October 2025. Theory-6, will be held in Catania (Italy). The selected contractor will provide conference facilities for the up to 40 participants to the workshop, hotel rooms and catering for the duration of the event (6 to 10 October 2025). The hotel needs to be 4 stars or equivalent, located in or in the surroundings of Catania. The selected contractor will also organize a social event, consisting of a sightseeing tour of half a day for the participants to the conference.

description: The objective of this framework contract is to continue the operation of the CEMS "Hydrological and Meteorological Data Collection Centers" (METEO and HYDRO) in support to the flood early warning and monitoring component of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS) which continues as full operational service as defined in article 51(1.b)) of the regulation (EU) 2021/696 of the Union Space Program. Meteorological and hydrological observations constitute a key input for the European and Global Flood Awareness Systems (EFAS and GloFAS) of the Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS). The role of METEO and HYDRO is to collect meteorological (Europe only) and hydrological in-situ observations in near real time (METEO only) as well as for historic periods, quality control and post-process the collected observations, manage and expand the data provider networks and further enhance the data collection. CEMS implementation is an interservice arrangement between DG JRC, DG DEFIS and DG ECHO (Ares (2021) 2234141). JRC is in charge of preparing and implements the CEMS work programs, manages dedicated budgets and supervises the implementation of service tasks.

description: The European Agency for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA) plans to launch a negotiated procurement procedure for data review, statistical analysis and data visualisation services supporting its forthcoming report, “OSH in Europe: State and Trends”. The new report will update the evidence presented in the 2023 edition and examine how major transformations in work are reshaping occupational safety and health (OSH) in Europe. The “OSH in Europe: State and Trends 2023” report is available here: https://osha.europa.eu/en/publications/occupational-safety-and-health-europe-state-and-trends-2023 The contract will cover three complementary tasks: 1. updating the quantitative evidence used in the 2023 report; analysing newly available data, comparing them, where appropriate, with previous comparable waves or reference periods; 2. Identify relations between indicators, trends and discuss areas of improvement, concern or stagnation and 3. selectively extend existing analyses at a broader context of megatrends, where further work would provide clear analytical or policy added value. The contractor will not be required to draft the complete report or collect new primary data. Expected deliverables Deliverables will include: an inception package with the inventory of 2023 statistical evidence, evidence map, dataset mappings, analytical questions and proposed methods; a 2023-to-current statistical crosswalk; a comparison matrix for new and previous comparable data; and an evidence-use log showing which findings were adopted, reproduced, updated, extended or excluded. The contractor will provide an interim and a final report, where all the findings will be presented. These will describe the methodology used for the analysis, the main findings and a discussion part which will critically assess and discuss each finding. Further to the OSH discussion, each one of the areas mentioned about should be discussed in dedicated section of the reports. The contractor will also provide in the reports interim and final statistical findings; updated tables and figures; targeted descriptive and inferential analyses; approximately 25–35 additional publication-quality graphs for new or extended analyses; editable graphs and underlying data tables; reproducible scripts and relevant data dictionaries; methodological, source, uncertainty and limitations notes; a concise synthesis; a technical annex. Visualisations must communicate the main findings clearly to non-specialist research and policy audiences. Finally, a PowerPoint presentation should be prepared by the contractor, presenting the main findings. Publication of this ex-ante publicity notice does not constitute a commitment by EU-OSHA to launch the procurement procedure. The planned maximum duration is seven months. The maximum budget is EUR 50,000, excluding VAT. Expression of interest Economic operators may express their interest either individually or as members of a consortium. Please note that invited candidates may submit a joint tender with other economic operators only if they have previously expressed their interest as a consortium. More information about the subject matter and the technical and professional capacity required for this contract can be found here: https://osha.europa.eu/en/about-eu-osha/procurement/call-tender/osha2026lvp0027-exa-data-review-update-and-statistical-analysis-osh-indicators-low-value-procedure

This work will focus on validating the potential of a collaborative European-led entity aiming to bring together diverse technological and data domains under a cohesive development strategy. The initiative will conceptualise the programme management, networking and governance structures needed to ensure coherent and outcome-oriented development of common SDV, AI and hardware initiatives in Europe). Maximum value of the procurement: 135.000 EUR - Contract duration: 6 months.

description: Contrat cadre d’une durée de quatre ans (2 + 1 + 1) pour le nettoyage et des services d'élimination des nuisibles et services divers des principaux bâtiments (JL, LEX, EB et la crèche). Il prévoit l’utilisation et la fourniture des produits qui respectent au mieux l’environnement ainsi que la mise en œuvre d’un équipement et du matériel adaptés aux besoins spécifiques du SGC. L’objectif est d’assurer un service de nettoyage optimal compte tenu de l’occupation des différents bâtiments et de la qualité du service voulu par le SGC.

description: The project aims to achieve circularity of C&DW management in Türkiye, Strategy of C&DW has the main objective to support Türkiye’s efforts towards zero waste management via developing a C&DW management strategy in line with EU circular economy policies. To accomplish this objective technical capacity on management of C&DW will be increased through current situation assessment of C&DW in Türkiye and preparation of Policy Recommendation Paper (PRP) and guidelines that provide a methodology for demolition or renovation of buildings and infrastructures, as well as, training and awareness raising activities in 7 different geographical regions of Türkiye. Last but not least, in 12 different areas, recommendations and methodologies defined in the PRP will be implemented on site.

description: The contract concerns the provision of technical assistance to strengthen the administrative and institutional capacities of the Ministry of Mining and Energy, in particular in the areas of EU integration, energy efficiency policy, and legislative alignment. It includes expert support for gap analysis, drafting or amending energy efficiency legislation, and developing methodologies for monitoring and reporting energy savings in line with EU acquis and Energy Community obligations. The assignment also supports knowledge transfer and capacity building to ensure effective implementation of the revised EU energy efficiency framework in Serbia.

description: The objective of this procurement procedure is to conclude a Framework Contract for the performance of Galileo Service Operations, in order to ensure the provision of the Galileo Services. The Galileo Service Operations activities to be performed within the FWC, include, at high level, the following activities: • operations of the Galileo Core Infrastructure (including the Galileo Space Segment and the Galileo Control and Mission Segments) deployed at the GCCs and at the relevant Remote Sites; • operations of the GNSS Service Centre (GSC) Infrastructure, significantly for what concerns SiS activities; • performance of the Infrastructure Logistic Support (ILS), including all levels of maintenance, of the Galileo Core Infrastructure and of the GSC Infrastructure under its responsibility. • provision of enabling services required for the operations of the above infrastructure: o Hosting Services o Communication Services (i.e. the GDDN – Galileo Data Dissemination Network) o Geodetic Services (i.e. the GRSP – Geodetic Reference Service Provider) o Timing Services (i.e. the TSP – Timing Service Provider) • support to the evolution activities of the Galileo System, including supporting the evolution and deployment of the Galileo Core Infrastructure and of the GSC Infrastructure that will be operated and/or maintained under the contract, and supporting the launch and initial testing of new satellites; • support to security (including cybersecurity) of the Galileo System, including the maintenance of the Infrastructure that will be operated and/or maintained under the contract. The Contractor to whom this tender will be awarded, will be a key partner of EUSPA for the provision of the Galileo Services for all the duration of the FWC, and will receive a significant level of delegation (and associated responsibilities) for the management of the wide scope of activities to be performed.

description:
The objective of this procurement procedure is to conclude a Framework Contract for the performance of Galileo Service Operations, in order to ensure the provision of the Galileo Services. 

The Galileo Service Operations activities to be performed within the FWC, include, at high level, the following activities:
•	operations of the Galileo Core Infrastructure (including the Galileo Space Segment and the Galileo Control and Mission Segments) deployed at the GCCs and at the relevant Remote Sites;
•	operations of the GNSS Service Centre (GSC) Infrastructure, significantly for what concerns SiS activities;
•	performance of the Infrastructure Logistic Support (ILS), including all levels of maintenance, of the Galileo Core Infrastructure and of the GSC Infrastructure under its responsibility.
•	provision of enabling services required for the operations of the above infrastructure:
o	Hosting Services
o	Communication Services (i.e. the GDDN – Galileo Data Dissemination Network)
o	Geodetic Services (i.e. the GRSP – Geodetic Reference Service Provider) 
o	Timing Services (i.e. the TSP – Timing Service Provider)
•	support to the evolution activities of the Galileo System, including supporting the evolution and deployment of the Galileo Core Infrastructure and of the GSC Infrastructure that will be operated and/or maintained under the contract, and supporting the launch and initial testing of new satellites;
•	support to security (including cybersecurity) of the Galileo System, including the maintenance of the Infrastructure that will be operated and/or maintained under the contract.

The Contractor to whom this tender will be awarded, will be a key partner of EUSPA for the provision of the Galileo Services for all the duration of the FWC, and will receive a significant level of delegation (and associated responsibilities) for the management of the wide scope of activities to be performed.

description: Disclaimer: the description of the nature and scope of the services and supplies of the Galileo Service Operator II (GSOp II) procurement is only indicative, aimed at outlining the concept in broad terms and it may need substantial adjustments. Therefore it shall not be considered final nor binding. The procedure is aimed at procuring services/supplies to ensure continuation of (most of the activities) currently being performed by the Galileo Service Operator (GSOp) under EUSPA contract (GSA/CD/14/14). The GSOpII contractor will be responsible for the performance of Galileo Service Operations, during the period January 2027 to December 2036, in order to ensure the provision of the Galileo Services. The Galileo Service Operations activities to be performed within this contract, include, at high level, the following activities: (i) operations of the Galileo Core Infrastructure (including the Galileo Space Segment and the Galileo Control and Mission Segments) deployed at the GCCs and at the relevant Remote Sites; (ii) operations of the GNSS Service Centre (GSC) Infrastructure, significantly for what concerns SiS activities; (iii) performance of the Infrastructure Logistic Support (ILS), including all levels of maintenance, of the Galileo Core Infrastructure and of the GSC Infrastructure; (iv) provision of enabling services required for the operations of the above infrastructure, including Hosting Services, Communication Services (i.e. the GDDN – Galileo Data Dissemination Network), Timing Services ((i.e. the TSP – Timing Service Provider) and Geodetic Services (i.e. the GRSP – Geodetic Reference Service Provider); (v) support to the evolution activities of the Galileo System, especially for what concerns the Infrastructure that will be operated under the contract and the launch and initial testing of new satellites; and (vi) support to security (including cybersecurity) of the Galileo System, especially for what concerns the Infrastructure that will be operated under the contract.

description: In view of the organisation of Trade Policy Day 2025, scheduled to take place on 20 November 2025 on European Commission premises in Brussels, we intend to launch a procurement procedure for catering services. The requested catering services will include welcome coffee for 430 participants; Standing lunch for 400 participants; VIP seated lunch for 30 participants and continuous coffee service throughout the day. The offer should foresee the provision of standing tables, while buffet tables will be made available on the premises.

description: Provision of supervision services for the Works Contracts for Establishment of Integrated and Financially Sustainable Regional Waste Management System in East and North-East Regions, which will be implemented according to the FIDIC conditions of contract. The works will be divided into two (2) lots, which are as follows: Lot 1: Construction of the Central Waste Management Facility for East and Northeast region in the Municipality of Sveti Nikole Lot 2: Construction of 6 Local Waste Management Facilities for East and Northeast region - Municipalities of Bérovo, M.Kamenica, Vinica, Stip, Rankovce and Kumanovo. description: The European Union Agency for Criminal Justice Cooperation intends to initiate a procurement procedure for the provision of copywriting, editorial, editing and proofreading services in English. The services may include the drafting, rewriting, adapting, editing and proofreading of legal, administrative and communication-related content, including articles, interviews, news items, reports, publications, summaries, speeches and video scripts. Tasks may also involve conducting supporting research to enable the performance of the tasks, updating existing content and adapting texts to different target audiences. The contractor will be expected to ensure that content is clear, concise and consistent with Eurojust’s editorial requirements and applicable style guides, while preserving the intended substantive and legal meaning of the original texts. The resulting Framework contract with one contractor is expected to have an initial duration of 24 months, renewable twice for periods of 12 months each (24+12+12), for a maximum duration of 48 months. Exclusion criteria: Tenderers must not be in any of the exclusion situations referred to in Article 138 or subject to any of the grounds for rejection referred to in Article 143 of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 (Financial Regulation). Access to procurement: Participation is open to natural and legal persons having access to EU procurement in accordance with Articles 179 and 180 of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509. This includes economic operators established in an EU Member State and economic operators established in third countries having a special agreement with the European Union in the field of public procurement, under the conditions laid down in the applicable agreement. Please note that Eurojust cannot benefit from the Agreement on Government Procurement concluded within the World Trade Organisation (GPA). Tenderers must comply with the applicable rules on access to procurement at the time of submission of their tender and throughout the performance of the Framework Contract. The rules on access to procurement apply to all members of a group of economic operators. They do not apply to subcontractors unless otherwise specified in the procurement documents. Subcontracting may not be used to circumvent the applicable rules on access to procurement. Interested economic operators should be able to comply, at least, with the following selection criteria: • Legal and regulatory capacity: authorisation to perform the contract under applicable national law, including enrolment in a relevant trade or professional register, where applicable. • Economic and financial capacity: average annual turnover of at least EUR 25,000 over the last two financial years. • Project management experience: availability of a Project Manager with at least 5 years of relevant professional experience. • Copywriting experience: availability of at least two writers, each with at least 10 years of professional experience, including at least 5 years of relevant experience in the role concerned. • Editing and proofreading experience: availability of at least two editors/proofreaders, each with at least 5 years of relevant professional experience. One team member may fulfil more than one role. • Relevant contract experience: at least 10 contracts of similar scope and complexity completed during the last three years, each with a minimum value of EUR 1,000. No evidence must be provided at this stage. Detailed requirements, award criteria, contractual conditions and the evidence to be provided will be specified in the procurement documents.

I. International Protection
II. Country of Origin Information (COI)
III. Program administration and project management

V. Knowledge management

description: The subject of this contract is the provision of access to a true color, cloud free satellite/aerial-based, hybrid, topographic and 3D terrain elevation basemap service to be integrated into web-based or native geographic information system (GIS) applications operated by the Contracting Authority. The basemap shall consist of optical high-resolution satellite/aerial-based, hybrid, topographic and 3D terrain elevation basemap provided as a tile-based online map service, suitable for interactive web/native app use. The objective of this contract is to ensure the availability of a high-quality, reliable, and scalable satellite/aerial-based, hybrid, topographic and 3D terrain elevation basemap that provides visual background context for geographic data displayed in a web application. The basemap shall support zoom levels corresponding to a ground resolution of approximately one (1) meter or better, particularly in urban and built-up areas.

description: The JRC and the European Commission's Competence Centre on Participatory and Deliberative Democracy (CC-DEMOS) have built a specific training offer on citizen engagement processes based on co-creation and deliberation for public administrations at local, regional and national level across the EU. The training offer targets three levels of competence (basic, advanced and train-of-trainers) and is available in EN, DA, PL. It includes a full package of resources: for each competence level, it provides a course-book, annotated PowerPoint presentations, roll-out of the course, agenda of the course, self-assessment questionnaire, in-class exercises, and case collection. In the perspective of upscaling the use of this training package and reaching out to a large number of administrations, JRC is collaborating with the EU Academy to make the offer available on-line and in the three languages. The development of the training offer through pilots in Denmark and Poland has revealed that it is paramount to have moderators with a high level of experience with and expertise on citizen engagement in order to deliver successful training and accommodate specific participants' requests for knowledge and competence. Moreover, experienced practitioners and moderators would ensure that more case studies and examples are brought in that meet the interest of participants and improve the overall quality of the training. Thus, JRC and CC-DEMOS are seeking to procure online moderation of the training on citizen engagement which will consist in combining asynchronous and synchronous sessions and ensure the creation of a community of learners from public administrations and future trainers.

description: This procurement aims to establish multiple framework contracts for catering services, supplies, and venue arrangements required for meetings and other events organised by the Contracting Authority, including the provision of food and drinks prepared off-site. To ensure specialised service delivery and increased competition, the procurement is divided into two lots: Lot 1 – Catering Services and Supplies, and Lot 2 – Arrangement of Venues. At this stage, economic operators are invited to express their interest by sending an email to tenders@eba.europa.eu quoting reference EBA/2026/OP/0007 by Wednesday 30 September 2026 at the latest. The EBA will invite interested economic operators to respond to a questionnaire. This will help the EBA identify the active companies in the field, analyse the market and develop the tender specifications. This prior information notice announces the contracting authority's intention to publish a future call for tenders. No other information or documents are available at this stage.
